body: Use an append-only JSONL event stream and reviewed Markdown in Git. Build SQLite FTS5 only as a disposable index. This preserves diffs, provenance, portability, and recovery.
summary: Canonical project memory is Git-tracked text; databases are derived caches.
title: Use files and Git as the canonical memory

body: Expose the same local store through MCP stdio and a shell CLI. Model subscriptions can invoke the local tool without the memory layer calling OpenAI, Anthropic, or another model API.
summary: Use MCP plus CLI as provider-neutral access paths with no model API dependency.
title: Keep the project memory provider-neutral

body: AgentMemory exposes recall, timeline, provenance verification, explicit save, diagnostics, and retrieval evaluation. Reuse its interface and benchmark ideas first; do not adopt its full 54-tool surface or runtime until independently evaluated.
summary: AgentMemory is a high-value source for MCP ergonomics, timelines, provenance tools, and retrieval benchmarks.
title: Audit AgentMemory as an interface and evaluation reference

body: Graphiti retains raw episodes, traces derived facts to their sources, and represents changing facts with temporal validity. Its graph backend and LLM extraction pipeline are too heavy for the project-memory bootstrap, but its data semantics are directly relevant.
summary: Graphiti is a strong reference for provenance, temporal validity, episodes, and non-destructive supersession.
title: Audit Graphiti's temporal provenance model

body: Arousal, valence, novelty, threat, reward, surprise, and goal relevance may influence encoding, consolidation, retrieval, or forgetting in different ways. The system should test these as separable signals and must not infer that a scoring mechanism gives an LLM subjective feelings.
summary: Emotion-related appraisal signals may improve memory prioritization if evaluated separately and protected against manipulation.
title: Test emotional salience as multiple memory-control signals

body: Compare plain file search, SQLite FTS5, hybrid lexical-vector retrieval, temporal retrieval, and graph-assisted retrieval on a fixed corpus. Include Recall@k, MRR/nDCG, answer support, contradiction handling, provenance accuracy, harmful intrusion, p50/p95 latency, token overhead, disk growth, and recovery after corruption.
summary: Do not add semantic or graph complexity until it beats lexical baselines on a reproducible gold set.
title: Gate memory complexity with controlled retrieval evaluation

body: Unit tests cover add/search, document indexing, provenance, supersession, malformed events, concurrent writers, and MCP tool calls.
summary: Implemented and smoke-tested append-only project memory with SQLite FTS5, CLI, MCP stdio, Codex configuration, and Claude Code configuration; no model API is required.
title: Provider-neutral project memory bootstrap implemented

body: Adding 12 query families produced 1066 unique OpenAlex leads across 32 families, but spot checks exposed substantial query drift. The new records are discovered-unscreened and cannot support a completeness or review claim.
summary: The initial 684-work catalog used 20 human/agent query families and did not systematically cover animal, motor, skeletal-muscle, immune, transcriptional, non-neural, prokaryotic, or collective memory.
title: Comparative biological memory was absent from the initial discovery coverage

body: Shared use of the word memory does not establish shared substrate, computation, cognition, or subjective experience. Each mapping needs an empirical assay, substrate, timescale, simpler baseline, predicted benefit, failure mode, and rejection criterion.
summary: Animal episodic-like memory, motor learning, skeletal-muscle history, immune memory, transcriptional priming, CRISPR, non-neural habituation, and collective memory must remain separate research tracks.
title: Study biological memory as distinct mechanism families

body: Retrieval and reader evaluation remain separate. High-impact conclusions require independent challenge, blinded backend labels where feasible, retained negative runs, and clean-environment reproduction.
summary: Freeze evidence, corpus, metrics, budgets, and rejection rules; compare no-memory, rg, FTS5, dense, hybrid, temporal, graph, and salience one level at a time.
title: Use stage-gated research laboratory before product architecture

body: API workers may propose relevance labels, source cards, or candidate claims through structured outputs, but cannot directly promote accepted evidence. Admission requires a frozen pilot measuring locator accuracy, unsupported claims, abstention, reviewer time, cost, privacy, and provider failures. Local embeddings do not require a chat-model API.
summary: The project does not need a separate API agent for canonical memory or initial benchmarks; any future cloud model is a replaceable batch worker.
title: Keep model APIs optional and review-gated

body: The new tracks cover associative memory, continual learning, semantic compression, engram allocation, replay, neuromodulated memory, prospective offloading, metamemory, durable storage, temporal provenance, distributed memory, and information thermodynamics. Eleven broad queries returned 40 top records; the metamemory query returned only two and is recorded as query-failed rather than saturated. Query drift and zero independent review prevent evidence claims.
summary: The OpenAlex discovery catalog now contains 1464 unique records and 12 newly tracked interdisciplinary topics, but all new topic results remain unscreened.
title: Interdisciplinary discovery broadens the candidate mechanism space

body: Priority-A topics advance through cycles of screening, exact-locator primary reading, adversarial challenge, synthesis, and registered experiment. A checkpoint occurs after 25 screened records or three newly primary-read decisive sources in one topic. Final architecture selection remains blocked until baseline reproduction and independent review.
summary: Broad discovery and structured evidence processing will run in parallel; raw paper counts will not gate the first lexical benchmarks.
title: Begin reversible mechanism synthesis before global completeness

body: Test each signal through separate write, replay, retention, and retrieval ablations. Reject or restrict the approach if it creates chronic threat bias, emotional-language poisoning, quiet-critical-memory loss, false persistence after correction, or no held-out consequence-weighted gain. These signals are not evidence of subjective emotion.
summary: Separate consequence valence, magnitude, urgency, surprise, controllability, uncertainty, explicit user weight, and recurrence may improve memory control beyond relevance and recency.
title: Operational emotion should be decomposed before salience testing

summary: In a frozen 125-record DeepSeek V4 Flash candidate-screening run, all outputs passed schema validation but two records without abstracts violated the prompt rule and were marked include. A deterministic policy layer downgraded them. The worker is admitted only for candidate generation, never evidence promotion. Conservative cumulative API cost including pilots was USD 0.0613668 under the USD 10 cap.
title: DeepSeek screening requires deterministic guards

summary: On the 24-query PMLAB development slice, ripgrep and SQLite FTS5 both reached Recall@5 0.841 but had forbidden-record intrusion 0.292, zero abstention on unanswerable queries, and zero cross-language recall. This exploratory authored slice diagnoses the instrument and cannot select an architecture.
title: Raw lexical retrieval has safety and semantic gaps

summary: Keep the 24-query corpus as an instrument-development slice. Before calling PMLAB v0 ready or testing embeddings as an architecture candidate, create 120 split-by-history examples, obtain independent A/B labels and adjudication, audit leakage, freeze hashes, and rerun unchanged B0/B1/B2 rules.
title: Expand PMLAB only after independent annotation

summary: Deterministic DOI/OpenAlex identity checks resolved all 37 DeepSeek include candidates. Abstract-level screening found 35 distinct intellectual works: 19 priority full reads, 9 background sources, 6 deferred sources, 1 challenge-only preprint, plus 2 merged records (a version duplicate and an eLife decision-letter artifact). No additional model spending is justified until full-text extraction.
title: DeepSeek include queue reduces to nineteen priority reads

body: DeMem constrains runtime decision states rather than disk storage; the compaction survey reports illustrative repeated-summary loss; human/computational RDT models motivate task-weighted distortion; semantic completion demonstrates plausible unsupported reconstruction risk.
summary: Five full-text reads converge on distinguishing a reversible high-fidelity archive from lossy semantic representations and a query-conditioned bounded working set; this convergence does not independently validate one final architecture.
title: Compression evidence supports separating archive from active budget

body: The raw archive remains canonical. Semantic summaries cannot overwrite evidence. Emotion is initially factor-separated metadata rather than a scalar truth or anthropomorphic internal state.
summary: A lossless versioned episodic archive plus rebuildable provenance-bearing semantic hypotheses plus query-conditioned context may outperform either raw retrieval or rolling summaries, but must be rejected if benchmark gains do not survive cost and safety controls.
title: Three-tier archive semantic hypothesis and working-set design

summary: Before promotion, test repeated compaction, delayed model change versus noise, plausible semantic completion, and factor-separated emotional allocation under matched context budgets and explicit safety and cost gates.
title: Compression mechanisms require four preregistered benchmark families

body: This is an artifact availability block not a failed scientific reproduction. Recheck later versions and supplements. Keep all three result families below the independent-reproduction gate.
summary: The rate-distortion working-memory repository was located and pinned but lacks a dependency lockfile bundled referenced data and a detected license; no matching public DeMem repository or compaction-survey experiment repository was found in the 2026-08-22 artifact search.
title: Public code does not yet make compression claims reproducible

body: Stress can favor habit strategies; reward effects depended on task-relevant semantic contingency; novelty rescued weak rat spatial memory only within mechanistic timing conditions; limited context sampling produced overgeneralization in male mice; an LC review proposes an encoding-versus-retrieval shift.
summary: Five full-text sources separate stress/arousal reward contingency novelty prediction-related updating encoding coverage and timing; their effects include subsystem shifts specificity changes and bounded persistence rather than a universal memory-strength increase.
title: Emotion-related memory modulation is multidimensional and phase-specific

summary: Raw episodes should be appended immediately while promotion into derived semantic or procedural memory may use an expiring eligibility tag linked to verified outcomes; this must beat raw retrieval and immediate promotion without promoting unrelated novelty or poison.
title: Safe delayed consolidation uses append-now promote-later eligibility

summary: Evaluate false context generalization and habitual procedure perseveration in addition to weighted recall; factor valence arousal consequence surprise reliability timing contingency scope and required controller separately.
title: Emotion benchmarks must test specificity and subsystem shifts

body: Nadasdy et al. reported recurring CA1 spike sequences above several surrogate families and short ripple-associated sequences, but null-model choice is critical. Olafsdottir et al. reported local/congruent/forward replay near task movement and broader deep-MEC-coherent replay during disengagement; engaged content predicted choices, while key state-by-accuracy interactions were nonsignificant.
summary: Two fully read rat electrophysiology studies support time-compressed recurrence and task-state-dependent awake replay; neither proves that replay causes long-term consolidation, and the strongest pre/post sleep evidence in the 1999 study used two rats.
title: Replay content is state-dependent but causal function remains unresolved

body: This is an engineering translation, not a biological-equivalence claim. Reject it if raw archive retrieval is within two points, if gains vanish after compute matching, or if it worsens rare-event coverage, poison persistence, unsupported consolidation, or post-change procedural perseveration.
summary: Under a fixed maintenance budget, a small task-local contradiction-aware replay phase near decisions plus diverse offline replay may improve both immediate action and delayed transfer more than uniform, recency, relevance-only, diversity-only, or no replay.
title: Phase-conditioned replay should beat one global replay policy

body: Post-training disruption slowed one maze but the effect was moderate and disappeared with extra training. Awake SWR disruption impaired outbound history-dependent alternation while sparing inbound performance, place fields, and later rest reactivation. The evidence upgrades replay-associated processing to a serious candidate while leaving its content-specific mechanism unresolved.
summary: Two small rat perturbation studies causally link ripple-associated hippocampal activity to selected spatial-memory performance, but neither selectively manipulated decoded replay content.
title: Causal ripple disruption supports a processing window not replay content alone

body: This separates benefit from replayed content from benefit due to extra tokens, regularization, or another maintenance window. Cross simple tasks with history-dependent tasks and require a content-by-demand interaction before promotion.
summary: Every replay experiment must compare targeted content with no maintenance, sham calls, random real episodes, corrupted/irrelevant episodes, and direct just-in-time retrieval under equal compute.
title: Replay benchmarks require content-specific causal controls

body: The original behavioral result did not directly identify reconsolidation, had later-disputed exclusion descriptions, and its one-year analysis used 19 participants. Null replications do not refute all molecular or animal reconsolidation, but they reject unconditional retrieval-triggered rewriting as an evidence-backed engineering rule.
summary: A prominent small fear study reported durable cue-specific benefit, but a preregistered 124-person direct replication and seven procedural/declarative sequence replications found no reliable reminder-triggered rewriting advantage.
title: Human behavioral reconsolidation updating is contested and boundary-sensitive

body: This is a safety invariant, not a claim that biological memories never reconsolidate. Corrections append evidence and may supersede scoped derived state while preserving predecessors. Learned triggers remain benchmark candidates and may not authorize truth changes from surprise alone.
summary: Retrieval alone must never rewrite canonical evidence or durable derived beliefs; revision requires an explicit evidence-bearing versioned transaction and return/rollback tests.
title: Project memory reads remain non-mutating

body: Research and testing may run in parallel across different hypotheses. Architecture promotion additionally requires a held-out gain over the simpler equal-budget baseline, adversarial and safety success, two task families, second-corpus and second-reader/provider reproduction where applicable, independent review, and justified cost.
summary: Do not wait for global literature completeness. A hypothesis enters exploratory testing only after its mechanism, challenge search, baseline, failure case, metrics, guardrails, and rejection rule are explicit; a confirmatory test is frozen before held-out results and may not be rewritten afterward.
title: Research-to-experiment transition is hypothesis-specific

summary: A missing or wrong answer must be localized across capture, canonical storage integrity, indexing/access, validity/selection/context assembly, reader use, and final action; checksum-valid direct recovery rules out storage loss.
title: Localize memory failures before declaring data loss

summary: A 2026 Drosophila study reports that behaviorally forgotten information could remain latent and be recovered by reminder plus context, while manipulated reminders could produce false memory; recovery benchmarks must therefore score provenance and distortion, not recall alone.
title: Silent memory recovery can coexist with distortion

summary: The Unable-to-Forget repository at commit 51c131691e75c293694b883d5e310ab8523ed778 is admitted only as a benchmark-generator reference after credential removal, deterministic seed freezing, parser tests, and suspected bug repair; it is not an architecture dependency or reproduced result.
title: Pinned PI-LLM generator for interference benchmark development

summary: In a deterministic non-held-out fixture with 28 F1 traces and 56 F2 queries, the stage localizer matched all authored labels while rg and FTS5 current-value log2 AUC was 0.417 with stale intrusion 0.857; these numbers validate and stress the instrument only, not an architecture.
title: F1/F2 authored development slice exposes temporal retrieval interference

summary: The first B3 development arm consumed gold history_id and as_of_version, making its perfect score incomparable with unscoped lexical baselines. A frozen DeepSeek challenge identified the problem; B3 was replaced by a query-text rule resolver, while the original review state remains preserved.
title: Oracle metadata invalidated the initial entity-time comparison

summary: Exact entity plus temporal validity is the next low-complexity candidate because it solves the authored interference fixture, but it cannot unlock architecture promotion or dense retrieval until unseen entities, paraphrased times, ambiguity, unequal histories, and reader-level value confusion are tested.
title: Advance explicit entity-time scoping only to held-out testing

summary: On 20 answerable and 4 unanswerable authored challenge queries with unseen entities, duplicate surface names, natural and relative time, B3 Recall@5 fell to 0.50, natural-language and relative-time recall was zero, and abstention was 0.25. This rejects B3 as a sufficient access layer but is not independent gold.
title: Unseen entity-time challenge breaks the development resolver

summary: The next F2 comparison must cross raw versus normalized entity-time queries with all-record versus validity-filtered candidate scopes so that query interpretation is not misattributed to the retrieval backend.
title: Factor query understanding from validity filtering

summary: The second DeepSeek methodology run reused an update-curve question for a category-based challenge, producing an inapplicable finding. The frozen output and rejection were preserved and preparation now selects a dataset-aware question.
title: Generic worker prompt asked for a nonexistent challenge curve

summary: On the 24-query FTS5 challenge, gold-normalized entity topic and ISO date increased Recall@5 from 0.40 to 1.00 while gold history scoping added 0.00; forbidden-version intrusion remained 1.00 in every FTS arm, separating target discovery from context validity.
title: Oracle query normalization dominates history scoping in challenge v0

summary: DeepSeek V4 Flash returned exact value evidence ID and abstention in 40/40 frozen synthetic cases across gold-only unrelated distractor stale-first stale-last and stale-only conditions. This is a narrow null result requiring higher stale counts and degraded validity cues.
title: No DeepSeek reader interference under explicit four-stale validity condition

summary: Because explicit validity metadata prevented errors with four stale competitors while retrieval still returned stale versions, the next reader test varies 1-64 stale records, similarity, validity-cue quality, order, language, and instruction explicitness before attributing failures to the reader.
title: Stress reader interference before changing retrieval architecture

summary: The prior claim of no DeepSeek reader interference is withdrawn: expected outputs were serialized into the API payload. The artifacts and USD 0.00796224 cost remain preserved as a benchmark-validity failure.
supersession_reason: The model request contained expected_answer expected_evidence_id and expected_abstain, so the 40/40 null result was label-leaked and scientifically invalid.
title: Reader pilot v0 invalidated by gold-label leakage

summary: V1 leaked explicit expected fields; v2 encoded chronology in evidence IDs and values; v3 reused record identities across cue conditions within batches. V4 salts IDs and values per case and excludes expected fields. Earlier artifacts are invalid or partial and remain preserved.
title: Reader stress required four iterations to remove leakage channels

summary: In leakage-controlled DeepSeek reader stress v4, full and weak cues remained perfect through 64 stale records and absent cues produced abstention. With two contradictory current markers and minimal instructions, accuracy fell to 4/8 at 64 stale; explicit abstention instructions restored 8/8.
title: Reader failures require high competition conflicting validity and weak policy in v4

summary: V0 and v1 leaked gold labels; v2 encoded chronology in IDs and values; v3 reused identities across conditions; v4 exposed condition names in case IDs. V5 excludes expected fields, salts opaque records per case, prevents cross-case identity reuse, and hashes case IDs. All earlier artifacts remain labeled invalid or partial.
supersession_reason: V4 still exposed experimental condition names in model-visible case IDs; v5 was required to remove that final known cue.
title: Reader stress required five iterations to close known leakage channels

summary: In audited v5, full or weak validity cues remained correct in 64/64 cases through 64 stale records and explicit abstention policy scored 64/64. Under minimal instructions, absent cues scored 8/16 and contradictory current markers 4/16. Failures were confident selections; count effects were non-monotonic and unreplicated.
supersession_reason: V4 condition names could cue abstention, so its calibrated results were only partially valid; v5 removes that channel and broadens the supported conclusion.
title: Validity ambiguity and weak abstention policy drive v5 reader errors

summary: The controller should resolve authorization and temporal validity before presenting records to the reader. If no unique current and authorized record exists, it should expose the conflict or abstain; reader prompting is a safeguard, not the primary consistency mechanism.
title: Require a unique valid winner before context assembly

summary: Across 174 authored traces, passive telemetry achieved exact fault-set accuracy 0.075, root accuracy 0.511, masked downstream-fault recall 0.146, and physical-data-loss decision coverage 0.414. Even complete passive telemetry found the root perfectly but exact sets only 0.138 because downstream faults were causally masked.
title: Passive cascade cannot identify complete memory fault sets

summary: The laboratory must support controlled capture receipts, direct-ID/full-scan/raw-byte storage checks, oracle-query retrieval, oracle-record context construction, oracle-context reader checks, and fixed-answer action checks. Before product adoption, inject probe noise and find the smallest adaptive probe budget that preserves safe data-loss classification.
title: Make active stage probes part of the memory diagnostic contract

summary: A runtime-label-free deterministic parser resolved answerable history and target date at 1.0 and raised FTS5 Recall@5 from 0.40 to 1.0 on 24 observed challenge templates, while unanswerable abstention reached 1.0. Forbidden stale-version intrusion remained 1.0, and template inspection makes the parser result developmental rather than held out.
title: Catalog parser matches oracle discovery ceiling only on observed templates

summary: Do not modify parser v0 until it has been tested on a newly authored set spanning paraphrases, aliases, typos, multilingual time expressions, alternate date formats, ambiguous topics, and out-of-range times. Keep query parsing and stale-version validity selection as separate measured stages.
title: Freeze parser v0 before adversarial language challenge

summary: After parser v0 was frozen at commit 1a43b7a, 21 new answerable queries reduced exact parse and Recall@5 from 1.0 on observed templates to 0.238. Relative time scored 0/4, new date formats 1/8, paraphrases 1/4, and multilingual 0/1. Strict abstention was 0.857; raw retrieval traded recall 0.381 for abstention 0.143.
title: Frozen perturbations falsify parser v0 generality

summary: Post hoc, falling back to raw retrieval only for unresolved-time cases reached Recall@5 0.619 while retaining abstention 0.857 on parser challenge v1; unconditional fallback had the same recall but abstention 0.143. This policy was chosen after failure inspection and must be preregistered and tested on new cases before use.
title: Typed parser failures may enable selective safe fallback

summary: Across 1,972 authored fault/noise cases, repeat-all reached exact localization 0.794 at 30 probe units but remained at 0.400 on persistent flips and 0.667 on correlated failures. Adaptive storage-diverse checks reached 0.741 at 24.16 units, made zero false loss/no-loss declarations, and abstained to 0.909 coverage.
title: Same-probe repetition fails under persistent and common-mode faults

summary: Do not count repeated execution of one probe as independent evidence. A physical-data-loss declaration must combine write, direct-ID/full-scan/raw-byte, and schema paths whose shared dependencies are documented; conflicts produce inconclusive. Adaptive diagnostics must also audit some healthy results because failure-only retry misses false-health signals.
title: Treat probe independence as a failure-domain property

summary: Under an exact 580-contribution uniformly placed transient-flip mixture with storage-diverse safeguards, reaching 0.95 expected exact localization requires auditing 72.38 percent of first-pass healthy results and costs 28.31 probe units versus 30 for repeat-all. Failure-only retry has no justified large cost advantage without probe-specific reliability priors.
title: Healthy-result auditing removes most adaptive retry savings at the F1 threshold

summary: A production audit budget must be derived from measured probe-specific false-health, timeout, persistent, and common-mode rates plus consequence limits. Until those priors exist, critical storage evidence remains failure-domain-diverse with conflict-to-inconclusive, and any cheaper success-sampling policy stays experimental.
title: Require empirical false-health priors before adaptive probe savings claims

summary: Direct-ID read full canonical scan raw-byte recovery and schema reparse all share the primary filesystem and storage device in dependency map v0. They can localize parser/index access faults but cannot alone justify PHYSICAL_LOSS_CONFIRMED; incomplete replica inventory or conflicting probes require INCONCLUSIVE.
title: Primary storage probes are logically diverse but media-dependent

summary: The empirical harness must add P10: raw checksum verification on a separately inventoried replica using an alternate runtime filesystem device and checksum implementation. Independence claims require both a no-shared-domain map and fault injection showing one path can fail while the other stays correct.
title: Add alternate-media evidence before physical-loss claims

summary: A disposable harness ran 300 real fsync read checksum unlink truncate schema index and forced-timeout trials with 300/300 authored classifications and zero PHYSICAL_LOSS_CONFIRMED outputs. C and D both map to Disk 0, so the score validates state-machine construction but supplies no alternate-media independence or reliability estimate.
title: Same-device filesystem harness validates loss-state guard only

summary: Windows reports workspace volume D and system volume C as partitions of Disk 0. Logical replicas across those volumes cannot satisfy the separate-storage-device dependency requirement; physical-loss confirmation remains prohibited until an independently inventoried device or remote/offline replica is available.
title: Current host cannot instantiate alternate-media probe P10

summary: Targeted primary-source review separates monitoring from control and shows that feeling-of-knowing can derive from cue familiarity plus accessible correct or incorrect partial information. Search termination is a control outcome. LLM semantic or sample agreement is likewise reader-level evidence and may share a common-mode wrong source.
title: Metamemory signals are heuristic evidence not privileged trace access

summary: The controller will expose capture durability query resolution retrieval stability validity evidence sufficiency reader stability action verification and search progress separately. It may answer change cue direct-probe expand ask abstain or stop; monitor output alone cannot mutate canonical memory.
title: Use typed metamemory state instead of one confidence scalar

summary: On cases crossing stored status cue recoverability ambiguity poison stale versions and reader disagreement a typed evidence monitor plus fixed escalation policy should improve risk-coverage and recover stored targets by at least 15 points over single-shot retrieval without raising each distortion metric more than 1 point. This requires a frozen benchmark and separate monitoring/control ablations.
title: Typed monitoring plus cue escalation can dominate scalar confidence

summary: The 26-case corpus was frozen at commit a4d5d3c before runner implementation. Typed monitoring recovered 0.333 of answerable targets with zero risk; fixed typed control recovered 1.0 with zero risk at 0.692 coverage and mean abstract cost 0.981. Scalar confidence familiarity and semantic-consistency arms each had 0.8 selective risk on deliberately adversarial high-confidence cases. This is a construction test only; live retrieval blinded labels risk-coverage sweeps and independent review remain required.
title: Typed control passes authored construction semantics

summary: On the existing 24-query PMLAB development corpus ripgrep and SQLite FTS5 were jointly unsafe on 13 cases and unsafe on 11 of 19 cases with matching top-1 IDs. Requiring top-1 agreement plus Jaccard at least 0.8 reduced answer coverage to 0.542 but left selective retrieval risk at 0.538. Same-cue agreement is rejected as independent confidence evidence; temporal entity or bilingual cue diversity must be tested next.
title: Lexical backend agreement is common-mode evidence

summary: After protocol freeze at 43cdec0 valid-time trust and tailored bilingual cue interventions raised safe-action accuracy from 0.458 to 0.833 reduced selective retrieval risk from 0.522 to 0.167 eliminated forbidden intrusion and recovered 2/2 cross-language targets. The bundle failed its frozen gate because unanswerable abstention remained 0/2. Residual errors isolate weak paraphrase multi-source completeness and absent-fact evidence sufficiency.
title: Diverse cues improve retrieval but do not supply abstention

summary: Primary answerability and RAG-evaluation sources plus the frozen diverse-cue failure show that topically relevant valid trusted retrieval can still lack an answer one facet a bridge conflict resolution or support for a generated claim. Citation presence and reader confidence are not sufficiency oracles. The monitor must keep answerability obligation coverage claim support conflict and collection closure separate.
title: Evidence relevance validity sufficiency and completeness are distinct

summary: PMLAB-SUFF-001 will map query obligations to supported partial contradicted or missing evidence and allow answer partial_with_gap retrieve ask or abstain. Inventory-incomplete states may say not found in searched scope but cannot say not stored. Query decomposition and the coverage checker must be ablated separately.
title: Represent missing evidence as typed obligations and gaps

summary: On 36 cases frozen at 4ca0309 nonempty retrieval had 0.75 selective risk four scalar arms had 0.80 and claim entailment had 0.20 with two critical false-sufficient cases. Retrieved-obligation monitoring reached 0.778 exact action with zero answer risk but its eight errors were exactly absent-versus-search and unavailable-partial-versus-recoverable distinctions. A gold collection-aware hybrid reproduced all actions but two matched-coverage gates failed.
title: Evidence sufficiency construction isolates collection-scope requirement

summary: A retrieved obligation miss may trigger more retrieval but cannot distinguish recoverable evidence from collection-confirmed absence or permanent partiality. ABSTAIN_NOT_FOUND and stable PARTIAL_WITH_GAP require an authorized collection inventory probe; incomplete inventory permits only ABSTAIN_INCONCLUSIVE or not-found-in-searched-scope language.
title: Require collection-scope probe before absence or permanent-gap decisions

body: Reiter separates OWA from negation by failure. Motro separates validity from completeness. Levy relates answer completeness to insertion independence, while Razniewski and Nutt derive query completeness from completeness statements over critical data fragments. This is the missing input exposed by PMLAB-SUFF-001.
summary: A globally incomplete memory may still be complete for one exact predicate, entity, time interval, namespace, authorization boundary, and replica/media inventory; insertion-sensitive missing records invalidate the closure claim.
title: Collection closure is query-relative

body: PMLAB-CLOSURE-001 must test certificate granularity, mutation invalidation, replica/media availability, authorization, query-to-scope mapping, and counterexample insertions. Global CWA, retrieval saturation, and coarse completeness flags are baselines, not accepted policies.
summary: Never turn a retrieval miss directly into absence or falsity. Distinguish NOT_RETRIEVED, NOT_FOUND_IN_SEARCHED_SCOPE, NO_AUTHORIZED_CURRENT_RECORD_IN_COMPLETE_SCOPE, and PROPOSITION_FALSE; N2 requires an exact current certificate and N3 additionally requires explicit negative evidence or a domain rule.
title: Use open-world default and four negative tiers

body: V0 freeze b99b20a hash 3599635e. V1 changed two bilingual certificate statuses to declared complete and added an evaluation-only adversarial flag before any runner existed; v1 freeze e9649ac hash 3450ebbe.
summary: The frozen v0 insertion-counterexample certificates already declared partial, so a certificate-only policy could reject them without inspecting admissible updates; v0 remains preserved and v1 repairs only this pre-run confound.
title: Closure v0 failed to isolate insertion independence

body: This is a 48-case authored construction result using synthetic inventories, probes, certificates, and insertions. Exact action/tier was 0.958, but critical tier was 0.941 and matched-coverage comparison was unavailable. It validates state transitions only.
summary: On PMLAB-CLOSURE v1, global CWA produced 40 unsupported N3, retrieval saturation 28 unsupported N2, coarse completeness 8, exact query certificates 2, and certificate-plus-insertion 0; the candidate also achieved 1.0 positive safe coverage and expiry/mutation invalidation.
title: Insertion-aware closure removes authored unsupported strong negatives

body: The insertion-aware candidate's only tier/action errors were the two bilingual multi-facet cases. This keeps critical tier accuracy at 0.941 below the preregistered 0.95 gate and identifies decomposition rather than closure evaluation as the next isolated subsystem.
summary: Do not patch PMLAB-CLOSURE v1 multi-facet cases. The next experiment must separately freeze query obligation decomposition and map each obligation to its own predicate/entity/time/namespace certificate before an unseen challenge.
title: Freeze decomposer and per-obligation scope mapper next

body: QDMR/BREAK supplies a candidate ordered decomposition representation. Text-to-SQL schema-linking analyses, Spider-Syn, COGS/CFQ, SCATE, and entity-linking work supply adversarial split and metric mechanisms. Full-text and multilingual audits remain incomplete.
summary: Question decomposition, dependency parsing, entity linking, predicate/schema linking, temporal normalization, and certificate routing are distinct failure stages; a correct closure evaluator can still be unsafe when any earlier mapping stage omits or mislinks an obligation.
title: Scope safety requires staged obligation mapping

body: PMLAB-MAP-001 will score critical obligation omissions separately from over-decomposition and will reuse the frozen closure evaluator for downstream unsafe N2/N3 outcomes. A model worker may be a replaceable arm but never gold.
summary: Do not randomly split bilingual or paraphrased mapper cases. Keep each semantic group in one split and hold out new operator compounds and schemas so lexical overlap cannot masquerade as compositional or schema generalization.
title: Group mapper splits by semantic template and schema

summary: Full-text audit and pmlab-obligation-ir-v0 now separate computation graphs from entity predicate namespace valid-time authorization and certificate scopes. Commit 4b6c47e froze 28 semantic groups expanded to 56 paired PL/EN construction cases, all 13 operators, and four structure-versus-denotation fixtures before parser implementation. This is non-independent development data, not a held-out result.
title: PMLAB-MAP construction corpus frozen

summary: On 56 inspectable PL/EN construction cases, repaired QDMR-inspired rules reached obligation F1 0.922, critical full recall 1.0, zero false closure, and 0.679 end-to-end exact. Entity accuracy 0.940 and predicate accuracy 0.916 miss the preregistered 0.95 gates; gold obligations with predicted links reached only 0.750 E2E. The arm is rejected for promotion. A first run with span-matcher and linker-isolation defects is preserved separately.

summary: Independence is redefined as measurable decorrelation of errors between the process producing a claim and the process checking it, rather than as an attribute of a person. Six tiers I0 to I5 each state what they rule out, what they cannot rule out, and how independence is measured rather than asserted. Binding rule: every label mechanically checkable must be checked mechanically before any human or model is asked.
title: Adopt the independence ladder in place of the binary reviewer gate

body: Falsifiable form for the current scale: partition the 170 canonical events by the deterministic shares_source graph, route with combined lexical and graph activation, and compare against flat retrieval on the frozen development corpora. Predicted failure modes to measure, not assume: routing error is silent and presents as absence, so a missed region is indistinguishable from a missing fact without a closure certificate per PMLAB-CLOSURE-001; a synthesizer composing several same-family workers launders correlated errors into apparent consensus, which same-cue agreement analysis already rejected once; and the composition gate must be measured for decorrelation per independence tier I3. At 170 events this architecture addresses a scale the project does not yet have, so the small routed version must be shown to beat flat search before any large version is justified. Related to PMLAB-ROUTER-001, which already preregisters deterministic, all-cheap, all-strong, two-tier and three-tier arms.
summary: Proposal: partition durable memory into regions, wake only the regions a cue activates, have each digest its own partition, and compose the results through a stronger synthesizer. This is the mixture-of-experts pattern applied to stored memory rather than to model parameters, and it composes with the association graph, where edges supply the routing structure.
title: Sparse region activation over a partitioned memory may beat flat retrieval

body: The mechanism creates memory without new evidence, which is the one thing this project's provenance discipline exists to prevent. A weak finding restated as a clean reflection launders uncertainty into confidence with no new observation. Stage 1 is therefore deterministic and model-free: same-source opposite-polarity claims, findings whose source_refs no longer resolve, decisions never later referenced, stale hypotheses with no linked outcome, and superseded memories still cited by active ones. Stage 2 may use a budgeted worker but must emit only kind question or hypothesis at low confidence, must cite the memory IDs it derived from, may not chain reflections beyond depth one, and must be excludable from any evaluation corpus. Measured memory composition motivating this: 172 events with 73 findings and 48 decisions but exactly 1 question, so the project asserts in about 70 percent of records and almost never records what it does not know. Usefulness is untested; the honest metric is whether a generated question later becomes an evidence-backed finding or failure. Tracked as issue 27.
summary: Proposal: when no task runs, agents read project memory and exchange information about what is unclear, writing the result back as new memory. The concept exists as Generative Agents reflection and as offline replay, and this project already preregisters it four times in PMLAB-REPLAY-R1 to R4, none executed. The constrained form is to emit questions and detected contradictions rather than syntheses.
title: Idle reflection should generate questions, not new facts

body: Surfaced by a plain example: memory holds that Ala has brown hair, then Ala dyes it green. Brown was never wrong; it is true of a closed past interval, and it also predicts a future state once the dye fades. The schema conflates two distinct operations under supersede: correction, where the prior claim was invalid and should leave ordinary search, and succession, where the prior claim was right and should stay searchable with its interval closed. The project already measured the consequence without attributing it to the schema: stale intrusion 0.857 in the F2 fixture and forbidden-version intrusion 1.00 even after oracle query normalization lifted recall from 0.40 to 1.00. Recall was fixable by retrieval; staleness was not, because the store cannot express what stale means. A further open problem is a state claim with an expected expiry and no observation behind it, whose confidence should decay without new evidence. Proposed direction is additive and append-only: optional valid_from and valid_to, a dispositional versus state claim class, correct versus succeed operations, and time-aware retrieval defaulting to as-of-now. Tracked as issue 29.
summary: The event schema has no valid-time field. created_at records when a claim was written, never when it held in the world. Because a superseded record is removed from ordinary search, the only way to record that a fact changed also hides the fact that was true before it, so the store cannot answer questions about a past state.
title: Project memory cannot represent when a fact was true

body: Gold was derived mechanically from co-citation, never authored. The held-out edge is absent from the fold graph, so any gain required transitivity. The 2-hop reachability ceiling was 0.2206, bounding the possible gain, and roughly one in five reachable targets became a recall gain, so the mechanism is not inert but the sample of 102 edges is too small to resolve it. B2 surrendered 1.76 lexical positions per query on average. Two fresh processes reproduced digest a5ea57f382aa6d53. An earlier revision produced a different digest; the hypothesis that FTS5 BM25 global corpus statistics let unrelated documents perturb memory ranking was tested by adding a large unrelated document and refuted, and no cause is asserted. This is the first experiment run under the Tier E rule, which permits cheap model-free exploratory runs with no independence gate provided they are labelled non-confirmatory.
summary: PMLAB-ASSOC-E1 materialized 102 shares_source edges from 57 shared source references, lifting connected nodes from about 11 percent to 58.6 percent. On 204 paired queries from 5-fold held-out edges, lexical-plus-graph RRF beat lexical alone by +0.0245 Recall@5 with 95 percent CI [-0.0343, 0.0833] and +0.0392 Recall@10 with CI [-0.0098, 0.0882]. Both intervals include zero, so the retrieval benefit is unproven.
title: First Tier E experiment: association graph helps structure, not yet retrieval

body: Proposed as a literature audit, not an experiment. Pharmacological dissociations are useful because they isolate one function while sparing neighbours: benzodiazepines produce anterograde amnesia while leaving retrieval of stored memories intact, alcohol blackout gives goal-directed behaviour with no encoding, and scopolamine impairs encoding specifically. Two cautions are registered up front. The reconsolidation-blockade literature has real replication problems and must enter as contested hypothesis, never as established. MDMA-assisted therapy for PTSD had functionally broken blinding because participants could tell whether they received the drug, and the FDA declined approval in 2024 pending further study. The project has already been burned by a vivid biological analogy once, when the emotion and salience audit rejected monotonic emotion-to-stronger-memory and found a 2009 stress-to-habit result now sits beside a 2025 null across 129 participants. First question to answer is whether clinical dissociations produce failure strata not already covered by the 174 authored fault traces; a negative answer is also informative. Subjective experience stays out of scope. Tracked as issue 31.
summary: Intrusive traumatic memory is characterized by involuntary retrieval on weak cues plus impaired temporal contextualization, which is the same defect as the missing valid-time field: a retrieved memory arrives with no closed past interval attached. Confabulation is characterized as a source-monitoring and reality-filtering failure rather than a generation failure, which is convergent evidence for the closure vocabulary separating NOT_RETRIEVED from NOT_FOUND_IN_SEARCHED_SCOPE from PROPOSITION_FALSE.
title: Clinical memory pathology names failure modes this project already measures

body: Addresses the recorded PMLAB-MAP failure where a post-freeze challenge was same-process and not independently held out, and was spent for tuning. The guarantee is bounded and stated: ordering rests on publication rather than a trusted clock, so an author holding the key could seal, peek and then register. What makes ordering real is pushing the sealed manifest and registration publicly before releasing the key. Building it surfaced three defects found by running it rather than by reasoning: Path.write_text translates LF to CRLF on Windows so in-memory digests disagreed with disk bytes, which is the same cross-platform freeze failure already recorded against this repository; an experiment sharing an identifier with one of its cases makes leak checking undecidable and is now refused at seal time; and substring leak scanning produced a false positive where an experiment identifier shared a prefix with case identifiers, so the check now compares exact JSON leaf values.
summary: scripts/sealed_split.py implements commit-and-reveal: seal splits a pool by HMAC(key, case_id) and publishes only the development half plus a manifest committing to sha256(key); register binds candidate artifact digests before the challenge exists; reveal refuses unless commitment, registration, candidate digests and pool bytes all check out; verify lets any third party recompute the split. 16 tests cover the honest path and twelve tampering cases.
title: Sealed held-out splits give tier I1 independence without a second person

body: The two problems needed opposite answers and separating them was the substance of the decision. For the 16, content never changed; only the declaration named the wrong byte form, so correcting it restores a true statement rather than rewriting evidence. '-text' was chosen over 'text=auto eol=lf' because normalizing would rewrite stored bytes and break declarations that are currently correct. The six genuine post-freeze modifications fail the CRLF test, meaning their content actually differs from what was frozen, and they were deliberately left untouched: re-declaring them would make the audit pass while destroying the evidence that a freeze broke. Every old and new digest is recorded in data/lab/provenance-repair-20260823/crlf-declaration-repair.json. The audit now reports 0 Windows-only declarations and 6 criticals, all of which are the genuine breaks tracked in issue 30.
summary: Issue 26 resolved by two changes. .gitattributes with '-text' stops all end-of-line conversion, taking files whose working copy differed from the stored blob from 843 of 1348 to 0, without rewriting a single blob. Then 16 declarations computed from Windows working copies were re-declared to the bytes actually stored, verified by the rule that sha256 of the same content with LF converted to CRLF equals the declared value.
title: Repair CRLF-derived hash declarations, never the six real freeze breaks

body: The five stale ones were repaired by marking the packet superseded rather than by touching its bytes: a superseded packet keeps what it actually declared, and rewriting it would destroy the record of what was frozen and when. The audit now skips declarations inside a directory carrying a SUPERSEDED.json marker. No reviewer had been exposed to v0, so no review work was invalidated. The sixth was an ordering defect at freeze time, not a later modification: the digest was computed and the file edited before it was committed, so manifest and repository were never in agreement. Since the declared byte sequence has never existed in this repository there was nothing to restore, and the committed 965-byte report is the version that was recorded, cited and reviewed, so the declaration was corrected with both values preserved in a repair record. Critical audit findings are now zero and the repository claim audit is a blocking CI job.
summary: Five belonged to independent-contract-review-v0, whose declarations were correct at freeze commit 44b2b9b and became stale when the contracts were revised and packet v0.1 was prepared; v0.1 verifies 13 of 13 while v0 verifies 2 of 7. The sixth, pmlab-obligation-mapping-deepseek-v1/report.md, declared a digest that matches no file at HEAD and no historical version of that file, so it was never true of anything committed.
title: The six broken freezes were two different defects, not one

body: The stratification was the point. Tag edges were authored by the same agent running the experiment, so tag-derived gold is weaker evidence and was reported separately. It did not inflate the estimate: the mechanical stratum, whose gold is co-citation, shared experiment identifier or explicit supersession, gave +0.0458 at depth 5 against the tag stratum's +0.0625 and the pooled +0.0542, and failed to exclude zero only because n was 240. Leakage control removes every direct edge between a held-out pair regardless of type, so gains still require transitivity. Two limits are registered rather than glossed: pooling strata to gain power was decided after seeing them, and no threshold was preregistered because this is Tier E. The result is labelled supports-association-benefit-exploratory and its promotion path is a sealed held-out test under independence tier I1, which needs no reviewer, no model and no budget.
summary: PMLAB-ASSOC-E2 added same_experiment, supersession and shared_rare_tag edges, taking the graph from 102 to 240 edges over 174 active events. Across 480 paired queries the pooled benefit was +0.0542 Recall@5 with 95 percent CI [0.0104, 0.0979] and +0.0458 Recall@10 with CI [0.0063, 0.0854], both excluding zero where E1 could not.
title: Association graph gives a small consistent retrieval benefit, not driven by authored gold

body: Demonstrated directly rather than inferred: 'dlaczego nie mozna re-deklarowac zamrozonych hashy' returned 0 memories while 'why can frozen hashes not be re-declared' returned the exact failure record, and 'czy graf asocjacyjny pomaga w wyszukiwaniu' returned 0 while 'does the association graph help retrieval' returned 4 including both association findings. This is the zero cross-language recall already measured against FTS5 on the 24-query slice, now shown to make the store useless to the person who owns it. PMLAB-ASSOC-E2 explicitly registered cross-language as untested because its corpus is predominantly English, so the association graph is an untested candidate remedy rather than a known one. Local multilingual embeddings are already revision-pinned as candidates: multilingual E5-small, BGE-M3 and multilingual MiniLM. This does not argue for abandoning English as the repository language; it argues that the retrieval path must bridge languages even when storage does not.
summary: Two questions whose answers were written into memory today returned zero memories when asked in Polish and one and four memories when asked in English. Repository policy stores durable findings in English, the maintainer works in Polish, and FTS5 has no cross-language recall, so the owner's own queries retrieve nothing.
title: Project memory is unreadable in the language its owner uses

body: In-place migration is mechanically impossible rather than merely discouraged: the canonical-store guard fails any pull request removing a line from events.jsonl, and a modified line counts as a removal. Two alternatives were rejected. Rewriting destroys the record of what was written. Appending a translated copy of every event doubles the log and makes supersedes ambiguous, because a copy is not a revision. The v1 to v2 upcaster adds the bitemporal fields issue 29 requires and is deliberately conservative: valid_from defaults to created_at as the weakest honest reading, valid_to stays open because the log never recorded when a fact stopped being true, and claim_class is unclassified rather than guessed, since a guess written into an upcast later reads as recorded evidence. Totality and no-field-dropped are tested against the real 184-event log rather than a fixture. One limitation is recorded rather than glossed: the guard runs on pull requests only, so a direct push to the default branch bypasses it and the protection becomes procedural.
summary: All 184 events sit at schema_version 1 and nothing reads that field, so the versioning mechanism was decorative. tools/project_memory/upcast.py makes it real: old events stay on disk as written, the reader presents them in the current shape, new events are written at the current version, and a mixed-version log is the normal steady state.
title: Schema evolution happens by upcasting, never by rewriting the log

body: This is the operating doctrine's first selection rule applied to ourselves: check whether the answer exists before designing. The specific failure mode being corrected is that the audit was performed, the conclusion was recorded in memory, and the design then started from scratch anyway; the audit existed but the link from audit to design did not. Bitemporal modelling has been standard in databases since SQL:2011, so agent memory is late to it rather than pioneering. The borrow is of semantics only. Graphiti's graph backend and LLM extraction pipeline were already recorded as too heavy for this bootstrap, and field semantics and query rules are separable from both. No dependency is added by reading. Anything the borrowed model leaves unsolved must be listed rather than inherited silently, and every claim about another system needs a pinned revision, because the project has already been burned by self-reported figures. The upcasting harness landed the same day, so the migration path for whatever schema is chosen is built and tested against the real log; only the design is missing.
summary: The bitemporal schema in issue 29 is blocked on issue 34, a focused read of Graphiti's temporal model and the SQL:2011 temporal-table standard. Project memory already recorded that Graphiti represents changing facts with temporal validity and is a strong reference for provenance, temporal validity, episodes and non-destructive supersession, which describes exactly what issue 29 asks for.
title: Borrow temporal semantics rather than reinvent them

body: Justified by evidence rather than appeal: three defects were found by using the memory and would not have appeared in an authored fixture, namely retrieval starvation where the state summary consumed the whole context budget, an 89.1 percent disconnected graph with 57 unmaterialized shared source references, and silence in the maintainer's language. It also answers the corpus problem the triage exposed, where 0 of 21 registered experiments had one. The corpus is unusually good because it was produced by real work before anyone knew what would be measured against it, which is close to the ideal condition for tier I1: it could not have been shaped to flatter a candidate that did not yet exist. Three failure modes are registered with rules against each. N equals one, so every self-observed finding is labelled as such and may not pass tier I1 on that evidence alone. The tool shapes the data it is measured on, which PMLAB-ASSOC-E2 already brushed when authored tags became graph edges, so memory content is never authored to suit a feature under test. Dogfooding prioritises irritation over importance, which is why the context budget was fixed in an hour while causal utility measurement has stood for months, so at least one item in flight must serve a research question rather than a usage complaint. The line in CLAUDE.md holds unchanged: the tool supports research continuity and is not evidence that the architecture works. Origin inside our own tooling earns no discount on the ladder.
summary: The memory we build is the memory we use to build it, stated explicitly rather than left implicit. It has three roles: working infrastructure, a corpus that grows at zero cost, and a source of hypotheses that using it seriously surfaces. Designs are borrowed from outside where a mature answer exists; measurement happens here.
title: Bootstrapping is the strategy: our memory is corpus and hypothesis source, never validation

body: The zero graph gain is structural, not incidental: graph expansion is seeded from top lexical hits, so when lexical search returns nothing there are no seeds and nothing to expand. PMLAB-ASSOC-E2 registered cross-language as its untested case and speculated the graph would help precisely here; that speculation is refuted. The run also corrects E2: in English at depth 5, graph fusion scored 0.711 against lexical's 1.000, so on queries lexical already answers correctly the graph pushes the target out of the top five in 29 percent of cases. E1 measured that displacement cost and E2 dropped the metric, so E2 as published told only the favourable half. Combined honest reading: the graph helps slightly on hard queries, hurts substantially on easy ones, and does nothing when lexical returns nothing. Local dense retrieval remains untested because weights are absent under external/models and downloading roughly two gigabytes plus an inference runtime is a maintainer resource decision. The glossary is hand-built, unweighted, cannot handle paraphrase and will not generalise; it is a stopgap that makes memory usable for its owner today, not the answer.
summary: On 45 paired Polish and English queries against the project's own memory, Recall@10 fell from 1.000 to 0.156 with only the language changed, and 26 of 45 Polish queries returned zero candidates. The association graph contributed exactly 0.0000 with a confidence interval of [0,0]. A hand-built hundred-term glossary lifted Recall@10 to 0.867.
title: A graph on top of lexical retrieval cannot rescue a query lexical cannot start

body: The mechanism was verified before the run: cosine between the Polish and English phrasings of the same question was 0.675 and 0.701, against 0.177 for an unrelated Polish phrase. Language is dissolved rather than translated around. Two secondary results matter as much. The hybrid arm scored 0.933 against dense alone at 0.978, so fusing a working arm with a failing one costs recall; this is the third independent measurement today of fusion taxing the stronger arm, after graph fusion dropping English Recall@5 from 1.000 to 0.711 and the association graph contributing exactly zero on an empty lexical seed. Fusion needs a condition, not a habit. Second, dense beats the glossary by a margin whose interval touches zero, so on this corpus the cheap remedy is nearly as good; the real difference is coverage, since a glossary handles only terms its author foresaw. Critically, no safety metric was measured. PMLAB-REUSE-CHAR-001 measured dense forbidden intrusion at 0.200 against FTS5's 0.050, and the worst case is structural because a superseded fact is maximally similar to its replacement. The mechanism that fixes cross-language recall is the same one that worsens stale intrusion, already measured at 0.857. Recall 0.978 is a licence to test dense against the safety metric, not to adopt it, and that test needs the current-versus-superseded labels that issue 29 must define first.
summary: On the same 45 paired queries, Polish Recall@10 went from 0.156 with FTS5 to 0.978 with a 0.22 GB multilingual embedding, a gain of +0.8222 with CI [0.7111, 0.9333], and the target sat at mean rank 1.96 when found. The hand glossary reached 0.867, so dense beat it by only +0.1111 with the interval's lower bound at exactly zero.
title: Local dense retrieval dissolves the language gap but its safety cost is unmeasured

body: The defect is precise. Gold pairs were derived from shared sources, and the leakage control removed only the direct edge between the held-out pair. Every other event citing that same source stayed connected to both endpoints, so a two-hop path A to C to B ran entirely inside the gold-generating group rather than through a different source. The report's claim that any gain therefore still requires transitivity was false for most recoveries. The correct control removes the whole group sharing the gold-defining source or tag when a pair is held out, not just the edge. Two further criticisms are accepted. Pooling strata to gain power was decided after seeing them, so the pooled interval describes the sample rather than testing a hypothesis; the only stratum with non-authored gold, the mechanical one, included zero at both depths, and the report's line that it fails to exclude zero because n is 240 rather than because the effect is absent is unfalsifiable. The honest label is inconclusive, exactly as PMLAB-ASSOC-E1 was. The bootstrap implementation, by contrast, was checked and is correct, including under a clustered resample over edges rather than query directions.
summary: PMLAB-ASSOC-E2 reported +0.0542 Recall@5 with CI [0.0104, 0.0979]. Independent reproduction shows 67.5 percent of graph-reachable targets were reachable only through the group that defined the gold pair, and 63 percent of depth-10 wins came through that group. Neutralizing those recoveries turns the difference negative: -0.0644 at depth 5 and -0.0436 at depth 10.
supersession_reason: An adversarial review found that the leakage control was insufficient, and independent reproduction confirmed it. Removing the direct A-B edge left every other event citing the same source connected to both endpoints, so the group that defined the gold reassembled over two hops. The reported gain is an artifact of that leak, not evidence of an association benefit.
title: The association-graph benefit was an artifact of insufficient leakage control

body: Each defect is an instance of one pattern: a control checked something narrower than what was claimed, and a single author who was also the only reviewer had nobody to notice the gap. The leakage control removed the direct edge between a held-out pair but left every other event citing the same source connected to both endpoints, so the gold-generating group reassembled over two hops; reproduction found 67.5 percent of graph-reachable targets reachable only that way and the difference reversing to -0.0644 at depth 5. The supersession marker suppressed all hash checking below any directory containing a file of that name, with contents never parsed, so an empty JSON object silenced every broken freeze in the tree; a proof of concept demonstrated it and validation is now fail-closed. The sealed split had no ordering guard, so an author could reveal, read the challenge, re-register a memorising candidate, and verify still passed; register and reveal now refuse after a reveal exists, and the receipt binds the registration digest. Key grinding was also demonstrated, 4000 keys yielding a split with 81 percent of a chosen subset in the challenge half, and it cannot be fixed offline; the manifest now records whether the key was self-generated and therefore grindable, or externally witnessed. The review also checked and cleared the bootstrap implementation, the CRLF repair rule as cryptographically sound, and found no evidence destruction or freeze cascade, which is what makes the rest credible.
summary: An external adversarial pass, independently reproduced, found that the association-graph benefit was a leakage artifact, that the supersession marker was an unvalidated audit kill-switch, and that the sealed split reported eleven green checks on a candidate tuned to the revealed challenge. All three were confirmed by running code, not by argument.
title: Adversarial review found three real defects, two in tools built the same day

body: The obvious test was malformed: search already excludes superseded records by metadata, so measuring stale intrusion would have measured the filter. The question that matters is whether anything other than metadata could do that job, and the answer is no. Two statements of the same claim at different times are semantic near-neighbours by construction, and for two pairs the embeddings are identical, so content-based retrieval cannot distinguish them at all rather than merely doing it poorly. A better embedding makes this worse, because it places the two statements closer. This bounds PMLAB-XLANG-E2: dense recall of 0.978 is safe only because the supersession filter exists, so swapping the index is admissible but dropping the filter is not. It upgrades the recorded audit of NOBI327/amygdala, whose schema lacks supersession, from a missing feature to a correctness defect, since such a system returns stale facts as top results by construction. It also answers the recurring hair-colour example of issue 29: brown and green are the same claim at different times, no retrieval method can order them from content, and only valid time can, which is what the store currently lacks. Limits: n equals 9, one model, one corpus, and the pairs skew towards revisions of experimental findings.
summary: Across all 9 supersession pairs in the canonical log, a superseded memory and its replacement sit at the 99.5th percentile of corpus similarity, mean cosine 0.816 against a baseline of 0.372, with 7 of 9 above the corpus 99th percentile and two pairs at cosine exactly 1.000. With the metadata filter removed the stale record is the nearest neighbour in 6 of 9 cases, in the top five in 8 of 9, median rank 1.
title: Supersession cannot be solved by retrieval; it must live in the schema

body: E2's reported +0.0542 was entirely the leak. The failure is in how the graph is reached rather than in the graph itself: expansion is seeded from the top three lexical hits, which helps in neither regime. When lexical retrieval fails there are no seeds, measured in PMLAB-XLANG-E1 as a gain of exactly 0.0000 with interval [0,0] on Polish queries where 26 of 45 returned nothing. When lexical retrieval succeeds the graph displaces the correct answer, measured in the same experiment as English Recall@5 falling from 1.000 to 0.711, and here as 4.2 lexical positions surrendered per query. Three independent measurements now agree that reciprocal rank fusion with this graph taxes the stronger arm. What is not concluded: that graphs are useless for agent memory, since an entry point not depending on lexical success was never tested; and that the graph is worthless as structure, since materialising it took the memory from 10 edges to 240 and connectivity from about 11 percent to 92 percent, which remains useful for navigation and consolidation. The arc across three experiments is E1 inconclusive, E2 retracted as a leakage artifact, E3 measuring harm. Any future attempt needs a different entry point, not a bigger graph.
summary: With the leakage control repaired to remove every edge whose generating groups all defined the held-out gold pair, the graph harms retrieval. On mechanical gold, Recall@5 falls from 0.400 to 0.286, a difference of -0.1143 with 95 percent CI [-0.1786, -0.0536] excluding zero. Both strata point the same way at both depths and the graph harms roughly twice as many queries as it helps.
title: Association graph as retrieval fusion is closed with a negative result

body: This is the SQL:2011 bitemporal model rather than a novel design, which is the strongest reason to borrow. My draft for issue 29 proposed only valid_from and valid_to beside created_at, which is one and a half axes and cannot separate a record withdrawn as an error from a world that changed; the transaction-side end must be explicit. The correct-versus-succeed operations I proposed are unnecessary, because one mechanism with two timestamps carries the same distinction and is easier to verify. Three things are deliberately not borrowed. Temporal values there are LLM-extracted and dropped silently on a parse failure, logging a warning and storing the fact with no start time, which makes a lost value indistinguishable from an unknown one and would be rejected by our own mechanical gate. Contradiction detection is model-decided rather than mechanically checkable, whereas our supersedes field is explicit and auditable, narrower in coverage and stronger in provenance. And there is no decay mechanism, so the recurring hair-colour case stays unsolved and is recorded as a known limitation rather than filled with an invented rule. The design error in my draft was caught by twenty minutes of reading code, which is the operating doctrine's first selection rule paying for itself.
summary: Reading Graphiti's implementing code shows four temporal fields on two axes: created_at and expired_at for transaction time, valid_at and invalid_at for valid time. On supersession it sets the prior fact's invalid_at to the successor's valid_at and stamps expired_at at write time, so succession and correction need no separate operations. Issue 29 is revised accordingly.
title: Adopt the four-field bitemporal model and drop the proposed correct-versus-succeed operations

body: The adaptation is an improvement on a literal port rather than a compromise. A stored end can drift from the revision that caused it, because two places would then hold the same fact; a derived end cannot, because the successor is the single source. Derivation follows the same pattern the store already uses for the active view, which is replayed rather than stored. Two axes remove the need for separate correct and succeed operations, but the log must still record which occurred, because it changes what is derived: a succession means the world changed so valid_to is derived from the successor's valid_from, while a correction means the record was wrong so nothing about the world changed and only expired_at is derived from the successor's created_at. Every version-1 supersession is unclassified and derives no valid_to, since the log recorded that a conclusion was revised but never whether the world changed. On the real 194-event log the derivation fills expired_at for exactly the 9 superseded records and no valid_to at all, which is the correct outcome and is asserted as a test.
summary: Version 2 adopts the four-field SQL:2011 model, but valid_to and expired_at are computed at read time from the superseding event rather than written onto the record they end. Graphiti mutates the prior edge to end it; an append-only log cannot, and the canonical-store guard enforces that.
title: Bitemporal ends are derived from the successor, never stored on the prior record

body: Recorded as unreproduced rather than fixed. Asserting over the real log is deliberate and valuable, because it is what makes the totality and no-field-dropped guarantees real rather than fixture-shaped, but it inherits the concurrency constraint already recorded: multiple agent sessions may write to this repository, and an append between collection and assertion changes counts a test may depend on. Two mitigations are available and neither is applied yet: snapshot the log bytes once per test session and assert against the snapshot, or have such tests skip when the canonical digest changes mid-run. The diagnostic failure is also recorded: the failure name was lost because the grep pattern used did not match pytest's output format, so the next occurrence must be captured with the full output retained.
summary: One full-suite run failed once and then passed on three consecutive reruns; the failing test name was not captured because the output pattern used did not match. The likely cause is that test_upcast and test_verify_memory_integrity assert over the live memory/events.jsonl while another process may append to it.
title: Tests that assert over the live canonical log are sensitive to concurrent appends

body: The write path is complete across all three surfaces: store, MCP server and CLI, the last of which is the documented fallback when MCP is unavailable. The recurring hair-colour example now round-trips end to end. A succession records that brown hair was true from January until June and that the record was withdrawn today, so the past interval is closed rather than erased. A correction records that a mis-read measurement was withdrawn today while leaving valid_to empty, because the world never changed and the person was never that height. Storing the derived fields is refused rather than merely discouraged, because a stored end is a second source for one fact and can drift from the revision that caused it. Every version-1 event still reads correctly through the upcaster, and the canonical log remains 196 events with zero violations, none of them rewritten.
summary: SCHEMA_VERSION is 2. New events carry valid_from and claim_class; a supersession also carries supersession_kind of succession, correction or unclassified. valid_to and expired_at are never written and are derived from the successor at read time. The mechanical gate now rejects a stored derived field, a bad claim class, a bad supersession kind, and a malformed valid_from.
title: Schema version 2 is live: memory now records when a fact was true

body: The earlier diagnosis was wrong in its cause and right in its caution. It attributed the failure to tests asserting over the live canonical log while another session might append, which is a real hazard and remains recorded, but was not what happened here. The actual sequence was that appending a version-2 event made a true assertion false. Two lessons are worth keeping. First, the diagnostic failure was mine: the grep pattern used to capture the failing test name did not match pytest output, so the name was lost and the cause was guessed rather than read; the second occurrence was captured with --tb=no and named immediately. Second, the test was replaced rather than deleted, because a mixed-version log is the intended steady state and the invariant that actually matters is that every version present is known to the reader and none is newer than it can handle. A test that fails when the system changes correctly is doing its job; the error was pinning the wrong property.
summary: The failure recorded earlier as an unreproduced flake is now identified: test_canonical_log_is_currently_single_version asserted the canonical log held only schema version 1. It began failing the moment the first version-2 event was appended. It was not flaky in the usual sense; it was correct and pinned to an assumption the upcasting design deliberately broke.
title: The unreproduced test flake was a test pinning an invariant the design had broken

body: Detected only by noticing the total was unchanged after adding five tests. The mechanism is specific and easy to repeat: appending with a shell redirect to a file that ends in the guard block places the new methods inside it at the same indentation, so Python accepts them and pytest never sees them. Prevention is now mechanical rather than procedural. tests/test_no_unreachable_tests.py parses every test file and asserts each test function is reachable, meaning defined at module level or directly in a class body, never nested inside a conditional, loop, with, try, or another function. It carries the actual failure as a fixture so the guard itself is tested against the thing that happened. The suite went from 369 to 456 once the six orphans were restored and the guard added. The wider lesson is the one the independence ladder already states: a green suite is evidence only about the tests that ran, and nothing in this project verified that set until now.
summary: Test methods appended after a module's if __name__ guard were parsed as part of that guard, because its body shares the class body's indentation. They were valid code, were never collected, and the suite stayed green because a test that does not run cannot fail. A commit message stated that a regression test pinned the supersession invariant; that test had never once executed.
title: Six tests existed and never ran, and a commit claimed one of them pinned an invariant

body: The schema change made earlier today on the strength of a code comparison is now measured rather than argued, and this run could have falsified it. Each single-axis arm fails precisely the question the other axis answers: valid_only knows what was true and answers what we believed with information from the future, while transaction_only knows what was believed and cannot reconstruct world-state. The caveat that matters most is that every arm scores 1.00 on current, so if the only question ever asked is what is true now, version 1 was adequate and the change buys nothing; the value exists exclusively in historical questions. One bitemporal failure is worth more than the score: on a future-effective rule, the resolver treated a superseded record as dead the moment a successor existed, but when a superseding record's valid_from lies in the future the record it supersedes is still the answer. Supersession ends a fact at the successor's valid_from, not at the successor's existence. That trap is registered before the store grows a real query layer, which it does not yet have.
