body:
OPERATIONAL FIT: PASS. Nine dimensions, zero failures, zero unverifiable. Accuracy deliberately not scored and no claim about it is made.
WHAT PASSED, WITH THE MEASUREMENT.
 reset            engine state digest after reset is byte-identical to the pre-ingest digest.
 leakage          no evidence and zero context tokens from a store that was reset.
 session grouping 4 records over 4 distinct days became 4 sessions, indices 0..3, times 1/2/9/3 in the order given and not sorted, every turn role=user.
 session_time     stored items carry created_session_time in {1,2,3,9}, exactly the times the records carried. The time reaches state, not just the call.
 answer shape     types conform on all five probes.
 abstention       derivable on every probe. CUPMem has NO abstention channel: its composer is instructed to always answer, and PremiseVerdict.status (SUPPORTED/OUTDATED/UNRESOLVED) judges the question's premise, not the system's willingness. Zero abstentions observed, which is a property of the system rather than of the probes.
 evidence         5 ids per probe, every one traceable to an item the store holds.
 cost             NATIVE per field, fully known, not a lower bound.
 mutation         engine state digest identical either side of a query.
MEASURED COST, from CUPMem's own get_usage_summary():
 ingest, 4 records over 4 sessions: 31 calls, 52,882 prompt, 2,821 completion, 34.1s -> about 7.8 calls and 13,200 prompt tokens PER RECORD.
 query: 3-7 calls, 9,130-17,316 prompt, 5.5-8s each.
 whole run, from the arena's own ledger beneath the system: 108 calls, 216,137 prompt, 15,671 completion, /usr/bin/bash.076 at DeepSeek list price.
FOUR ADAPTER MAPPINGS WERE WRONG AND HAD TO BE FIXED FIRST. All four had been certified by a double the adapter's author wrote from the same reading, so the double agreed with the adapter exactly where the adapter was wrong.
 cost           probed llm.usage, which does not exist. LLMClient has get_usage_summary() and get_call_records(). We reported a competitor as unobservable on the axis this project insists on keeping separate from capability.
 abstention     read from verdict.unknown_current and answer.text. Neither exists; unknown_current is a section of the store and AnswerResult has answer/brief_rationale.
 session time   a record list spanning four days became one session carrying the first day.
 context tokens counted  keys, which their query path never emits (it emits payload.value and text_preview). Reported context_tokens 0 for a query that had just delivered five records - a false zero, not an unknown.
CONTROLS. Source pinned at commit ea7d391103a151927cd29d2f01d87597a782bdcb with a tree digest over 46 files; embedding revision 1110a243fdf4706b3f48f1d95db1a4f5529b4d41; response cache refused at construction because their client bills a cache hit as zero; decoding fixed at temperature 0 by wrapping their provider client, which overrode CUPMem's own 0.3 on 21 of 108 calls (their latent_invalidation_temperature).
summary: Real CupMemEngine, pinned source and embedding revision, decoding fixed at temperature 0. Reset, leakage, session grouping, session_time, answer shape, abstention, evidence, cost and query mutation all check out. Four adapter mappings had to be corrected first.

body:
MEASURED, deepseek-chat, temperature 0, 20 identical draws per probe:
 short_factual    1 distinct / 20, modal share 1.00  reproducible
 free_form        4 distinct / 20, modal share 0.75  NOT reproducible
 structured_json  3 distinct / 20, modal share 0.90  NOT reproducible

The third matters most. It is a short structured object of the kind every system in the arena asks for, where one differing field changes a parsed decision. Temperature does not fix this; it is a property of the deployment.

HOW IT SURFACED. CUPMem's query path is read-only over engine state, established twice: no apply_update, no chunk_bank append and no counter advance appears anywhere under query/, and a live run fingerprinted everything their own reset() clears either side of a query and got identical digests. On the strength of that the adapter declared read_only. The next run was rejected: "declared read_only but a repeated query returned different results". The store had not changed. The decoder had.

Sharper still, within one run: the operational-fit pass saw a repeated probe differ, and the frozen-contract pass minutes later saw it not differ. Same check, same process, two answers.

WHAT THIS COSTS.
 1. The contract's read_only is a STRONGER predicate than read-only. It means read-only AND reproducible, and no model-backed system can satisfy the second half. CUPMem is therefore declared `unknown` while we hold a proof that it is read-only, and a harness reading that field alone cannot learn that probe order does not matter for it.
 2. A frozen common run will not be bit-reproducible. A per-probe difference between two systems carries decoder variance that has not been separated out.
 3. Any single-run comparison has an unmeasured noise floor. On the structured probe the modal answer appeared 90% of the time, so roughly one call in ten differs, and a query chaining 3 to 7 calls compounds that.

WHAT IT DOES NOT SHOW. Whether this holds for another provider, another model, or the same model next month. Reproducibility is a property of a deployment. One provider, one model, one day, 20 draws, 3 prompts.
summary: 20 identical requests per probe against deepseek-chat at temperature 0: free-form gave 4 distinct outputs, structured JSON gave 3. The frozen contract detects query-time mutation by repeating a probe and comparing outputs, and therefore cannot separate a store that learned from a decoder that drew differently.
title: The arena's decoder is not reproducible at temperature 0, so the contract's mutation check cannot work

body:
THE RULE. A double certifies a contract only where it disagrees with its adapter. When the same person writes both from the same reading, the double encodes the adapter's assumptions and then certifies them.

EVIDENCE. Last session found the double had certified an ingest that stored nothing, and fixed that one field. The class was untouched. Reading CUPMem's code then found four more mappings the double had also certified wrongly: cost observability, abstention, session time, and context tokens.

THE STRUCTURAL FIX. The double now quotes their code, and each quotation names the module it came from. A separate module re-checks every quotation against the real checkout: their client's method names, the absence of the attribute the first adapter probed, the premise-status vocabulary, the answer field names, the snapshot sections, the chunker's filter, and that their query path contains no write.

THAT MODULE CAN FAIL, AND WAS SHOWN TO. Three mutations, each producing exactly one failure: a fabricated status added to the vocabulary; a field dropped from the state-fingerprint list; the double's chunker filter relaxed to accept anything.

THE COST. The external checkout is a gitignored local cache, so these checks skip in CI. A skipped check is not a passed one, which is why each quotation is also stated in prose in the double itself.
summary: The CUPMem double was written by the adapter's author from the adapter's reading, and agreed with the adapter in all five places the adapter was wrong. A point fix on one field last session did not address the class; reading their code found four more.
title: A test double must be built from the system's code, not from the same reading the adapter was built from

body:
The adapter must reset their tracker so that ingest cost and query cost are separable. The run total was then read from that same tracker at the end of the run, after a reset the contract validator performs, and reported 4 calls, 5,553 prompt tokens and $0.0026 for a run that had made 107 calls, 209,834 prompt tokens and $0.073. A factor of 28.

Both numbers are wanted, so both are now kept, in ledgers with different owners and different lifetimes. The system's counter answers what one operation cost, is resettable by the system, and is what the Cost fields are derived from. The arena's ledger sits beneath the system in the provider wrapper, counts every request, and cannot be cleared by anything the system does.

The ledger records per call rather than per run, for the reason already on the record: a background run once died after 29 calls with no result file and the spend was still real.
summary: CUPMem's usage tracker is cleared by reset_usage_tracking, and the adapter calls it on every reset so ingest and query price separately. Reading the run total off that same counter reported only what happened after the last reset.
title: A run total read from a counter the system can reset reported 4 calls for a run that made 107

body:
CORPUS. Every step of the arena plan says dry-run and frozen run without naming what they run on.
 STALE ships a generation pipeline and no dataset. Its data directory holds ontology seeds only, and building the benchmark requires background noise-session data plus its own model spend. Using STALE means generating STALE.
 LongMemEval-S cleaned is on disk at dataset commit 98d7416c24c778c2fee6e6f3006e7a073259d48f, with a frozen 36-question bridge selection in data/lab/longmemeval-bridge-v0. That selection was frozen for a lexical-retrieval transfer protocol, not for the arena, and its labels are public. Reusing it for the arena is a decision, not a default.

BUDGET, measured rather than guessed.
 rate, from the operational-fit run: 7.75 calls and 13,220 prompt tokens per single-turn session.
 corpus shape, counted from the file: 36 units, 1,736 sessions, median 48 sessions per unit, 8,830 user turns, so 5.1 user turns per session.
 floor projections for CUPMem ingestion alone, at DeepSeek list price:
   1 unit   48 sessions      374 calls    0.6M prompt   at least $0.21
   10 units 482 sessions   3,737 calls    6.4M prompt   at least $2.10
   20 units 964 sessions   7,474 calls   12.8M prompt   at least $4.19
   36 units 1,736 sessions 13,454 calls  23.0M prompt   at least $7.54
 Every figure is a FLOOR and must not be read as a total. The rate was measured on single-turn sessions; their write path spends per extracted chunk, so a 5-turn session yields more chunks and costs more. Query cost, retries, and the other four systems are all excluded.
 Realistic 20-unit dry-run: $8 to $20 per system. Five systems over the full bridge: three figures.

WHY THIS IS NOT MINE TO DECIDE. Total project spend to date is under $2, and every finding on the front page except the reader runs cost nothing. The corpus choice determines what the arena can claim; the budget determines whether it runs at all. Both are prior to any measurement.
summary: Operational fit passes, so the plan says dry-run next. The plan never names a corpus, and the first measured cost puts a 20-unit CUPMem dry-run at a floor of $4.19 against a project total under $2 to date.
title: The arena dry-run is blocked on two things nobody has decided: which corpus, and whose money

body:
THE FIELD'S STATED PURPOSE, from the frozen contract: evidence_ids is what the system put in front of its reader, and the harness needs it to separate never-retrieved from retrieved-and-misused.

THE PROBLEM. Doing that requires evidence in the arena's record space.
 AAMR stores the records, so it returns r1, r2, r3 and the mapping is free.
 CUPMem stores derived facts, so it returns i_00001-style item ids over its own schema. Five ids per probe, every one traceable to something its store holds, and none of them naming an ingested record.
Hindsight, Mem0 and Graphiti all extract too, so this is not a CUPMem property.

A MAPPING IS CONSTRUCTIBLE AND WAS NOT BUILT. ProfileItem.evidence_chunk_ids names chunks, SessionChunk.source_turn_ids names turns, and the adapter knows which record it wrote as which turn of which session. So item -> chunk -> turn -> record can be walked. It is one-to-many, because one item can merge several records.

WHY IT WAS NOT BUILT. The operating plan's own rule: if a system fails operational fit, question the requirement first, not how to work around it. A requirement no independent system can meet natively is a finding about the requirement. Record-level evidence provenance may be a requirement that exists only because our own system happens to keep raw records. Building the mapping quietly would have converted a finding about the arena into four adapters' worth of schema modelling.

WHAT IT COSTS TO LEAVE IT. Without a decision, the per-probe error matrix cannot attribute a CUPMem failure to retrieval rather than to use, for any system that extracts. That is one of Phase B's stated outputs.
summary: AAMR returns arena record ids because it stores records. CUPMem returns item ids for facts it extracted. The harness cannot ask 'was the gold record retrieved' across both, which is the question the field exists for.
title: evidence_ids is underspecified: the reference adapter answers in record ids and CUPMem answers in its own

body:
THE DEFECT. ARENA-0 decided query-time mutation by asking one probe twice and comparing the ANSWERS. A live run fingerprinted everything CUPMem's own reset() clears, either side of a query, and got identical digests; the contract on the next run reported "declared read_only but a repeated query returned different results" and rejected the adapter. Measured directly: deepseek-chat at temperature 0 gave 4 distinct outputs in 20 identical free-form requests and 3 in 20 structured ones.

THE AMENDMENT, in scripts/arena/adapter_v0_1.py, contract digest recorded in every result.
 query_mutates_state: read_only | mutates_by_design | unknown, decided by observing STATE through a probe. Without a probe it is unknown, which is recorded and is NOT a failure: a system that cannot expose its state must be controlled for, not excluded.
 output_reproducible: true | false | unknown, decided by repeating a request. A property of the decoder and the deployment, reported beside the systems it affects and never charged to one.
 read_only together with output_reproducible false is the ordinary case and is no longer treated as a contradiction.

WHAT DID NOT CHANGE. Measure, Cost, Answer and the three-method protocol are imported from ARENA-0 as the same objects, so this is an amendment rather than a fork, and a test asserts they are identical objects rather than copies.

ARENA-0 IS NOT EDITED. It stays in scripts/arena/adapter.py as the historical artefact, and a test asserts it still contains the rejection message it is being amended for. Results carry contract_version and contract_digest; ARENA-0 and ARENA-0.1 results must never share a table without an explicit version column.

EVIDENCE THE TESTS CAN FAIL. One test runs the same read-only-but-sampling adapter through both contracts and asserts ARENA-0 rejects it while ARENA-0.1 admits it. Another asserts no problem string in ARENA-0.1 ever mentions reproducibility, so reinstating the old rule in another spelling breaks the suite.
summary: ARENA-0's read_only was silently a conjunction of read-only and reproducible, which no model-backed system can satisfy. 0.1 measures state through a probe and reproducibility by repetition, and never infers one from the other.
title: ARENA-0.1 splits query_mutates_state from output_reproducible; ARENA-0 stays as the historical artefact

body:
MEASURED, unit ba358f49, 15 sessions, 69 user turns, 144 calls, 296,178 prompt tokens, 14,716 completion, $0.0962, 184 seconds.
Calls per session, in order: 8 1 1 1 10 7 11 15 14 20 1 15 13 12 15.
 first half mean  5.6
 second half mean 13.1

WHY. Their write path spends per accepted chunk and per invalidation proposal. An empty store yields no invalidation candidates, so the first sessions pay for chunking and little else. Once state exists, every session also pays for proposals and their judges.

WHY IT MATTERS TO THE ARENA. A cost column that reports dollars per record is reporting a number that depends on how much the system already remembers. Two systems measured at different corpus positions are not comparable on cost, and a per-record rate taken from a short prefix under-states a long run. The earlier projection extrapolated from four single-turn synthetic sessions and was wrong in both directions at once: it over-stated calls per session and missed the growth entirely.

DOES IT SATURATE. Believed yes, not proved. Every candidate pool in their config is top-k bounded (candidate_top_k 5, invalidation_global_recall_top_k 4, invalidation_merge_max_keep 2, query_top_k 8) so per-call prompt size cannot grow without limit, and the last three calibration sessions are flat at 13, 12, 15 rather than still climbing. The pilot projection therefore carries both a plateau model at $1.84 and a linear model at $4.00, and names which one it believes and why.

NOT SHOWN. Whether the plateau holds past 15 sessions. The pilot's per-session call series over 198 sessions will answer it, and that series is recorded for exactly this reason.
summary: Measured on 15 real LongMemEval sessions: 5.6 model calls per session over the first half, 13.1 over the second. An empty store has nothing to invalidate, so the write path's expensive lanes only switch on once there is state to work against.
title: CUPMem's ingestion cost is not linear in corpus size: it more than doubles as the store fills

body:
MEASURED, arena-pilot-v1, four units, 197 sessions, 996 user turns, identical harness and identical embedder.

  system   ingest    query     query calls   per-session cost shape
  CUPMem   $1.4802   $0.1091   4-8 / probe   rises: 5.6 -> 13.1 calls per session
  Mem0     $0.2960   $0.0000   0 / probe     flat at ~2 calls per session
  AAMR     $0.0000   $0.0000   0 / probe     no model anywhere

THREE THINGS THIS SETTLES THAT n=4 CANNOT THREATEN.
 1. Query cost is not a small part of the bill for one of these systems and is literally zero for another. Mem0's search is embedding retrieval and calls no model; CUPMem runs a chain of 4 to 8. A cost column quoted per query would rank them the wrong way round, and a cost column quoted per stored record would too.
 2. CUPMem's ingestion cost GROWS with the store and Mem0's does not. CUPMem's write path spends per invalidation proposal, and an empty store has nothing to invalidate; Mem0's add is a fixed extract-and-reconcile per session. So a dollars-per-record figure for CUPMem depends on where in the corpus it was measured, and for Mem0 it does not. Two systems measured at different corpus positions are not comparable on cost unless the shape is known.
 3. 93 percent of CUPMem's bill is paid before a single question is asked. Any evaluation that prices memory systems at query time would call it cheap.

WHAT THIS IS NOT. Not a statement about accuracy, quality, or which system is better. Four units, one run, a substring proxy, and a decoder that is not reproducible.

CONTROLS. Same four frozen units, same ingestion order, same embedder checkpoint (all-MiniLM-L6-v2, arena-enforced over each system's native default), same decoding (temperature 0, arena-enforced; CUPMem natively asks 0.3 on 544 of 1,985 calls, Mem0 0.1 on all of its). ARENA-0.1 throughout.
summary: On the same four frozen units: CUPMem $1.4802 ingest / $0.1091 query with 4-8 model calls per probe; Mem0 $0.2960 ingest / $0.0000 query with zero model calls per probe. Mem0's per-session cost is flat, CUPMem's more than doubles as the store fills.
title: Where the money goes differs by system in kind, not degree: CUPMem pays to remember, Mem0 pays nothing to recall

body:
MEASURED. Four units, 197 sessions, 996 user turns, zero model calls, zero dollars. Stored items: 0. State digest after ingest: unchanged from empty. Abstained: 4 of 4, channel 'no address resolved'.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A LOW SCORE. This is not a system that retrieved badly. Its deterministic address extractor fired on none of the 996 turns, so nothing was ever stored and the retrieval half never ran. E2-A and its successors reached 1.000 on this project's own corpus and 0.000 on external questions; that gap has been on the record as a registered negative since it was measured, and it has now been reproduced on a corpus this project did not write.

WHAT IT BUYS. A screen needs to know what zero looks like, and an arm that costs nothing can supply it on every future run without touching the budget. It also bounds the crude substring metric: a system that answers nothing scores 0 of 4, and two of the model-backed systems scored 1 of 4, so the metric's usable range on this sample is one unit wide. That is a fact about the sample, not about the systems.

NOT FIXED, DELIBERATELY. The arena measures what was frozen. Improving the extractor because the arena showed it failing would be tuning a system on the benchmark, and the negative is the finding.
summary: AAMR-CANDIDATE-0 through the same four frozen units ingested 996 user turns and stored zero records, then abstained on all four probes with 'no address resolved'. The registered negative, reproduced externally rather than asserted internally.
title: The reference system stored nothing at all on an external corpus: zero addresses resolved in 996 user turns

body:
WHAT WENT WRONG. The Mem0 state probe called get_all(user_id=...) and took the default limit of 100. Every unit then reported stored_items = 100 exactly, which is the tell, and evidence_all_traceable = False on all four, because the surfaced ids were checked against a truncated page rather than against the store.

WHY IT IS SERIOUS RATHER THAN UNTIDY. The probe exists to establish query_mutates_state by construction. A fingerprint over a prefix cannot do that: a query writing to row 101 would have left the digest identical and been recorded as read_only. The finding would have been an artefact of the page size, and nothing in the artefact would have said so.

THE SAME CLASS, TWICE. The CUPMem probe was written with an explicit guard against this — it verifies its field list against that engine's own reset() and raises if the engine grows state it does not watch. The Mem0 probe was written without one because get_all looked like it returned everything. The guard belongs on the probe, not on the author's attention.

FIXED BY CONSTRUCTION. The probe now pages fully and RAISES if it ever reaches its limit, so a truncated read stops the run instead of quietly measuring a prefix. The affected run is kept as pilot-mem0-truncated-probe.json rather than deleted, and was rerun.
summary: Mem0's get_all defaults to limit=100 and truncates silently. The first Mem0 pilot fingerprinted 100 rows of a larger store, reported exactly 100 stored items for all four units, and called every evidence id untraceable. All three were artefacts.
title: A state probe that read only the first page reported read_only for a store whose tail it never looked at

body:
WHAT WAS TRIED, in order, each fixed at the adapter level until one could not be.
 1. kuzu, their only in-tree embedded backend. Their own import says: "The Kuzu backend is deprecated and will be removed in a future release - the upstream Kuzu project is no longer maintained. Migrate to Neo4j or FalkorDB."
 2. clear_data on a store never written raises AttributeError on a private driver field. Fixed by building the schema before clearing - an ordering choice the adapter is allowed to make.
 3. add_episode with any explicit group_id runs graphiti.py:1079, `self.driver._database`, which KuzuDriver does not define, so every episode raises. Worked around by using their provider default group, which takes the other branch.
 4. json_schema structured output is rejected by DeepSeek with "This response_format type is unavailable now". Resolved with their own structured_output_mode='json_object' switch, which exists for providers without native json_schema.
 5. search raises "Binder exception: Table RelatesToNode_ doesn't have an index with name edge_name_and_fact". Their Kuzu driver creates node tables lazily on first write, so indices built before ingest are built on tables that do not exist, and rebuilding after ingest does not create this one either. THIS IS THE ONE THAT STOPS IT: it is inside their driver, and editing their source would mean the measured system is not the released one.
 6. falkordblite, their other embedded option, fails at pip build: "The redislite module is not supported on the win32 platform".

COST: four provider calls, $0.0030, counted in the night ledger.

WHAT THIS IS AND IS NOT. It is a finding about Graphiti's embedded deployment on this machine, and about the arena's infrastructure as much as about the system: the operating plan has carried "databases for Graphiti and Hindsight" as an open blocker since it was written, and Hindsight cleared it with an embedded Postgres while Graphiti did not. It is NOT a finding about Graphiti's temporal model, which is the reason it is in this arena and which none of this measured.

WHAT WOULD UNBLOCK IT: a Neo4j or FalkorDB service; or a non-Windows host, where falkordblite builds; or an upstream fix to a backend they have deprecated.

THE RULE THAT WAS FOLLOWED. Record BLOCKED with the exact reason and start the next system, rather than spending the night on one. Three of the six steps were legitimate adapter-level choices; the fourth would have been editing the system under test.
summary: Kuzu is deprecated upstream and its full-text index is never created, so search raises. falkordblite does not build on Windows. Everything else needs a database service. Adapter written, structural fit passes, operational fit never reached.
title: Graphiti is blocked by its deployment story, not by its mechanism: neither embedded backend runs here

body:
MEASURED, arena-pilot-v1, four frozen units, 197 sessions, 996 user turns, identical harness, identical embedder, ARENA-0.1.

 system      score  ingest    query    total     ingest calls  query calls  context tokens  evidence ids  mutation             reproducible  cost obs
 AAMR        0/4    $0.0000   $0.0000  $0.0000   0             0            0               0             read_only            true          native
 Mem0        1/4    $0.2939   $0.0000  $0.2939   337           0            93-112          10            read_only            true          instrumented
 CUPMem      1/4    $1.4802   $0.1091  $1.5892   1928          28           588-829         28-36         read_only            FALSE         native
 Hindsight   1/4    $1.7917   $0.0105  $1.8123   1246          1            3182-3330       159-188       mixed                mixed         instrumented
 Graphiti    BLOCKED, no runnable backend on this machine

WHAT SEPARATES THEM, AND WHAT DOES NOT.
 The score column separates nothing. Three systems scored exactly 1 of 4 and matched on the SAME unit, the knowledge-update one; the fourth scored 0 because it stored nothing. At n=4 with a substring proxy, that is one unit of range and no signal.
 Everything else separates them by factors.
  COST OF REMEMBERING: 0, $0.29, $1.48, $1.79. Six times between the two cheapest model-backed systems.
  COST OF RECALLING: exactly zero for Mem0 and effectively zero for Hindsight; $0.11 and 4-8 model calls per probe for CUPMem. Two of these systems do no model work at query time at all.
  CONTEXT DELIVERED: 100, 700, 3300 whitespace tokens. Hindsight puts thirty times as much before its reader as Mem0 does, on the same question.
  EVIDENCE GRANULARITY: 10, 30, 175. Mem0 returns a fixed top-k, Hindsight returns an order of magnitude more.
 These are regime differences, and none of them needs more units to be real.

THE ONE MEASUREMENT THAT DISAGREED WITH ITSELF. Hindsight's 'long' unit reported query_mutates_state = mutates_by_design and output_reproducible = false, while its other three reported read_only and true. Their server consolidates on a BACKGROUND WORKER, so a state change observed after a query is not necessarily caused by the query. This is recorded as an ambiguity the current probe cannot resolve, not as a property of their recall path. Resolving it needs a quiet-period check around the probe, which the pilot did not have.

DECODING. Every system was run at temperature 0, arena-enforced and NOT preregistered. CUPMem natively asks 0.3 on 544 of 1,985 calls; Mem0 asks 0.1 on all of its; Hindsight asks 0.1 or null on 1,290. Every override is recorded per call.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SHOW. Which system is better, at anything. Four units, one run, a substring proxy rather than LongMemEval's judge, and a decoder measured at 3-4 distinct outputs in 20 identical requests.
summary: AAMR, Mem0, CUPMem and Hindsight over the same four LongMemEval-S units. Total cost spans a factor of infinity to 6x, context delivered spans 0 to 3330 tokens, query-time model calls are 0 for two systems and 4-8 for one. All four scored 0-1 of 4 on the substring proxy, which separates nothing.
title: Four systems, one frozen sample: the differences that survive n=4 are structural, and none of them is accuracy

body:
WHAT HAPPENED. AAMR abstains, so its four raw answers are empty strings. The official LongMemEval prompt was filled in verbatim and the response slot was blank. The judge answered 'yes' to all four, in pass A and again in pass B, with no variation.

WHY THE EVALUATOR DOES NOT CATCH IT. LongMemEval's own runner always produces a hypothesis string, so an empty one never occurs in their pipeline. Their abstention template exists but is selected by the QUESTION ID ending in '_abs', not by the response being blank. An answerable question with an empty answer is outside the evaluator's domain and it fails open.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THIS RUN. Any system can obtain a perfect score on this evaluator by declining to answer. That is a property of the metric, not of the system, and it would have inverted the pilot's entire conclusion: the arm that stored nothing would have ranked first and the arm that answered the temporal question would have tied with it.

THE FIX, AND WHY IT IS NOT A NEW CRITERION. An empty response to an answerable question is scored wrong without a call, by the evaluator's own stated rule: 'answer yes if the response contains the correct answer'. Nothing contains nothing. Applying their rule to an input their code never sees is not inventing a second criterion. The abstention branch is left alone, because on a genuinely unanswerable question a blank response is a real judgement call.

HOW IT WAS FOUND. Because a zero-cost floor arm was in the pilot. Without AAMR the defect would have sat undetected in every future scored run — which is the argument for keeping a free arm on every one.

BOTH ARTEFACTS ARE KEPT. pilot-judged-unguarded.json holds the raw 4/4 with its judge outputs; pilot-judged.json holds the guarded run.
summary: The official evaluator, handed 'Model Response: ' with nothing after it, answered yes deterministically in both passes. That gave the arena's floor arm — which stored nothing and abstained on every probe — a perfect 4/4.
title: LongMemEval's judge scored an empty answer as correct, four times out of four

body:
PROTOCOL. LongMemEval src/evaluation/evaluate_qa.py @ 9e0b455f: per-type prompt templates verbatim, temperature 0, max_tokens 10, n 1, label rule "'yes' in response.lower()", binary with no partial credit. One deviation, recorded: judge model is deepseek-chat because this machine has no OpenAI credential. Scores are comparable within this run and NOT with published LongMemEval numbers.

RESULT.
 system     judged  substring  pilot cost  $/correct
 AAMR       0/4     0/4        $0.0000     -
 Mem0       1/4     1/4        $0.2939     $0.2939
 CUPMem     1/4     1/4        $1.5892     $1.5892
 Hindsight  2/4     1/4        $1.8123     $0.9062

PER PROBE, one question per type, so each cell is a single observation and not a rate.
 short  / multi-session         nobody
 medium / temporal-reasoning    Hindsight only
 long   / single-session-user   nobody
 update / knowledge-update      Mem0, CUPMem, Hindsight

THE PATTERN WORTH THE MONEY. The unit every model-backed system solved is knowledge-update — a fact superseded by a later one. The unit only Hindsight solved is temporal-reasoning. The two nobody solved are the plain find-the-evidence retrieval questions, on haystacks of 41 and 57 sessions. On this sample the systems agree on what is easy and disagree on exactly one question, and the one they disagree on is temporal. That is the first cross-system observation consistent with the operating-regimes hypothesis this project has carried as an internal pattern, and one question is not enough to promote it from observation to anything more.

JUDGE STABILITY. 16 of 16 stable across two independent passes; zero needed a third. Notable given the same provider gave 3 distinct outputs in 20 identical structured requests: a ten-token yes/no is far more stable than the structured extraction calls the systems themselves make.

THE SUBSTRING PROXY WAS ALMOST RIGHT, AND WRONG WHERE IT MATTERED. One false negative, zero false positives: it missed Hindsight's temporal answer, which is the single result that separates any system from any other. The earlier "everyone scored 1/4" was therefore an artefact of the metric on precisely the one cell that carried signal.
summary: LongMemEval's own evaluator, prompts verbatim, 16/16 judgements stable across two passes, $0.0011. Hindsight is the only system that answered the temporal-reasoning unit; all three model-backed systems answered knowledge-update; nobody answered the two retrieval units.
title: Judged on the frozen four: Hindsight 2/4, Mem0 and CUPMem 1/4, AAMR 0/4, and everyone solved the same update unit

body:
WHAT WAS LOST. The composed answer text for Mem0's and Hindsight's four arena-pilot-v1 units. The file is rewritten on every flush, so it went as soon as the expansion run started. pilot-raw/ is gitignored, so there was no committed copy.

WHAT SURVIVED, AND WHY IT MATTERS LESS THAN IT COULD HAVE. The sixteen judgements are in pilot-judged.json, which is committed, so every label, both judge passes and the raw judge output for those four units are intact. The per-unit metrics are in pilot-mem0.json and pilot-hindsight.json, also committed. The ten-unit report reuses those JUDGEMENTS rather than re-judging the answers, so the loss changes no result. AAMR's and CUPMem's raw files were untouched because neither system was rerun.

THE DEFECT. The output path was derived from the system name and nothing else, while every other artefact the runner writes takes its name from the run. A second selection over the same system was therefore guaranteed to overwrite the first, and nothing warned.

THE FIX. Raw answers are now written to data/lab/arena/raw/<selection_id>/<system>.json. Two runs of one system under different selections can no longer collide, and the path names the experiment rather than only the system.

WHY IT WAS NOT CAUGHT EARLIER. Every prior run was a first run for its system under its selection, so the collision could not arise; and CUPMem's and AAMR's raw files still sit at the old path as evidence that nothing else was touched. A path that is only safe while no experiment is ever repeated is not safe.
summary: The pilot runner wrote raw answers to data/lab/arena/pilot-raw/<system>.json regardless of which selection was running. Starting the expansion destroyed the pilot's raw answer text for Mem0 and Hindsight within seconds, before anything had been judged.
title: A fixed per-system path let a second run overwrite the first run's raw answers

body:
MEASURED, arena-expansion-v1, ten units, evidence mapped to corpus sessions by session date, no semantic guessing.

  system     answered  gold-in-context  mean gold rank  mean p@k  mean evidence  mean context
  Mem0       2/10      4/5              1.0             0.54      10             106 tokens
  Hindsight  4/10      5/5              22.4            0.12      ~150           3,158 tokens

WHY THIS IS THE RESULT WORTH HAVING. The arena was built to separate never-retrieved from retrieved-and-misused, and this is the first run that could. On this sample the answer is unambiguous: retrieval nearly always succeeded. Nine of ten observable units across two systems had a gold session in the delivered context, and six of those ten answers were still wrong. Spending more on retrieval quality would buy almost nothing here.

TWO SYSTEMS, TWO ROUTES TO THE SAME RETRIEVAL OUTCOME. Mem0 returns ten memories at precision 0.54 and finds gold at rank 1. Hindsight returns about a hundred and fifty at precision 0.12 and finds gold at mean rank 22. Both get it into context. One is surgical and one is a dragnet, and on gold-in-context they are equivalent — a genuine operating-regime difference that costs Hindsight thirty times the context tokens and six times the money.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT IDENTIFY. Where downstream the failure is. NEITHER SYSTEM COMPOSES AN ANSWER: both return a stored memory, and the judge compares that memory against a gold answer. So part of what is being scored may be the absence of a reader rather than a failure of memory. This data cannot separate that from genuine reasoning failure, and the next experiment worth running is the one that can — the same retrieved context handed to a fixed reader for both systems.
summary: Over ten units, Mem0 retrieved a gold session in 4 of 5 observable units at mean rank 1.0 and answered 2 of 10. Hindsight retrieved one in 5 of 5 at mean rank 22.4 and answered 4 of 10. The evidence was there and the answer was wrong anyway.
title: Retrieval is not the bottleneck: both systems put the gold session in front of the reader and still answered wrong

body:
WHAT WAS UNDER TEST. The pilot's only difference between systems was a single temporal-reasoning unit that Hindsight answered and nobody else did. arena-expansion-v1 was built to test it, with temporal-reasoning deliberately at 3 of 10 against a corpus proportion near 1 in 6 — a confirmatory sample, designed after the result, and never to be read as representative.

RESULT.
  temporal-reasoning   Hindsight 1/3   Mem0 0/3   margin 1 unit
  pilot                Hindsight 1/1   Mem0 0/1   margin 1 unit

The margin did not grow when the sample tripled. Replication would mean the effect held its RATE, not merely its sign, and it did not.

AND THE LEAD IS NOT TEMPORAL. Hindsight answered 4 of 10 against Mem0's 2 of 10, but only one of those four is temporal. The others are two knowledge-update and one single-session-user. Whatever separates these two systems on this sample is not concentrated in the type the run was built to test, which is the opposite of what a confirmatory design is supposed to find.

A CORRECTION MADE BEFORE IT SHIPPED. The first version of the verdict rule called any Hindsight lead over three units 'replicated', and it would have reported this as a confirmation. Leading 1-of-3 against 0-of-3 is the same one-unit margin the pilot already had. The rule now requires the rate to hold, and the sign alone returns 'weakened'.

WHERE BOTH AGREE. Both answered 2 of 3 knowledge-update and 0 of 2 multi-session. Superseded facts are the type these systems handle; multi-session retrieval is the type neither does.
summary: The pilot had Hindsight 1/1 and Mem0 0/1 on temporal-reasoning. Over three temporal units it is Hindsight 1/3, Mem0 0/3. The sign survived, the rate did not, and Hindsight's overall 4-2 lead is not concentrated in temporal.
title: The temporal signal weakened rather than replicated: the margin stayed at one unit while the sample tripled

body:
WHAT WAS NEEDED AND WHAT EXISTS. The experiment hands each system's delivered context, verbatim and in order, to one identical reader. What the artefacts hold is context_tokens (a count), evidence_ids (identifiers), and the single top memory as the system's answer. The other retrieved items exist only as ids.

WHY THE IDS DO NOT HELP. The runner calls adapter.reset() before every unit, so each store holds one unit at a time. After the run: Hindsight's bank reports 0 memories, Mem0's collection holds 271 points, one unit's remnant. Nine of ten units per system are gone from both stores. An id cannot be resolved against a store that no longer contains it.

WHY NOTHING WAS RECONSTRUCTED. Re-running retrieval would produce a different measurement wearing this one's name, and rebuilding a context from ids by matching text would be the semantic guessing the retrieval-truth module already refuses. Both were forbidden by the experiment's own terms and both would have been wrong anyway.

THE DEFECT, STATED GENERALLY. A measurement was taken of an artefact that was then discarded. context_tokens is a summary of something, and the something was never kept, so the summary can never be checked, re-analysed or reused. This is the same class as a state probe that reads one page: what was measured is not what was preserved.

FIXED. Adapters now report context_texts — the distinct delivered texts in delivered order — and the runner persists them beside the answer. The cost is bytes.

WHAT IT COST. The experiment as designed needs a re-ingest of ten units for both systems to regenerate contexts, which is roughly $3.10 at measured rates. That is not spent, and the question it would answer is still open.
summary: Twenty of twenty memory arms are UNOBSERVABLE. The runner recorded how many tokens each system delivered to its reader and never recorded what they were, and both stores are reset per unit, so nothing can be looked up. Only the question-only baseline was runnable.
title: The fixed-reader experiment could not run: context tokens were counted and the context itself was thrown away

body:
MEASURED. Ten units of arena-expansion-v1, one reader (deepseek-chat, temperature 0, max_tokens 300), the fixed reader prompt given verbatim, no memory context at all. Judged by the corrected LongMemEval protocol with the empty-response guard. 10 of 10 judgements stable across two passes, zero disputed. $0.0015 for the whole arm including judging.

  baseline                    0/10
  Mem0, no common reader      2/10
  Hindsight, no common reader 4/10

WHAT IT SETTLES. Contamination and prior-knowledge shortcuts are ruled out for this sample. These questions cannot be answered without the haystack, so any score above zero is memory doing work. That was worth knowing before spending more: a baseline near the systems' scores would have meant the arena was measuring the reader's training data.

  baseline wrong and a memory system right   5 of 10
  baseline right and both memory wrong       0 of 10
  memory turned a right answer wrong         0 of 10

WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE, AND THIS IS THE IMPORTANT HALF. The Mem0 and Hindsight columns above are NOT reader-vs-reader. Those two systems were never given the common reader — their contexts had not been persisted — so each system's "answer" is still its top stored memory judged against a gold answer. Comparing them with the baseline is comparing a composed answer against a raw memory, and the difference between 2 and 4 remains uninterpretable for exactly the reason this experiment existed to remove.

So the baseline rules out one explanation of the earlier result and leaves the main one open.
summary: The question-only baseline, same reader and same prompt as the memory arms, answered none of the ten units. On five of them a memory system answered where the baseline did not, and on none did memory turn a right answer wrong.
title: A reader with no memory scores 0 of 10: the benchmark is not answerable from model priors

body:
PROTOCOL. arena-expansion-v1, ten units, both systems rerun for context persistence only — no setting changed. One reader (deepseek-chat, temperature 0, max_tokens 300), one system prompt given verbatim to all three arms, blind to system identity. Judged by LongMemEval's own evaluator with the empty-response guard. 30 of 30 judgements stable across two passes, zero disputed. $5.1732 of a $6.00 cap.

  arm         correct  gold-in-context  mean gold rank  mean p@k  mean context
  Hindsight   7/10     9/9              10.44           0.088     3,117 tokens
  Mem0        4/10     8/9              1.00            0.578       106 tokens
  no memory   0/10     -                -               -             0

WHAT THE READER CHANGED. Both systems roughly doubled: Mem0 2->4, Hindsight 4->7. So the earlier ten-unit numbers were substantially an artefact of judging a raw stored memory against a gold answer, exactly as suspected. What did NOT change is the ordering — Hindsight was ahead by 2 units and is now ahead by 3.

THE RESULT THAT REVERSES AN EARLIER READING. Retrieval quality and answer quality come apart, and they come apart in the direction opposite to the obvious one. Mem0 puts the gold session at RANK 1 in eight of nine observable units, with precision 0.578 and 106 tokens of context, and still answers only 4 of 10. Hindsight buries gold at mean rank 10.44 with precision 0.088 among 3,117 tokens, and answers 7. Four of Mem0's six failures are RETRIEVED_READER_WRONG: the gold was at rank 1 and the answer was still wrong.

So precision and rank do not predict answer quality here. Volume does. On this sample the surrounding low-precision material is doing work that the single right memory cannot do alone — plausibly because a memory system's extracted fact is not the same object as the passage that supports an answer. That is a hypothesis this data raises and does not test.

FAILURE DECOMPOSITION, ten probes.
  MEMORY_ASSISTED_SUCCESS          8   baseline wrong, at least one memory arm right
  MEMORY_INTERFERENCE              0   memory never turned a right answer wrong
  RETRIEVED_READER_WRONG mem0      4
  RETRIEVED_READER_WRONG hindsight 2
  RETRIEVAL_FAILURE mem0           1   the only genuine retrieval miss in either system
  BOTH_ARMS_CORRECT                3
  BOTH_ARMS_WRONG                  2
  UNKNOWN (unobservable retrieval) 1 per system

PER TYPE, one to three units each, so each cell is an observation and not a rate.
  knowledge-update    Mem0 2/3  Hindsight 2/3
  temporal-reasoning  Mem0 1/3  Hindsight 2/3
  single-session-user Mem0 1/2  Hindsight 2/2
  multi-session       Mem0 0/2  Hindsight 1/2

REPLICATION CHECK. The six units Mem0 had run before were rerun: gold-in-context identical on all six, gold rank identical on all six, precision@k identical on three and within 0.2 on two. The rerun is the same measurement with telemetry added.
summary: Giving both systems' persisted contexts to one identical reader roughly doubled both scores (Mem0 2->4, Hindsight 4->7) and widened the gap. Hindsight's 30x larger, thirty-times-less-precise context beats Mem0's rank-1 retrieval by three units.
title: With one reader over both contexts: Hindsight 7/10, Mem0 4/10, no memory 0/10 — and the earlier scores were half artefact

body:
Supersedes no prior record; extends PM-20260823-aea83c73 (APEX-MEM / Verbatim Chunks pass) and confirms A-TMA, left unverified there, is real and matches its reported claims exactly including +0.240 accuracy over Graphiti.

NOVELTY NOW CLOSED (previously open or assumed in project framing): 'no single memory substrate dominates, therefore route' is Harness the Memory's own dated headline (submitted 15 Aug 2026), not available as an AAMR novelty claim. 'A controller over memory operations' (MemCon), 'learned selection among memory structures' (FluxMem), 'learned write-admission' (MemRouter), 'autoresearch of retrieval config' (EvolveMem + at least 5 adjacent 2026 papers) are all taken. Note: Harness the Memory and MemCon share 4 authors, and MemRouter shares a 5th with Harness the Memory -- this looks like one coordinated research cluster working the controller angle from multiple sides, a bigger threat than 3 unrelated papers.

CANDIDATE OPEN GAP, bounded by a real but non-exhaustive search: an explicit BASE/BASE+A/BASE+B/BASE+A+B interaction measurement between mechanisms extracted from two or more independently-built, pre-existing systems' own codebases, run before any router is trained on the result. Closest found: A-TMA (found via broad sweep to already compare 9 pre-existing host systems under one harness, not disclosed in the original brief) and 'Exploring Cross-Scenario Generality of Agentic Memory Systems' (arXiv 2606.04315, not previously known to this project -- its AutoMEM system literally imports code-level components from two named prior systems, PlugMem + LightMem, the closest precedent found anywhere). Neither runs the full interaction grid or trains a router over cross-system-validated mechanisms. One lead (OpenReview id AIJsjIqfsp, 'Memory Transplants for LLM Agents') could not be verified -- access blocked three times -- and is flagged for a direct follow-up check.

RECOMMENDED NEXT DIRECTION: run the 3 experiments in the full report before any controller work -- (1) transplant Hindsight's code-verified deterministic entity resolver onto Mem0's baseline on the frozen 10-unit arena-expansion-v1 sample, (2) a cheap deterministic approximation of A-TMA's current/historical/transition tagging on the 3 weakened temporal-reasoning units, (3) raw-source-chunk supplementation on Mem0's gold-in-context-but-wrong failures. All Tier E, near-zero cost, doctrine-compliant. Controller work stays gated until at least 2 independently-transplanted mechanisms each show a replicated positive isolated delta and one BASE+A+B interaction has actually been measured.
summary: Primary-source check of 11 claimed papers (Harness the Memory 2608.15008, MemCon 2607.13591, FluxMem 2602.14038, A-TMA 2607.01935, D-MEM 2603.14597, Microsoft Human-Inspired 2605.08538, MemRouter 2605.00356, MINTEval/ex-LongMINT 2605.18565, Supersede 2606.27472, Engram 2606.09900, EvolveMem 2605.13941) found all 11 real, with fixable citation issues (D-MEM name-collides with the unrelated Zou et al. DeMem 2605.10870 already in this project's reading queue; LongMINT renamed to MINTEval at v2; FluxMem name-collides with two unrelated papers). Full report: docs/research/RELATED_WORK_AND_POSITIONING_2026-08-24.md.
title: All 11 externally-claimed 2026 papers verified real; the open gap narrows to cross-system transplant-and-ablate, not routing itself

body:
arena-context-ablation-v1, $0.0288 of a $0.50 cap. No ingest, no retrieval, no new units, no change to either system or to the reader. 48 of 48 judgements stable across two passes, zero disputed. Frozen manifest with source hashes, reader prompt hash, judge protocol hash and the transformation rules written before any call.

EXPERIMENT A, HINDSIGHT CONTEXT-SIZE CURVE. Whole evidence items, original order, added while the next fits the budget; no re-ranking, no summarising, no item chosen using the gold answer.
  budget      mean tok  gold kept  correct
  Mem0-matched   102      7/9       4/10
  500            499      8/9       6/10
  1000           998      8/9       6/10
  full          3117      9/9       7/10

THE NUMBER THAT MATTERS. At Mem0's own per-probe token budget Hindsight scores EXACTLY 4/10 - Mem0's score. The advantage does not exist at equal context size and returns as the budget grows. Since the budget is the only thing that varies, this is causal evidence for context breadth ON THIS FROZEN SAMPLE. It is not a general law and not a claim that volume is what a memory system should optimise.
Most of the gain arrives by 500 tokens; 500 and 1000 are identical, so there is a plateau there and only the tenth unit needs full breadth.

EXPERIMENT B, RAW PROVENANCE. The raw source session whose date matches Mem0's top-1 hit, verbatim, about 2,150 words, appended to its compact context. Mapping by session date only; one unit is UNOBSERVABLE because its haystack repeats a date.
  Mem0 compact                 4/10
  Mem0 compact + raw top-1     4/9
  Mem0 raw top-1 only          3/9
  COMPACT_WRONG_RAW_FIXES        0
  RAW_CAUSES_REGRESSION          0
The same four probes are right in both arms. H3 - that Mem0's compaction discarded the supporting passage - is REFUTED on this sample. And raw-only is WORSE than compact, so compaction is doing work rather than merely losing information.

FAILURE MODES, KEPT APART.
  GOLD_DROPPED_BY_BUDGET      4
  GOLD_PRESENT_READER_WRONG  10
Even inside the truncation curve, losing the gold is the minority failure. Having it is not sufficient.

WHAT REMAINS UNTESTED. 500 tokens of Hindsight already beats 106 of Mem0, and this experiment never varied MEM0's breadth, so breadth-alone and difference-in-kind are not separated. One non-monotonic cell (the `medium` probe answered at 102 and 500, missed at 1000, answered at full) is noise until replicated and is recorded as such rather than explained.

PROMOTION. BROAD_CONTEXT_EXPANSION, PROMOTE to an isolated test, on the grounds that it is the only candidate with controlled evidence. RAW_PROVENANCE_EXPANSION dropped as next candidate. title: Hindsight's advantage is context breadth, and raw provenance explains none of it: 4/6/6/7 against 0 repairs

body:
ROOT CAUSE, confirmed in their code and proved empirically. mem0/memory/main.py Memory.delete_all resolves the rows to remove with self.vector_store.list(filters=filters)[0] and passes NO limit; QdrantVectorStore.list is declared list(self, filters=None, limit: int = 100). One call therefore deletes at most a hundred memories however many the store holds. Proved without any model call: 250 stored, delete_all left 150, a second call left 50 - exactly 100 per pass.

OUR HALF OF IT, which is the worse half. The adapter called delete_all ONCE and wrapped it in `try/except Exception: pass`, never checking that the store was empty afterwards. The cap is Mem0's. Not verifying the postcondition is ours, and it is what turned a library limit into ten units of quietly wrong results.

MEASURED CONSEQUENCE, ten-unit rerun, per run position. Residue entering each unit is derived from the proved cap plus the measured store size after each ingest.
  #  unit                   residue in  after ingest  own items  foreign evidence delivered
  1  short                        0          220        220        0
  2  medium                     120          242        122        0
  3  long                       142          239         97        1
  4  update                     139          253        114        1
  5  temporal-reasoning-1       153          262        109        0
  6  temporal-reasoning-2       162          298        136        1
  7  knowledge-update-1         198          351        153        1
  8  knowledge-update-2         251          389        138        0
  9  multi-session-1            289          392        103        0
 10  single-session-user-1      292          355         63        4
Eight of one hundred delivered evidence items belonged to other units of the same selection, and each of the four in the last unit maps to a DIFFERENT earlier unit.

SECOND-ORDER EFFECT, the part that is easy to miss. Residue changed what Mem0 WROTE, not only what it retrieved. Derived own-items per unit fall from 220 to 63 as residue grows, because Mem0's add reconciles against existing memories and increasingly chose UPDATE or NOOP over ADD. So the contamination reached the write path.

HINDSIGHT IS CLEAN, and the audit metric nearly said otherwise. A first pass reported 585 of 1458 Hindsight evidence items carrying a date outside the unit's haystack, which reads as catastrophic contamination. ZERO of those 585 map to any other unit in the selection: they are dates Hindsight derived from content rather than session timestamps. Its reset_returns_to_empty is True on all ten units. Reporting the 585 as contamination would have been a false accusation produced by my own instrument.

WHAT IS AFFECTED. Every Mem0 result in the project: the four-unit pilot, the six-unit expansion, the ten-unit rerun, the fixed-reader mem0 arm at 4/10, its gold-rank-1 retrieval figures, and all three context-ablation mem0 arms. Artefacts are marked INVALIDATED_BY_CROSS_UNIT_CONTAMINATION and kept, not deleted.
WHAT IS NOT. Hindsight throughout, including its context curve 4/6/6/7. The question-only baseline at 0/10. CUPMem, whose engine reset reassigns its collections and whose operational fit verified a byte-identical state digest. AAMR, which stored nothing.

FIXED BY CONSTRUCTION. reset() now loops delete_all until the bank measures empty, bounded at 64 passes, and RAISES if the store stops shrinking while non-empty. Five regression tests, four of which fail against the previous code, including one that ingests unit A, resets, ingests unit B and asserts A cannot appear in B's delivered context.
summary: Their delete_all resolves rows with vector_store.list(filters) and passes no limit, and that method defaults to limit=100. Units stored 220-392, so every reset left 120-292 behind. 8 of 100 delivered evidence items came from other units. Hindsight is clean.
title: Mem0's reset deleted at most 100 memories per call, so every arena unit ran on the previous units' residue

Total cost $0.767607 against a $1.00 experiment-scope cap (ingest $0.740452, reader $0.023023 across an original 40-call run plus a 17-call corrective delta after fixing a truncation bug, judge $0.004132).

Unlike Hindsight, Mem0's gold_in_context is already 9/9 (of 9 observable units) at its smallest, native arm -- so NEW_GOLD_COVERAGE is structurally impossible here (0 of 4 unit-transitions). body:
Fix: truncate() continue->break (same defect, same fix as PM-20260824-aba1b1f7's Mem0 case). Also fixed kept_times, which aligned evidence times to kept items by TEXT equality (`item in keep`) rather than position -- provably harmless once truncate() is prefix-correct, but that safety depended entirely on the invariant that had silently broken, so replaced with direct positional slicing. Also discovered mid-audit: raw/arena-expansion-v1/mem0.json is not a stable artifact -- it gets overwritten by the newest Mem0 run against the same selection_id (this session's clean rerun overwrote it), so the hindsight_mem0_matched arm's budget was pinned to the historically-recorded per-unit value instead of being recomputed, or the correction would have silently started matching against the wrong (clean, not contaminated) Mem0 context sizes. Also found and fixed: run_breadth_reader.py/run_breadth_judge.py hardcoded their own ledger run_id, so this correction's --cap-scope ablation-fix- never actually matched any of its own spend -- the /usr/bin/bash.10 intended scope cap was not the operative constraint (the flat /usr/bin/bash.05+/usr/bin/bash.05 per-run ceilings were); true spend was /usr/bin/bash.008, nowhere near either cap, but the scoping mechanism itself needed a --run-id parameter to work as designed. Fixed for future reuse.

Effect of the fix alone (old buggy judged labels vs corrected): 1 of 30 flipped (False->True, hindsight_mem0_matched, gpt4_f420262c), 0 regressed. gold_state changed for 0 of 30 despite 18 having different context text.

Cross-budget mechanism, corrected Hindsight curve: gold_in_context 7/9 (matched) -> 8/9 (500) -> 8/9 (1000) -> 9/9 (full) observable, unlike Mem0's flat 9/9 at every budget -- Hindsight has real headroom to gain from newly-surfaced gold that Mem0 structurally lacks, yet in this specific 10-unit sample that headroom did not land on the same units that flipped answer-correctness (NEW_GOLD_COVERAGE 0, same as Mem0's 0). Both curves' movement is GOLD_ALREADY_PRESENT_MORE_CONTEXT_FIXES (Hindsight 3, Mem0 2) against ADDITIONAL_CONTEXT_REGRESSION (Hindsight 1, Mem0 2).

Final comparison:
  Mem0:      native 5/10  500 6/10  1000 6/10  3000 5/10
  Hindsight: matched 5/10  500 6/10  1000 6/10  full 7/10

Causal reading: breadth, matched exactly, explains essentially the entire historically-reported gap through ~1000 tokens -- the two curves are identical there. It stops explaining anything at the widest budget: Mem0's own extra context nets negative (2 fixes, 2 regressions) while Hindsight's nets positive and reaches its sample maximum. That specific, localized divergence -- not a diffuse shortfall across the whole curve -- is the signal that something about representation or composition, not sheer volume, is what lets Hindsight use a very wide context productively where Mem0 cannot.
summary: Closed the last methodological gap in arena-mem0-breadth-ablation-v1: mechanism_ablation.py (source of the reused Hindsight curve) had the identical continue-vs-break truncation bug as mem0_breadth_arms.py. Audited against the still-frozen, untouched Hindsight retrieval data (no new Hindsight ingest/retrieval), fixed, and only the 18 of 30 affected (arm,unit) pairs re-read (/usr/bin/bash.008 total). Corrected Hindsight curve: matched 5/10 (was wrongly 4/10), 500 6/10, 1000 6/10, full(3117) 7/10 (unchanged, never truncated). Against clean Mem0's 5/6/6/5, the two systems are now EXACTLY tied at every comparable budget except the widest, where Mem0 falls back to 5/10 and Hindsight climbs to 7/10. Verdict: REPRESENTATION_COMPOSITION_SIGNAL.
title: Corrected: at matched budgets Mem0 and Hindsight tie exactly (5/6/6); the whole residual gap is at the widest budget, where Mem0 regresses and Hindsight keeps climbing

Does not supersede PM-20260824-e77b21f0 -- extends it. That finding's core gap claim (cross-system transplant-and-ablate-and-route, as a full conjunction) still holds; this pass narrows and sharpens it.

RESOLVED: the OpenReview paper 'Memory Transplants for LLM Agents...' (id AIJsjIqfsp), previously the single biggest unresolved risk, is now confirmed (via ICLR's own first-party site, OpenReview.net itself still unreachable after 8 total attempts) to be an ICLR 2026 MemAgents workshop poster about within-system domain transfer (code-to-math), not cross-system mechanism grafting. Low threat, cite defensively only.

NEW CLOSEST PRIOR ART for the interaction-grid claim specifically: 'Memory in the LLM Era: Modular Architectures and Strategies in a Unified Framework' (arXiv 2604.01707, code at github.com/Yanchen398/Memory-in-the-LLM-Era). Its Table 8 (BASE=MemoryOS=37.36, +Tree=41.15, +SP=39.01, +Tree+SP=43.40) is the closest thing found anywhere to AAMR's proposed BASE/+A/+B/+A+B measurement, limited only by BASE being a donor system rather than a neutral harness, and by the interaction never being named or computed by the paper's own authors.

NEW: for the just-completed arena-context-ablation-v1 experiment specifically (not covered by the original positioning report), TierMem (arXiv 2602.17913, built on Mem0, learned RL router) and Eywa (arXiv 2605.30771, fixed-rule raw-episode rescue) are close published architectural neighbors that CONTEXT_AND_PROVENANCE_ABLATION_V1.md does not yet cite. Separately and independently of this literature search, that experiment's own real result already dropped RAW_PROVENANCE_EXPANSION (0/9 repairs) -- an empirical finding, not a literature one.

DIRECTION UNCHANGED: still GO. No claim was fully falsified across ~113 queries and 3 recovered background-agent interruptions. Recommended: tighten the positioning report's wording on the interaction-grid step to explicitly differentiate from Memory-in-the-LLM-Era and AutoMEM rather than asserting the step is unoccupied in general.
summary: Adversarial search (~113 queries, 5 tracks) targeting the remaining novelty claim from PM-20260824-e77b21f0 found no full falsification. The BASE/+A/+B/+A+B interaction-grid piece is weaker than stated: AutoMEM (2606.04315) has cleaner isolated BASE+A/BASE+B than previously credited, and a newly-found paper, 'Memory in the LLM Era' (arXiv 2604.01707, public code), contains ablation-table data arithmetically equivalent to a full 4-cell grid across two independently-built donor systems with computable mild positive synergy -- uncomputed and unframed as such by its own authors. The router-after-validation-of-cross-system-mechanisms claim (Type D) survives: FluxMem (2602.14038) does the identical validate-then-route sequencing but only over self-designed structures, not transplanted mechanisms. Full report: docs/research/RELATED_WORK_RED_TEAM_2026-08-24.md; append-only update on docs/research/RELATED_WORK_AND_POSITIONING_2026-08-24.md.
title: Red-team pass: novelty claim narrows further but survives; new closest threat identified (Memory in the LLM Era)

arena-mem0-breadth-ablation-v1 follow-up: HINDSIGHT_INFORMATION_COMPOSITION_ARCHAEOLOGY_V1, diagnosis-only, 0 USD new spend. Re-verified frozen scores (Mem0 5/6/6/5, Hindsight 5/6/6/7) from artifacts. Built a per-probe comparison matrix for all 10 units (Mem0-3000 vs Hindsight-full): 2 HINDSIGHT_CORRECT_MEM0_WRONG, 5 BOTH_CORRECT, 3 BOTH_WRONG, 0 MEM0_CORRECT_HINDSIGHT_WRONG. In both group-A probes Mem0's gold_rank is 1 vs Hindsight's 5 -- ruling out "better retrieval rank" as the explanation before any content reading began.

Close read plus anti-storytelling controls (group C as negative controls) identified two code-verified, non-post-hoc candidate mechanisms: (1) TEMPORAL_GROUNDING_AT_EXTRACTION -- Hindsight's fact_extraction.py requires a "when"/"who" field appended as "| When: X | Involving: Y" at write time; Mem0's extraction prompt already asks to preserve dates but main.py never threads a real timestamp into it, so _resolve_dates() silently defaults to ingestion wall-clock time and OSS add() explicitly refuses an external timestamp argument -- a plumbing gap upstream of an already-existing instruction, not a missing one. (2) REDUNDANT_RAW_FACT_ACCUMULATION -- Hindsight has no similarity check on the raw-fact write path and its consolidation dedup never removes originals from recall; Mem0 suppresses near-duplicates at extraction time by design. Candidate 2 failed the anti-storytelling sharp-correlation check (present in a BOTH_WRONG control without helping) and the "small enough for BASE+X" / "not just more tokens" transplant gates.

FIRST_TRANSPLANT_CANDIDATE: TEMPORAL_GROUNDING_AT_EXTRACTION -- passes all 7 gates (observable data diff, code coverage, no gold needed, isolable, falsifiable prediction, small enough for BASE vs BASE+X, not just more tokens). Minimal transplant: thread the real historical message timestamp through Mem0's add() call chain into generate_additive_extraction_prompt()'s current_date/observation_date, instead of the current silent datetime.now() default. Prediction: should specifically help multi-fact temporal-ordering questions where Mem0 already retrieves the right facts but strips their dates (gpt4_f420262c-shaped); should NOT help probes where the needed fact is absent from Mem0's retrieved context entirely (ba358f49, 69fee5aa-shaped).

No BASE+X implemented. No system changed. Full structured data in data/lab/arena/hindsight-archaeology-v1/information-composition-v1.json and docs/research/HINDSIGHT_INFORMATION_COMPOSITION_ARCHAEOLOGY_V1.md.

Per-probe audit of the 2 probes where Hindsight beats clean Mem0 at matched widest budgets found the cause is not retrieval rank (Mem0 gold_rank=1 in both, Hindsight's is 5) but write-time information loss: Hindsight requires a When/Involving field per fact; Mem0's extraction prompt already asks to preserve dates but is never given a real timestamp to ground on (OSS add() rejects one; _resolve_dates() silently defaults to ingestion wall-clock time). FIRST_TRANSPLANT_CANDIDATE: TEMPORAL_GROUNDING_AT_EXTRACTION, passes all 7 transplant gates. A second candidate (Hindsight's lack of raw-fact dedup) was found and code-verified but failed the anti-storytelling and small-transplant gates.
title: Hindsight archaeology v1: temporal grounding at extraction is the first transplant candidate, not breadth

See PM-20260824-d07d2a4b for the full candidate ranking and the next proposed experiment.

body:
Top 5 testable hypotheses ranked (full detail in the report): (1) GRAVITY-derived event/temporal anchors on Mem0, retargeted at AAMR's own temporal-reasoning weakness rather than GRAVITY's own best-average component (entity anchors, which likely has less headroom since Mem0 already has an entity store); (2) query-conditioned reranking of Mem0's own already-retrieved items -- convergent evidence from GRAVITY (removing reranking was its single largest ablation effect, bigger than removing any anchor type) and 'Diagnosing Retrieval vs Utilization Bottlenecks' (retrieval-method choice swings accuracy 20pp vs write-strategy's 3-8pp); (3) Mem0 breadth expansion at k=50/150; (4) a context-sufficiency gate before attempting any expansion, motivated by the absence-vs-under-detail reconciliation; (5) a bounded second-hop provenance search, since TierMem's own escalation does warm-start-then-multi-hop while AAMR's already-dropped test was single-hop only.

PRIORITY DECISION: #3 (Mem0 breadth expansion, k=50/150) is the recommended next mechanism to test, chosen on evidence strength/portability/mechanistic clarity/cheap falsifiability/relevance to AAMR's own failures -- explicitly not on novelty. It is not drawn from the literature at all; it is the other half of an experiment AAMR already ran (the Hindsight breadth curve), already estimated at ~/usr/bin/bash.05 in CONTEXT_AND_PROVENANCE_ABLATION_V1.md, and independently reinforced by TierMem's per-category data showing the same categories (multi-session-adjacent, temporal-reasoning) have the largest summary-to-raw gaps.

Also produced: 4 falsifiable hypotheses reconciling the TierMem/AAMR tension (absence-vs-under-detail; raw-volume-threshold; multi-hop-access; category-alignment) -- none require reversing the existing RAW_PROVENANCE_EXPANSION DROP decision, they narrow when it might still matter. A router-signal feature table found retrieval-confidence and score-margin are notably absent from every routing system checked (FluxMem, MemRouter, Eywa, TierMem) -- either a real gap or a quietly-negative unpublished result, worth a cheap direct check before building anything elaborate.
summary: Deep synthesis over already-verified papers (GRAVITY, Memory-in-the-LLM-Era, TierMem, FluxMem, and others) built a mechanism x regime dependency map and reconciled the TierMem-vs-AAMR raw-context tension with a concrete differentiating variable: TierMem's own error taxonomy is 41.3% gold-absent vs 28.8% under-detailed, the opposite starting condition from AAMR's Mem0 (gold typically present at rank 1) -- explaining why AAMR's raw-provenance test found zero repairs while TierMem's raw context helps substantially. Full report: docs/research/MECHANISM_DEPENDENCY_SYNTHESIS_2026-08-24.md.
title: Dependency synthesis: Mem0 breadth expansion (k=50/150) is the best-evidenced next , not a literature-derived mechanism

body:
Top 5 testable hypotheses ranked (full detail in the report): (1) GRAVITY-derived event/temporal anchors on Mem0, retargeted at AAMR's own temporal-reasoning weakness rather than GRAVITY's own best-average component (entity anchors, which likely has less headroom since Mem0 already has an entity store); (2) query-conditioned reranking of Mem0's own already-retrieved items -- convergent evidence from GRAVITY (removing reranking was its single largest ablation effect, bigger than removing any anchor type) and 'Diagnosing Retrieval vs Utilization Bottlenecks' (retrieval-method choice swings accuracy 20pp vs write-strategy's 3-8pp); (3) Mem0 breadth expansion at k=50/150; (4) a context-sufficiency gate before attempting any expansion, motivated by the absence-vs-under-detail reconciliation; (5) a bounded second-hop provenance search, since TierMem's own escalation does warm-start-then-multi-hop while AAMR's already-dropped test was single-hop only.

PRIORITY DECISION: #3 (Mem0 breadth expansion, k=50/150) is the recommended next mechanism to test, chosen on evidence strength/portability/mechanistic clarity/cheap falsifiability/relevance to AAMR's own failures -- explicitly not on novelty. It is not drawn from the literature at all; it is the other half of an experiment AAMR already ran (the Hindsight breadth curve), already estimated at roughly five cents in CONTEXT_AND_PROVENANCE_ABLATION_V1.md, and independently reinforced by TierMem's per-category data showing the same categories (multi-session-adjacent, temporal-reasoning) have the largest summary-to-raw gaps.

Also produced: 4 falsifiable hypotheses reconciling the TierMem/AAMR tension (absence-vs-under-detail; raw-volume-threshold; multi-hop-access; category-alignment) -- none require reversing the existing RAW_PROVENANCE_EXPANSION DROP decision, they narrow when it might still matter. A router-signal feature table found retrieval-confidence and score-margin are notably absent from every routing system checked (FluxMem, MemRouter, Eywa, TierMem) -- either a real gap or a quietly-negative unpublished result, worth a cheap direct check before building anything elaborate.
summary: Deep synthesis over already-verified papers (GRAVITY, Memory-in-the-LLM-Era, TierMem, FluxMem, and others) built a mechanism x regime dependency map and reconciled the TierMem-vs-AAMR raw-context tension with a concrete differentiating variable: TierMem's own error taxonomy is 41.3% gold-absent vs 28.8% under-detailed, the opposite starting condition from AAMR's Mem0 (gold typically present at rank 1) -- explaining why AAMR's raw-provenance test found zero repairs while TierMem's raw context helps substantially. Full report: docs/research/MECHANISM_DEPENDENCY_SYNTHESIS_2026-08-24.md.

No change to the underlying finding -- text only.

body:
arena-mem0-base-plus-x-v1 calibration result: STOP, do not run the 10-unit experiment.

Corrected an earlier code-citation error: the archaeology finding (PM-20260824-d07d2a4b / PM-20260824-bc15991a) cited source from external/repos/mem0ai__mem0 (an unreleased/HEAD checkout), not the actually-running pinned mem0ai==1.0.6 installed in external/venvs/mem0. Re-verified against the real 1.0.6 source: USER_MEMORY_EXTRACTION_PROMPT is a module-level f-string, "Today's date is {datetime.now():%Y-%m-%d}.", evaluated once at process import -- empirically confirmed unpatched value "Today's date is 2026-08-24" while ingesting a 2022/2023 corpus.

Implemented and reproducibly documented a narrow, named treatment, PER_SESSION_REFERENCE_DATE_AT_EXTRACTION (deliberately not called full Hindsight temporal grounding): (a) get_fact_retrieval_messages() gained an optional reference_date parameter that substitutes into the hardcoded date line; reference_date=None is verified byte-identical to the original unpatched prompt. (b) _add_to_vector_store() threads metadata["timestamp"] -- already computed correctly per-session by the arena's own Mem0Adapter.ingest(), just never used for this -- into that parameter. Exactly these two changes, confirmed by direct diff against a checked-in original 1.0.6 snapshot. Full provenance (pinned version, original/patched SHA256 of both files, unified diff, description) in data/lab/arena/base-plus-x-v1/vendor-patch/manifest.json, independent of the gitignored venv. 5 no-LLM-call prompt-construction tests added and passing (tests/test_mem0_per_session_reference_date_patch.py).

ONE calibration case run under a $0.02 hard cap (actual cost $0.001584, 4 calls): same synthetic input ("...JetBlue from San Francisco to Boston today...") ingested as BASE (reference_date=None) and TREATMENT (reference_date=2022-11-17) into isolated banks. Result: the extracted fact text is BYTE-IDENTICAL between BASE and TREATMENT -- "Took a red-eye flight on JetBlue from San Francisco to Boston today" in both arms. The relative word "today" is preserved verbatim in both, NOT resolved to an absolute date, despite the TREATMENT prompt correctly stating "Today's date is 2022-11-17."

Root cause, read directly off the real 1.0.6 prompt text: USER_MEMORY_EXTRACTION_PROMPT states the current date as a bare contextual fact but contains NO instruction telling the model to use it to resolve relative time expressions when writing extracted facts. Its own few-shot examples demonstrate the opposite: "Yesterday, I had a meeting..." -> ["Had a meeting with John at 3pm..."], with "Yesterday" simply dropped, never converted to an absolute date. The patch supplies a correct anchor; it does not supply an instruction to use it.

STOP per explicit instruction: the model does not use the correct date when only a correct reference_date is supplied. The 10-unit BASE+X experiment is NOT run. Any further attempt (e.g. adding an explicit "resolve relative time expressions using today's date" instruction to the prompt) would be a THIRD change beyond the two authorized here and needs separate approval -- not attempted in this phase.

Secondary, minor finding: the calibration script itself had a cap_scope/run_id prefix mismatch (run_id did not start with cap_scope), so its own live cost display read $0.0000 against a real $0.001584 spent. The $0.02 cap was still actively enforced throughout by the provider proxy's separate, in-process cap (ProxyState.spent_usd/check(), independent of ledger cap_scope matching) -- no overspend risk existed, only a reporting bug, since fixed in the script for future reuse.

Full result: data/lab/arena/base-plus-x-v1/calibration-per-session-reference-date.json.
summary: One /usr/bin/bash.02-capped calibration call (actual /usr/bin/bash.001584) shows the model does NOT use a corrected session reference date to resolve relative-time expressions: BASE and TREATMENT extract byte-identical fact text ('...today', unresolved) despite TREATMENT's prompt correctly stating the real date. Root cause: the pinned mem0ai==1.0.6 prompt states today's date as a bare fact with no instruction to use it for resolving relative time in extracted facts -- its own few-shot examples demonstrate dropping 'Yesterday' rather than converting it. STOP per explicit instruction: the 10-unit BASE+X experiment is not run.
title: Calibration STOP: PER_SESSION_REFERENCE_DATE_AT_EXTRACTION does not change what Mem0 extracts
