body:
arena-mem0-breadth-ablation-v1 follow-up: HINDSIGHT_INFORMATION_COMPOSITION_ARCHAEOLOGY_V1, diagnosis-only, 0 USD new spend. Re-verified frozen scores (Mem0 5/6/6/5, Hindsight 5/6/6/7) from artifacts. Built a per-probe comparison matrix for all 10 units (Mem0-3000 vs Hindsight-full): 2 HINDSIGHT_CORRECT_MEM0_WRONG, 5 BOTH_CORRECT, 3 BOTH_WRONG, 0 MEM0_CORRECT_HINDSIGHT_WRONG. In both group-A probes Mem0's gold_rank is 1 vs Hindsight's 5 -- ruling out "better retrieval rank" as the explanation before any content reading began.

Close read plus anti-storytelling controls (group C as negative controls) identified two code-verified, non-post-hoc candidate mechanisms: (1) TEMPORAL_GROUNDING_AT_EXTRACTION -- Hindsight's fact_extraction.py requires a "when"/"who" field appended as "| When: X | Involving: Y" at write time; Mem0's extraction prompt already asks to preserve dates but main.py never threads a real timestamp into it, so _resolve_dates() silently defaults to ingestion wall-clock time and OSS add() explicitly refuses an external timestamp argument -- a plumbing gap upstream of an already-existing instruction, not a missing one. (2) REDUNDANT_RAW_FACT_ACCUMULATION -- Hindsight has no similarity check on the raw-fact write path and its consolidation dedup never removes originals from recall; Mem0 suppresses near-duplicates at extraction time by design. Candidate 2 failed the anti-storytelling sharp-correlation check (present in a BOTH_WRONG control without helping) and the "small enough for BASE+X" / "not just more tokens" transplant gates.

FIRST_TRANSPLANT_CANDIDATE: TEMPORAL_GROUNDING_AT_EXTRACTION -- passes all 7 gates (observable data diff, code coverage, no gold needed, isolable, falsifiable prediction, small enough for BASE vs BASE+X, not just more tokens). Minimal transplant: thread the real historical message timestamp through Mem0's add() call chain into generate_additive_extraction_prompt()'s current_date/observation_date, instead of the current silent datetime.now() default. Prediction: should specifically help multi-fact temporal-ordering questions where Mem0 already retrieves the right facts but strips their dates (gpt4_f420262c-shaped); should NOT help probes where the needed fact is absent from Mem0's retrieved context entirely (ba358f49, 69fee5aa-shaped).

No BASE+X implemented. No system changed. Full structured data in data/lab/arena/hindsight-archaeology-v1/information-composition-v1.json and docs/research/HINDSIGHT_INFORMATION_COMPOSITION_ARCHAEOLOGY_V1.md.

Re-verified against the correct source: the date-grounding gap is real and, if anything, more precise -- a module-level prompt f-string frozen at process-import time, confirmed empirically to read the real 2026 wall-clock date while ingesting 2022/2023 content. Corrected citations, causal diagnosis unchanged. See PM-20260824-c76d8a96 for what happened when this was calibrated.

  SECONDARY/BOUNDARY:  ba358f49       -- predicted possible flip at native and/or wide; needs the age fact ("Is 32 years old") correctly time-anchored AND correctly attributed to the user, so a clean flip here plausibly needs +SRC or +BOTH, not +TIME alone -- a +TIME-only non-flip on this unit is not by itself a mechanism failure.
  SECONDARY/BOUNDARY:  gpt4_f49edff3  -- predicted possible flip ONLY at wide (already correct at native, so native is regression-watch for this unit, not a flip target). A non-flip at wide is explicitly uninformative against the mechanism (Hindsight itself recovered only 2 of 3 needed dates here and still failed), not a falsification signal.

PREDICTED NON-EFFECT (must remain wrong at both operating points):
  69fee5aa       -- the corrected value was never captured by either system; no date can conjure information that was never stored.
  gpt4_59c863d7  -- a scattered-counting/enumeration failure, not a temporal-composition failure; +TIME is not expected to touch it.

REGRESSION WATCH (must not flip correct -> wrong; per operating point, since correctness differs between them):
  at native: gpt4_98f46fc6, 58bf7951, gpt4_f49edff3, eace081b, 311778f1
  at wide:   gpt4_98f46fc6, 58bf7951, 6a27ffc2, eace081b, 311778f1
  Any regression on any of these units, in the arm/operating-point where it is currently correct, triggers the stop-and-analyze-transcript rule before any further arm runs (per instruction).

PRIMARY METRIC (declared before running): PREDICTED_FLIPS_NET_OF_REGRESSIONS, per arm, per operating point. A flip outside this registered set is not counted as mechanism success, regardless of direction.

This registration will not be edited after treatment answers are read. Any post-hoc observation about an unregistered unit will be reported separately and explicitly labeled as such.

body:
E1 (arena-base-plus-x-v2), read-side temporal anchoring micro-grid, run per pre-registered predictions (PM-20260824-d4155074). Combined new spend with E3: $0.091839 of a $0.20 hard cap.

TEMPORAL_ANCHOR_AT_CONTEXT (+TIME, rendering each already-retrieved Mem0 fact as "[YYYY-MM-DD] {fact}" using its positionally-aligned evidence_times, no new ingest/retrieval): native 5/10 -> 7/10, wide 5/10 -> 8/10. Every pre-registered predicted flip target flipped: PRIMARY gpt4_f420262c at both operating points; SECONDARY/boundary ba358f49 at both; SECONDARY/boundary gpt4_f49edff3 at wide (its only eligible point). Zero regressions on +TIME at either point. Predicted non-effect units (69fee5aa, gpt4_59c863d7) stayed put under +TIME exactly as predicted. Transcript-level: the reader explicitly cites the rendered anchor dates when reordering gpt4_f420262c's answer (e.g. "JetBlue (..., around November 17, 2022)... United Airlines (..., around January 28, 2023)... American Airlines (..., on February 10, 2023)"), direct evidence of mechanism use, not coincidental relabeling.

SOURCE_TAG_AT_CONTEXT (+SRC, "(source: user's message) {fact}", uniform since every item in this store originates from a user-role turn): net negative on this sample -- 0 predicted flips, 1 regression at each operating point (native: gpt4_f49edff3; wide: gpt4_98f46fc6). Both regressions transcript-explained: the source annotation makes the reader more cautious, converting a BASE answer that guessed an ordering from a weak cue (list order, "today"/"tonight" phrasing) and happened to match gold into an explicit "cannot be determined" abstention, which the binary judge scores wrong on an answerable question. Not an unexplained/anomalous regression.

+BOTH (gated on +TIME's clean predicted flips): native 6/10 (+1 predicted net), wide 7/10 (+2 predicted net), zero regressions at either point.

+PLACEBO (gated on +TIME's predicted flip; "[item-NNN]" neutral tags, token-matched to +TIME): native 5/10, zero effect. Wide 7/10: flips ba358f49 (a predicted target) AND gpt4_59c863d7 (explicitly predicted as a NON-effect unit -- an unexpected flip not credited to any mechanism). This is an honest, stated caveat: at wide, part of the gain is a general per-item-boundary-clarity effect shared by a content-free tag, not unique to temporal information. +TIME still nets 2 more predicted flips than +PLACEBO at wide (gpt4_f420262c, gpt4_f49edff3, neither touched by placebo), and at native the entire +TIME effect is placebo-free (placebo: zero change there).

VERDICT: TEMPORAL_ANCHOR_SUPPORTED. Meets all three stated criteria (>=1 pre-registered predicted flip -- exceeded; no unexplained regression -- +SRC's are transcript-explained; transcript behavior consistent with anchor use -- directly confirmed). The wide-operating-point placebo overlap is carried forward as an explicit magnitude caveat, not hidden.

Full data: data/lab/arena/base-plus-x-v2/e1-analysis.json. Report: docs/research/READ_SIDE_TEMPORAL_ANCHOR_V1.md.
summary: Read-side temporal anchoring (rendering already-persisted session dates next to already-retrieved Mem0 facts, no new ingest/retrieval): native 5/10->7/10, wide 5/10->8/10, all 3 pre-registered flip targets hit, zero regressions, transcript directly shows the reader citing rendered dates to reorder correctly. SOURCE_TAG_AT_CONTEXT alone was net negative (explained: induces cautious abstention). Wide-point gain partially overlaps a token-matched placebo effect (stated explicitly, not hidden) but +TIME still exceeds it by 2 predicted flips there and is placebo-free at native. First validated AAMR transplant candidate.
title: E1 verdict: TEMPORAL_ANCHOR_SUPPORTED -- every pre-registered flip landed, transcript confirms anchor use

body:
E3 (arena-provenance-clean-v2), clean raw-provenance retest, run alongside E1. Combined new spend: $0.091839 of the same $0.20 hard cap (E3 portion: $0.018390).

This SUPERSEDES the "RAW_PROVENANCE_EXPANSION -> DROP, zero repairs" conclusion in docs/research/CONTEXT_AND_PROVENANCE_ABLATION_V1.md (Experiment B) and everywhere it propagated (MECHANISM_DEPENDENCY_SYNTHESIS_2026-08-24.md, RESEARCH_ROADMAP_EVIDENCE_DRIVEN_V1.md's invalidation table). That conclusion was computed entirely against cross-unit-contaminated Mem0 data and is not valid evidence; no clean provenance test existed before this one.

Method: no new Mem0 ingest, no Hindsight calls. COMPACT+RAW and RAW-ONLY arms built via arena.mechanism_ablation.build_arms(), called fresh -- verified this session that the underlying raw/arena-expansion-v1/mem0.json now holds the clean run's data (0/18 mismatches against the frozen mem0_original arm, checked before spending). Deterministic session-date-only provenance mapping, no semantic/gold-aware matching. 9/10 units observable; 69fee5aa UNOBSERVABLE (haystack dates don't uniquely identify a session -- consistent with every other diagnostic pass on this unit this whole session).

Scores (9 observable units): compact 5/9, compact+raw 6/9, raw-only 4/9. COMPACT_WRONG_RAW_FIXES: [6a27ffc2], 1 unit. RAW_CAUSES_REGRESSION: [], zero.

The one repair, examined rather than assumed a content-absence win: 6a27ffc2 ("how many Corey Schafer Python videos completed", gold 30). Compact answered "20" (a stale count also present in Mem0's own context alongside the updated "30"); compact+raw answered "30" correctly. Gold was ALREADY present at rank 1 in compact for this unit (as it was for ALL 4 of the 9 observable units' compact failures -- GOLD_OR_GOLD_ADJACENT_PRESENT_IN_COMPACT 4/4, ABSENT_FROM_COMPACT 0/4). So this is not an absence-regime repair; it is raw text disambiguating between two competing facts already extracted into compact. The pre-registered H1 (absence-vs-under-detail) framing does not cleanly apply -- there was no absence-regime failure in this sample to test it against.

Category breakdown of the 4 compact failures: temporal-reasoning 1 (gpt4_f420262c, not repaired, as predicted -- its dates are scattered across 4 sessions, top-1 provenance reaches only one); multi-session 2 (ba358f49, gpt4_59c863d7, neither repaired); knowledge-update 1 (6a27ffc2, repaired). No single-session/other failures in this set.

Specifically flagged units: ba358f49 -- compact/compact+raw/raw-only all WRONG, not repaired (contrast with E1, where this same unit DOES flip correct under +TIME and +BOTH -- its fix is temporal anchoring, not raw provenance). 69fee5aa -- UNOBSERVABLE, untestable. gpt4_f420262c -- not repaired, as predicted; does not weigh against its own +TIME success in E1, different mechanisms.

VERDICT: RAW_PROVENANCE_CONDITIONAL_SIGNAL, with an explicit correction to what it signals: not a strong revival (1/9, via disambiguation not absence-filling), and not a restoration of the old DROP (now confirmed unsupported on the correct clean-data grounds, which is itself the more important methodological result of this retest).

Full data: data/lab/arena/base-plus-x-v2/e3-analysis.json. Report: docs/research/CLEAN_RAW_PROVENANCE_RETEST_V2.md.
summary: Clean raw-provenance retest (no new ingest, no Hindsight): compact 5/9, compact+raw 6/9, raw-only 4/9. 1 repair (6a27ffc2), 0 regressions. The repair disambiguates competing facts already in compact (gold was rank-1 present in compact for all 4 failures) rather than filling a content gap, so it does not cleanly confirm the absence-vs-under-detail (H1) framing. Supersedes CONTEXT_AND_PROVENANCE_ABLATION_V1.md's contaminated-data DROP conclusion, which was never valid evidence.
title: E3 verdict: RAW_PROVENANCE_CONDITIONAL_SIGNAL on clean data -- supersedes the invalidated DROP conclusion

body:
StateMemBench claims verified and corrected: the plus-32-to-67-point wrapper gain and the plus-15-to-32-point structure-attribution are NOT independent facts -- the second is a nested subset of the first. The 44.4 percent state-drift figure carries a Wilson 95 percent CI of 30 to 60 (n=36, one backbone). The transplantable unit is the read-only wrapper (Trace then Resolve), not the full write-path method.

Most consequential single external finding: 'When Memory Becomes Authority' (arXiv 2608.01679) found authority collapse (consolidation preserves content, silently drops source-scope constraints) in 48 of 49 tested consolidator-times-backbone configurations. Not actionable against AAMR's current arena (no consolidation mechanism exists yet; Tree/SP explicitly off the candidate board), but AAMR's own project-memory schema already carries the kind of typed provenance fields (claim_class, source_refs, bitemporal) this paper's fix retrofits elsewhere -- flagged as a design principle for whenever AAMR builds a consolidation step, not a near-term action.

Second most consequential: the deterministic-freshness-beats-LLM-conflict-resolution finding (arXiv 2606.01435, roughly 20-point gap on MemoryAgentBench FactConsolidation) was independently triangulated by four separate research passes today -- the single most-replicated finding across the whole sweep -- and converges with AAMR's own already-logged Mem0 date-extraction defect via an independent benchmark (HaluMem, arXiv 2511.03506: Mem0 scores only 25.50 percent correct / 74.02 percent omission at the memory-updating stage specifically).

Two new, free-to-cheap diagnostic hypotheses were proposed against AAMR's own frozen data, neither previously in the candidate board: a zero-answer-dispersion check (resample the reader at temperature greater than zero on the two known group-A failures to test whether they are 'coherent lock-in' or reasoning noise, motivated by arXiv 2606.22728's finding that 42 to 59 percent of RAG errors show zero answer dispersion) and a harmful-sibling/distraction re-read of the unexplained 'Spirit' airline appearing in Mem0's wrong answer on gpt4_f420262c (motivated by arXiv 2606.10388's harmful-sibling-rate metric from the skill-retrieval literature). Both cost zero or near-zero and were recommended as free additions alongside the already-planned E1/E3, not replacements.

DECISION: the roadmap's E1/E2/E3 sequence (read-side temporal anchoring first) stands unchanged. No external mechanism family found stronger evidence, better fit to AAMR's own measured failures, lower cost, or a more concrete unlocked decision than E1 already has.
summary: A 9-agent frontier-mapping pass (not a novelty search) covering the whole LLM-agent-memory field, triggered by StateMemBench (arXiv 2608.19652), found roughly 150 papers/systems and produced a Top-10 mechanism-family map plus a curated negative-results catalog. Cross-referenced against the current (post-contamination-fix) roadmap in RESEARCH_ROADMAP_EVIDENCE_DRIVEN_V1.md: no external finding clears the bar to jump ahead of E1 (read-side temporal anchoring). Five cross-paper hypotheses were produced, four of which fold into currently-planned stages at near-zero marginal cost, one (authority-collapse-safe consolidation) explicitly deferred as future-scale. Mix 5 TEMPORAL_POSITIVE + 2 TEMPORAL_BOUNDARY + 3 NON_TEMPORAL_CONTROL (70/30). Predictions registered in PM-20260824-eb86fcf3 before any ingest.

Bug caught and fixed before further spend: the first contamination-audit pass flagged 2 units (0977f2af, 0bb5a684) as contamination failures. Root cause: both units' own haystack_dates are non-unique, so session_map() correctly returns None and gold_state() takes the UNOBSERVABLE branch, which carries no foreign_from_other_units key; comparing that missing key against ==0 read as failure. Not a real contamination signal -- same condition as 69fee5aa in the original 10-unit set. Fixed per the bug-discipline protocol (regression tests added and confirmed against the fix, contamination_status() extracted as a named PASS/FAIL/UNOBSERVABLE function) before proceeding to any paid reader/judge call.

Ingest: 10/10 complete, reset postcondition (before==after==0) holds for every unit, contamination audit clean (2 legitimately UNOBSERVABLE, not failures). Cost $0.715117.

Results: BASE 7/10, +TIME 6/10, DELTA -1. Zero flips within the pre-registered TEMPORAL_POSITIVE bucket. Two flips to correct landed in TEMPORAL_BOUNDARY instead (08f4fc43: reader explicitly cites both rendered dates and computes a 30-day gap matching gold; 0bc8ad92: reader cites the rendered date and a context-stated current date, computes ~4 months against a gold of 5, forgiven by the frozen judge's own explicit off-by-one duration tolerance -- a real pass, not noise). Three regressions: 031748ae (TEMPORAL_POSITIVE) -- the reader correctly notices a 5-month gap between two facts' anchors and hedges rather than assuming BASE's lucky guess, a more careful answer the binary judge penalizes; 0977f2af (TEMPORAL_POSITIVE) -- both arms are near-identical honest abstentions that both name the gold entity, flip reads as judge phrasing-sensitivity, TEMPORAL_INFORMATION_USED=NO for both, not a mechanism effect; 00ca467f (NON_TEMPORAL_CONTROL, predicted no effect) -- the clearest genuine negative-transfer case: two March medical facts share one later session anchor while their event dates are named inside the fact text (March 3rd, March 20th); +TIME renders only the session-recording date, and the reader undercounts, dropping the March 3rd item. This is exactly the boundary condition the session-timestamp-vs-resolved-event-date distinction predicts.

NET_PREDICTED_REPAIRS = 0 - 3 = -3. Both verdict trigger conditions hold independently: regressions >= repairs, and the observed effect does not match the pre-registered regime.

Per the required interpretation discipline: this is NOT "temporal grounding does not work." It is "session-timestamp anchoring at context assembly did not replicate under this Stage-2 regime" -- specifically landing its real effects in TEMPORAL_BOUNDARY rather than TEMPORAL_POSITIVE, and showing one concrete, mechanistically-explained negative-transfer mode (session anchor diverging from in-text event date) worth carrying into any future design of this mechanism, though not investigated further in this phase. Resolved-event-date / write-side grounding (C3/E2) remains a separate, untested hypothesis, neither weakened nor strengthened by this result.

VERDICT: TEMPORAL_ANCHOR_FAILED_REPLICATION. REPLICATED_VALIDATED_TRANSPLANT for Mechanism A: NO. E1 (PM-20260824-2d603195) stands, not retracted, not superseded -- a valid single-sample signal that did not clear the Stage 2 replication bar.

body:
Per-unit archaeology (all 10 Stage 2 units) read directly from frozen data/lab/arena/stage2-fresh-replication/*.json, no new calls. Session-vs-event-time finding: alignment status alone does not predict direction. 00ca467f (session-event DIVERGENT, many-item filter/count over a repeated shared session tag) regresses -- reader drops a real, correct fact (March 3rd appointment) after the session anchor competes with an in-text date on a filter/count task. 08f4fc43 (also session-event DIVERGENT, structurally similar shared-anchor-plus-differing-in-text-dates) repairs instead -- because it is a bounded two-item lookup where each fact's own in-text date resolves the arithmetic regardless of the anchor. Working distinction: task type (bounded lookup/arithmetic vs many-item filter/count with a repeated tag), not divergence alone.

H5 harmful-sibling/distraction: primary case is E1's gpt4_f420262c ("Spirit" wrong answer) -- confirmed TRACEABLE_DISTRACTOR, two real Spirit Airlines items at close rank (5, 12) to the relevant flight cluster (0,2,3,7,9), correct answer (Delta) requires a harder multi-hop link. Same check applied to all 5 Stage 2 repair/regression cases: 0 of 5 show this pattern. Stage 2's changes are hedges/omissions/same-entity-date-conflicts, not sibling substitution. One case (0bc8ad92) shows a real near-miss distractor ("with dad" vs gold "with a friend") correctly avoided under +TIME -- a useful negative control. HARMFUL_SIBLING_DISTRACTION status: OBSERVED_CASE, explicitly not promoted to a general failure mode on one example.

Competing explanations (H0-H5_LOCAL, full evidence-for/against in the report): H0 (noise) WEAK, explains 1-2 of 5 events not the 2 content-level cases. H1 (session time helps when good event-time proxy) SUPPORTED but incomplete. H2 (session time hurts on divergence) SUPPORTED for one instance, directly contradicted in simple form by a structurally near-identical repair case -- WEAK as a general rule. H3_LOCAL (prefix exposes harmful sibling) DISFAVORED, 0/5. H4 (sample composition explains E1 vs Stage2 gap) SUPPORTED -- E1's win pattern (multi-fact ordering, session anchor as only signal) did not recur in Stage 2's gold-blind TEMPORAL_POSITIVE bucket; Stage 2's real wins landed in the structurally different TEMPORAL_BOUNDARY bucket. H5_LOCAL (E1 was small-n noise) PARTIALLY SUPPORTED, overlaps with H4 -- not that the effect is illusory (it's mechanistically confirmed twice, independently, in Stage 2), but that E1's specific regime composition was small-n and didn't recur.

E1 vs Stage2 reconciliation: REGIME_DEPENDENCE. The mechanism (rendering usable dates aids date-arithmetic) is real and repeatedly transcript-confirmed. The regime prediction that failed to replicate is narrower than believed: not "ordering questions" as a category, but specifically bounded lookups over explicitly-or-well-anchored named events. E1 (PM-20260824-2d603195) stands, NOT retracted, NOT superseded -- QUALIFIED_BY this Stage 2 fresh replication and this archaeology: the mechanism's positive regime is narrower than E1 alone suggested, and a specific negative-transfer regime (session-vs-event divergence on filter/count tasks) is now documented (Ledger Entry B).

3 new hypotheses recorded, none tested: EVENT_TIME_OVER_SESSION_TIME_PRECEDENCE (targets 00ca467f-style negative transfer, ~$0.05-0.10), DISTRACTOR_AWARE_CONTEXT_ASSEMBLY (targets H5-style sibling substitution, ~$0.05), TASK-TYPE-CONDITIONAL TEMPORAL ANCHOR (gates rendering by task type, ~$0.05-0.10).

E2 decision: E2_CALIBRATION_JUSTIFIED -- Stage 2 surfaced a concrete, well-understood failure (session-vs-event divergence in filter/count tasks) that E2's write-side resolved-event-date design would address by construction, sharper motivation than existed pre-Stage-2. This is a rendered decision label only, NOT approval to run E2 or its calibration.

Backlog, not run: ZERO_ANSWER_DISPERSION_DIAGNOSTIC (frontier H2), CHEAP_FOLLOWUP/NOT_RUN, ~$0.01-0.02, trigger = future $0 pass cannot distinguish noise from stable failure. AUTHORITY_COLLAPSE_SAFE_CONSOLIDATION (frontier H3) recorded as Ledger Entry D, EXTERNAL_STRONG_SIGNAL/AAMR_UNTESTED/NOT_ACTIONABLE_YET, future trigger = first AAMR consolidation mechanism design.

Artifacts: docs/research/TEMPORAL_ALIGNMENT_AND_DISTRACTION_ARCHAEOLOGY_V1.md, data/lab/arena/temporal-alignment-and-distraction-archaeology-v1/analysis.json, docs/research/MECHANISM_REGIME_EVIDENCE_LEDGER.md. Zero new API spend confirmed throughout -- no reader, judge, embedding, ingest, or web calls made this turn.

body:
Question: does Mem0 1.0.6 extraction, given a correct per-session reference_date AND an explicit instruction to resolve relative temporal expressions against it, represent EVENT_TIME as an absolute date -- vs. CONTROL (same reference_date, no instruction), which prior calibration (PM under data/lab/arena/base-plus-x-v1/calibration-per-session-reference-date.json) already showed is INERT? Capability calibration only, not a benchmark accuracy test.

Treatment definition: EVENT_TIME_RESOLUTION_AT_EXTRACTION = PER_SESSION_REFERENCE_DATE_AT_EXTRACTION (correct reference_date threaded into "Today's date is ...") PLUS one instruction bullet inserted immediately after that line: resolve relative time expressions (today/yesterday/tomorrow/last month/next year) against the reference date when unambiguous; never fabricate a date otherwise. Implemented as get_fact_retrieval_messages(..., resolve_relative_time=True) in the vendored mem0/memory/utils.py (patch: data/lab/arena/event-time-resolution-calibration-v1/vendor-patch/EVENT_TIME_RESOLUTION_AT_EXTRACTION.patch, manifest with baseline/patched sha256 in the same directory).

Control definition: identical call with resolve_relative_time=False (the default) -- byte-identical prompt to the already-calibrated-INERT PER_SESSION_REFERENCE_DATE_AT_EXTRACTION treatment. Confirmed by tests/test_mem0_event_time_resolution_patch.py::test_control_default_matches_reference_date_only_baseline (no LLM call).

5 case IDs, reference dates, expected resolution:
CASE1_TODAY: reference_date=2022-11-17, input event phrase "today" -> expected absolute event date 2022-11-17, "today" not left as the only temporal anchor.
CASE2_YESTERDAY: reference_date=2023-01-28, input event phrase "yesterday" -> expected absolute event date 2023-01-27.
CASE3_NEXT_YEAR: reference_date=2022-06-15, input event phrase "next year" -> expected year 2023, no day/month forced beyond what input text supports.
CASE4_LAST_MONTH: reference_date=2023-03-10, input event phrase "last month" -> expected February 2023 / 2023-02, no specific day forced.
CASE5_NO_DATE: reference_date=2023-02-10, input contains NO event-time clue -> expected no fabricated event date; reference_date must not be auto-copied into the fact as if it were the event date.

Negative control: CASE5_NO_DATE is the negative control -- success requires FABRICATED_DATE_ON_NONE=NO regardless of what happens on cases 1-4.

Success gate (pre-registered, exact per user spec):
E2_CALIBRATION_PASS iff TREATMENT resolves >=3 of 4 date-bearing cases (1-4) correctly AND CASE5 has zero fabricated event date AND treatment changes extraction in the intended temporal direction relative to CONTROL.
E2_CALIBRATION_PARTIAL iff 2/4 resolved correctly AND no fabricated date, OR behavior is mixed in a mechanistically interesting way.
E2_CALIBRATION_FAIL iff <=1/4 resolved OR fabricates an event date in CASE5 OR instruction does not change extraction behavior at all vs CONTROL.
UNRESOLVED iff provider/harness anomaly prevents interpretation.

Call discipline: CONTROL once + TREATMENT once per case = 10 extraction calls maximum (Mem0 1.0.6's fact-retrieval path is a single model call per add(); confirmed by direct code read of _add_to_vector_store, one get_fact_retrieval_messages() call followed by one llm.generate_response() call, no secondary extraction call). No retries except transport/provider/parse failure, retry reason logged.

Hard cap: $0.03 new spend, enforced via SpendLedger(cap_scope="e2-calib-", ...) plus the provider proxy's independent per-process cap. Cost gate computed and logged before the first paid call (see next project-memory/task entry). If projection > $0.03: STOP, no calls made.

Explicitly NOT approval for: full E2, benchmark ingest, a 10-unit run, a new Stage 2, any Frankenstein/router mechanism, or a second mechanism candidate.
summary: E2_CALIBRATION_PREREGISTRATION: capability calibration of EVENT_TIME_RESOLUTION_AT_EXTRACTION, isolating the explicit temporal-resolution instruction against a correct-reference-date CONTROL. Registered before any paid call. Hard new spend cap $0.03; projected spend ~$0.008 (10 calls at prior calibration's measured ~$0.0008/call).
title: E2_CALIBRATION_PREREGISTRATION: EVENT_TIME_RESOLUTION_AT_EXTRACTION

body:
Relation to failed session-anchor replication (Stage 2, PM-20260824-8dc62d48) and the zero-cost archaeology (PM-20260824-368e6a17): the archaeology found a concrete negative-transfer mode in 00ca467f where a rendered session anchor competes with an in-text explicit event date on a filter/count task, and recommended E2 (write-side resolved event time) as a design that would address this by construction -- rendered as E2_CALIBRATION_JUSTIFIED (a label only, not approval). This calibration tested the simplest possible instantiation of that idea: adding one explicit instruction bullet to the extraction prompt telling the model to resolve relative expressions against the reference date. Result: the instruction is inert.

Exact treatment: EVENT_TIME_RESOLUTION_AT_EXTRACTION = get_fact_retrieval_messages(..., resolve_relative_time=True) in the vendored mem0/memory/utils.py, patch at data/lab/arena/event-time-resolution-calibration-v1/vendor-patch/EVENT_TIME_RESOLUTION_AT_EXTRACTION.patch (baseline sha256 3ca63bed9b8080342a91c74819be41faa92c6f71a03a473c40bfc8eb1f6af0ed, patched sha256 994656285d2b03a31c1826e99e6bbf6564aaf14b6ac5bd127262d8d33da2bae3). Inserts exactly one bullet after "Today's date is X." instructing relative-expression resolution, never fabricating a date. No other prompt, dedup, retrieval, or reader change.

Exact control: same call with resolve_relative_time=False (default) -- byte-identical to the PER_SESSION_REFERENCE_DATE_AT_EXTRACTION baseline, confirmed by a no-LLM-call unit test.

4/4 temporal outcomes: CASE1_TODAY (ref 2022-11-17, expected 2022-11-17) -- "today" preserved verbatim in both arms, no absolute date. CASE2_YESTERDAY (ref 2023-01-28, expected 2023-01-27) -- "yesterday" preserved verbatim. CASE3_NEXT_YEAR (ref 2022-06-15, expected 2023) -- "next year" preserved verbatim. CASE4_LAST_MONTH (ref 2023-03-10, expected 2023-02) -- "last month" preserved verbatim. All 4: TREATMENT_RESOLVED=NO, CONTROL_VS_TREATMENT_TEXT_CHANGED=NO.

No-date outcome: CASE5_NO_DATE (ref 2023-02-10, input has no temporal clue) -- 2 non-temporal facts extracted identically in both arms, FABRICATED_DATE_ON_NONE=NO. Negative control technically passes but is moot given zero effect elsewhere.

Spend: $0.002811 of $0.03 hard cap. 10 calls total (5 cases x 2 arms x 1 extraction-only call each; confirmed by code read that memory.add() itself would make 2 calls per arm -- extraction + update-memory-decision -- but this calibration deliberately bypassed the second call as out of scope, so real call count matched the pre-registered "max 10" exactly).

Verdict: E2_CALIBRATION_FAIL (both independent gate conditions triggered: resolved_count 0/4 <=1/4, AND instruction changed extraction behavior in 0/5 cases).

Whether full E2 becomes eligible: NOT_ELIGIBLE. This closes the specific minimal-instruction design; it does not close the underlying write-side-resolution idea in general (a differently-structured treatment, e.g. a dedicated output field, was not tried and would need separate pre-registration per the "no few-shot tuning after failure" discipline).

Report/json/ledger paths: docs/research/EVENT_TIME_RESOLUTION_CALIBRATION_V1.md, data/lab/arena/event-time-resolution-calibration-v1/calibration.json, docs/research/MECHANISM_REGIME_EVIDENCE_LEDGER.md (Entry E). Does not overwrite or retract PM-20260824-368e6a17's E2_CALIBRATION_JUSTIFIED recommendation label -- that label described why E2 was WORTH calibrating, which happened; this event records that the calibration itself failed.
summary: E2_EVENT_TIME_RESOLUTION_CALIBRATION result: E2_CALIBRATION_FAIL. Isolated test of an explicit temporal-resolution instruction on top of a correct per-session reference_date (already separately calibrated INERT on its own -- PM/data/lab/arena/base-plus-x-v1/calibration-per-session-reference-date.json). CONTROL (reference_date, no instruction) vs TREATMENT (reference_date + instruction): 5 synthetic cases, TODAY/YESTERDAY/NEXT_YEAR/LAST_MONTH/NO_DATE. TREATMENT_RESOLVED=0/4, CONTROL_RESOLVED=0/4, FABRICATED_DATE_ON_NONE=NO, instruction changed extraction text in 0/5 cases (parsed facts byte-identical CONTROL vs TREATMENT in every case). title: E2_EVENT_TIME_RESOLUTION_CALIBRATION: instruction-only treatment is inert (FAIL)

body:
User's assessment after reviewing E2_CALIBRATION_FAIL: this is a good, cheap negative result ($0.002811), not a project failure -- it closes the simple instruction-only write-side design specifically, not the concept of event-time resolution generally. Chain: SESSION_TIME rendering (E1 positive exploratory) -> Stage2 (failed fresh replication) -> zero-cost archaeology (REGIME_DEPENDENCE, session time != event time in specific task shapes) -> EVENT_TIME_RESOLUTION_AT_EXTRACTION via Mem0 prompt instruction -> CALIBRATION FAIL. None of these individually or together license the claim 'temporal grounding works' -- no mechanism in this family has cleared independent replication.

Decision: pause the temporal branch (do not run another temporal-only prompt/experiment next). Move to an independent mechanism family for the next candidate: STATE / SUPERSESSION -- recognizing which of several stored facts about the same slot is current when memory holds a temporal sequence of updates (example given: employer Microsoft -> left Microsoft -> Google; naive retrieval surfaces all three with no resolution of which is current). Distinct mechanism class from context-timestamp rendering; intended as an independent Frankenstein component (BASE / +A / +B / +A+B interaction testing later, once at least one mechanism independently replicates). Partial external motivation cited by the user: StateMem/STALE literature -- not independently verified or researched in this session (no web research performed).

Stated plan for the next turn: a cheap/zero-cost design and candidate-selection pass for State/Supersession, explicitly before running any expensive experiment -- mirroring the calibration-first discipline eventually applied to the temporal branch. This project-memory entry records the STRATEGIC decision only; it is not itself an authorization to start implementation, and no task under this decision has been started.

Does not retract or delete any temporal-branch record: E1 (PM-20260824-2d603195) remains QUALIFIED_BY Stage 2; Stage 2 (PM-20260824-8dc62d48) and the archaeology (PM-20260824-368e6a17) and the E2 calibration (PM-20260824-36f46bed) all stand unmodified.
summary: TEMPORAL_BRANCH_PAUSE: after E1 (positive exploratory), Stage 2 (failed replication), zero-cost archaeology (REGIME_DEPENDENCE), and E2 instruction-only calibration (FAIL, PM-20260824-36f46bed), no mechanism in the TEMPORAL_ANCHOR_AT_CONTEXT / EVENT_TIME_RESOLUTION family has cleared independent replication. The branch is PAUSED, not abandoned or retracted -- E1 stays exploratory-valid (QUALIFIED_BY Stage 2), Stage 2 and the E2 calibration both stand as valid negative/mixed results. Next mechanism candidate selected for a future turn: STATE / SUPERSESSION (recognizing which of several stored facts about the same slot is current, e.g. employer Microsoft -> left Microsoft -> Google), motivated in part by external StateMem/STALE literature (not independently verified this session). Plan: a cheap, low/zero-cost design and selection pass before any expensive experiment, mirroring the temporal branch's eventual calibration-first discipline. This is a strategic/discussion decision, not yet an authorized task -- no experiment has been started.
title: TEMPORAL_BRANCH_PAUSE; next mechanism candidate STATE/SUPERSESSION

body:
Relation to temporal branch: TEMPORAL_BRANCH_PAUSE (PM-20260824-23cd74aa) recorded after E2_CALIBRATION_FAIL (PM-20260824-36f46bed) that no mechanism in the TEMPORAL_ANCHOR_AT_CONTEXT/EVENT_TIME_RESOLUTION family had cleared independent replication, and selected STATE/SUPERSESSION as the next mechanism family per the user's explicit direction. This event records the zero-cost design step for that candidate family, per an explicit authorization scoped to ZERO-COST MECHANISM B DESIGN + FAILURE-MODE DEFINITION + TRANSPLANT SPECIFICATION + EXPERIMENT PREREGISTRATION only -- NOT implementation, NOT an experiment.

Candidate family selected: STATE/SUPERSESSION, motivated by StateMemBench/StateMem (arXiv:2608.19652, StateMemWrapper's transplantable Trace->Resolve pattern, deep-verified in GLOBAL_AGENT_MEMORY_FRONTIER_MAP_2026-08-24.md), STALE (arXiv:2605.06527), StateAuditor (arXiv:2608.01619). External mechanism archaeology built a full field table for all four systems from already-recorded frontier docs only, honestly marking fields "not detailed further" where the frontier doc's own STALE/StateAuditor coverage was shallower than its StateMem/SMW coverage, rather than fabricating detail.

Why selected mechanism (CURRENT_STATE_OVER_HISTORY) rather than the whole StateMem system: explicit instruction was to find the smallest atomic transplantable unit, not adopt a host architecture. Isolated exactly one of SMW's four precedence rules ("later supersedes earlier"), rejecting the LLM-mediated Trace+Resolve call and StateMem's write-path (TurnEncoder, StateStore, dependency-graph Rechecker -- which its own paper reports over-propagating -12.5pp on one subset). Candidate board of 5 built (CURRENT_STATE_OVER_HISTORY, EXPLICIT_SUPERSESSION_LINK, DETERMINISTIC_LATEST_VALID_VALUE, STATE_TRANSITION_TRACE, POST_HOC_STATE_AUDIT), scored against the 8 required selection criteria. DETERMINISTIC_LATEST_VALID_VALUE explicitly flagged as a major design risk (destructive overwrite, violates the mandatory append-only principle) and not selected despite lowest implementation cost.

Why distinct from temporal branch: TEMPORAL_ANCHOR_AT_CONTEXT uniformly annotates every retrieved item with its date and does no grouping/filtering/precedence logic; CURRENT_STATE_OVER_HISTORY actively restructures which items render where based on a detected state-key match, and is inert (byte-identical to BASE) when no key matches. Per CROSS_PAPER_HYPOTHESIS_MAP_2026-08-24.md's own framing ("AAMR's C1 [temporal anchor] is a narrower, already-in-flight instance of this broader [state/supersession] family"), this document does NOT claim ORTHOGONAL to the temporal family -- it records PARTIALLY_OVERLAPPING, since both consume the same evidence_times metadata and both aim at delivering the right version/timing of a fact. vs RAW_PROVENANCE (E3/C4): ORTHOGONAL (different failure territory -- absence vs conflicting-presence). vs HARMFUL_SIBLING_DISTRACTION (Ledger Entry C, H5): PARTIALLY_OVERLAPPING -- same observable shape (reader picks a wrong item among several plausible candidates) but different underlying axis (entity-identity vs temporal-validity); V1's R4 adversarial control probes are specifically built to catch an over-loose key match misfiring in an H5-adjacent way.

Target failure: STALE_STATE_CONFUSION, broken into 6 submodes (A direct supersession, B negation/revocation, C return/reactivation, D multi-attribute state, E dependency cascade, F ambiguous update) per the required decomposition. V1 covers A/C directly with 3 dedicated probes each, B partially (3 dedicated probes, though negation-only facts without a replacement value are structurally harder for a pure recency rule), D only as an adversarial negative control (not its own regime), E and F explicitly deferred/out of scope -- consistent with the explicit instruction not to assume the first test must cover everything.

Negative regimes preregistered (all 7 required categories addressed): related-facts-mistaken-for-same-state and parallel-attributes-collapsed both targeted by 3 adversarial R4 control probes (two cats, two languages, home vs work address -- each deliberately sharing surface vocabulary while requiring separate state keys); historical-question-asks-old-value explicitly flagged as NOT measured by V1's 12 probes (an honest gap, not papered over -- no dedicated historical-question probe exists in this design); ambiguous-update-treated-as-supersession out of scope (mode F deferred); return-to-old-value-mishandled directly tested by the 3 R3 probes; context-clutter-from-state-trace tracked via a token_delta metric; over-propagation-of-invalidation has no dependency graph to over-propagate in V1, but the base current/history split's own mis-grouping risk is exactly what the R4 controls test.

Gold-blind state-key matching: selected Option A (deterministic normalized/pattern matching, 9 fixed keyword/regex templates covering exactly the 12 probes' attributes), explicitly rejecting Option B (construction-time metadata keys -- would answer the question only for hand-authored probes, not test the real mechanism), flagging Option C (LLM-assisted keying) as a cost/confound future extension, and Option D (hybrid) as the natural v2 once Option A's real-corpus miss rate is measured. The key-extraction function operates only on retrieved item text, never sees the question/expected-answer/judge output -- construction-time probe design and runtime key-matching are kept deliberately separate.

Experiment design (preregistered, NOT run): MECHANISM_B_STATE_SUPERSESSION_V1, 12 probes (3 CLEAN_SUPERSESSION + 3 REVOCATION + 3 RETURN + 3 NO_UPDATE_CONTROL, matching the suggested distribution exactly, frozen before any probe was checked against expected behavior), arms BASE vs +B (single shared Mem0 ingest per probe, same pattern as E1's +TIME arm -- the mechanism is purely a post-retrieval render transform). Full probe text/dates/expected-values in the JSON preregistration. Primary metrics: accuracy, repairs, regressions, net repairs, current-state accuracy, historical-question accuracy (no data available in V1 -- flagged gap), false supersession rate, state-key collision rate, token delta, latency delta. Mechanistic per-probe metrics as required. GO gate MECHANISM_B_EXPLORATORY_SUPPORTED requires positive net repairs across R1+R2+R3, zero false-supersession events across the 3 R4 controls, no systematic R4 harm, and a traceable causal path on every repair. FAIL gate covers no-signal, common false supersession, mechanism-caused regression, token-volume-only effect, or a gold-specific-oracle implementation. Replication gate: even a clean V1 pass caps at EXPLORATORY_SUPPORTED, never REPLICATED_VALIDATED_TRANSPLANT -- that needs a fresh, independently-constructed or gold-blind-selected set, with LongMemEval-S's real 'knowledge-update' category (78 units, 0 used in this arena to date, verified this pass) identified as the natural future real-corpus replication pool, mirroring the E1-to-Stage-2 pattern.

Cost estimate (not spent): ingest ~$0.15-0.20 (12 short synthetic probes, far smaller than a real 40+-session unit at the roadmap's own ~$0.074/unit figure), reader ~$0.014, judge ~$0.001, expected total ~$0.15-0.25, recommended hard cap $0.30 if a future turn separately authorizes the run.

Unresolved questions carried forward honestly: V1 has zero historical-question probes so the mechanism's stated risk of hiding needed history is asserted, not measured; the 9-template key strategy's real-corpus miss rate is unknown; the timestamp-tie fallback path is untested by any of the 12 constructed probes; whether Mem0's own near-duplicate suppression (roadmap F13) could merge two temporally-distinct same-key statements before this mechanism ever sees them is unverified and flagged as worth a cheap deterministic check before any paid run.

No implementation, no arena code change, no probe generation via a live pipeline, no ingest, no reader call, no judge call, no API call, no web search performed this turn. New API spend: $0.00.

title: MECHANISM_B_STATE_SUPERSESSION_DESIGN: CURRENT_STATE_OVER_HISTORY (zero-cost design)

body:
Per-probe archaeology (required 10-point decomposition, full table in stage1-archaeology.json): for all 9 R1/R2/R3 probes except SUP3, exactly 1 stored item survived Mem0's write path -- state_key detection was trivially N/A (nothing to match against), supersession was never detected because there was nothing to detect, and historical evidence was lost by Mem0's own write path before the mechanism's read-side logic ever ran. SUP3 (2 surviving items) showed correct state-key detection and a correct, safe tie-fallback (both items' metadata.timestamp read identically after Mem0's UPDATE path silently overwrote the older item's date) rather than guessing. All 3 R4 controls correctly kept their 2 distinct items separate in both runs (0/3 false supersession).

Classification: REGIME_FAILURE, not MECHANISM_FAILURE, not IMPLEMENTATION_FAILURE, not READER_FAILURE, not JUDGE_NOISE (0 disputed judge passes across both runs), not SELECTION_ARTIFACT in the pejorative sense (probe topics were fine; the flaw was structural -- turns packed in immediate adjacency with nothing else in the store).

Repair decision: REPAIR_AND_RETEST, justified as a single, deterministic, uniformly-applied harness-precondition fix (2 fixed filler turns per gap, template-verified to trigger none of the 9 state-key patterns, applied identically to all 9 affected probes, R4 left untouched) rather than per-probe wording tuning, gold-aware logic, or a host-specific hack. One retest only, $0.041754 spent of the $0.30 repair budget.

Repair retest outcome: the causal hypothesis (adjacency causes consolidation) was falsified. Stored item counts rose to 3-5 per probe, but this was entirely due to the filler turns themselves surviving -- the state-carrying facts still collapsed to exactly one item in every probe, because Mem0's own "existing memories" comparison inside its ADD/UPDATE decision is semantic/embedding-based, not proximity-based, so spacing related statements apart in the conversation does not stop Mem0 from finding and merging them. Verified precisely: current_history_split (the mechanism's one core action) fired zero times across all 24 probe-executions in both runs combined. One nominal answer flip (RET3_DIET, BASE wrong -> +B correct) was traced to the render transform's passthrough ordering moving the sole surviving relevant fact later in the context (after filler items) -- a token-order/salience side effect of the implementation, not the intended Current/History split logic -- and is explicitly NOT counted as a real repair, per the "never reinterpret a failed replication as success" discipline. A second data point, RET1_JOB (BASE wrong AND +B wrong), showed Mem0's own write-time consolidation kept the middle of three sequential facts ("...Globex") rather than the truly most recent one ("Rejoined Acme Corp") -- the host's own implicit consolidation is not even reliably recency-correct.

New infrastructure finding, not previously recorded anywhere in this project: Mem0 1.0.6's write-time UPDATE path can silently overwrite metadata.timestamp on an EXISTING memory to match a LATER, textually-unrelated add() call's date, even when that memory's own text is left completely unchanged. Directly observed on SUP3_RELATIONSHIP_STATUS: "Got engaged to my partner" kept its exact original wording, but its stored metadata.timestamp was rewritten from the original 2021-08-05 to 2023-02-14 (matching the later, unrelated "married" ingest call), confirmed via a zero-cost diagnostic read (memory.get_all() against the persisted on-disk Qdrant store -- a vector-store list operation, not an LLM call). This means evidence_times -- the sole recency signal both the already-paused TEMPORAL_ANCHOR_AT_CONTEXT (Ledger Entries A/B) and CURRENT_STATE_OVER_HISTORY depend on -- is not always a trustworthy record of a memory's true original observation time on this Mem0 version. Flagged for any future experiment that trusts this field.

Verdict: DROP (V1 harness, this host) -- MECHANISM_LOGIC_UNEXERCISED, NOT REFUTED. The mechanism's own design (state-key detection, tie-safe no-guess fallback, non-collapse of genuinely distinct entities) was verified correct in every single case across both runs where it had material to act on. It was simply never given that material: Mem0 1.0.6 itself absorbs sequential same-key state changes at write time, via its own internal ADD/UPDATE/DELETE reconciliation LLM call, before any read-side mechanism of this shape can ever see the "stale + current both present" precondition the mechanism was designed to resolve. Per the one-retest rule and the circuit breaker (no repeated failed paid actions on the same fingerprint -- same host, same consolidation behavior, would fail a third attempt the same way), no further repair is attempted.

Explicitly not concluded: "state/supersession mechanisms don't work" (mechanism untested, not refuted), "Mem0 already solves this so no mechanism is needed" (its own consolidation is demonstrably inconsistent and not even reliably recency-correct per RET1_JOB), or "CURRENT_STATE_OVER_HISTORY is a bad design" (never exercised). The honest status is that mechanism-level evidence is absent, not negative.

Total spend this mechanism: $0.064069 (original $0.022315 + repair $0.041754) of the $1.50 per-mechanism budget ceiling -- well under budget; the limiter was the one-retest/no-prompt-tuning-loop discipline, not cost.

Next: per the autonomous campaign contract (section 11), proceeding to select an independent second mechanism candidate (Stage 3), since Mechanism B is now closed (1 of the "3 consecutive failed families" circuit-breaker count, not yet triggering a campaign stop).

Verdict: DROP (V1 harness, this host) -- mechanism logic itself was never exercised (0 of 24 probe-executions across both runs ever fired the core current_history_split action), not refuted. Original run: BASE 12/12, +B 12/12, net repairs 0, $0.022315 spend. Zero-cost diagnostic (memory.get_all() reads, no LLM call) found Mem0 1.0.6's own write-time ADD/UPDATE reconciliation fully consolidated 8 of 9 R1/R2/R3 probes into a single surviving memory before the mechanism could see competing items. Repair hypothesis (turn-adjacency causes consolidation) tested via filler-spaced retest, $0.041754 -- hypothesis WRONG: state facts still fully consolidated regardless of spacing (Mem0's existing-memory match is semantic, not proximity-based). One nominal flip (RET3_DIET) traced to a context-reordering artifact, not the intended mechanism logic -- not counted as a real repair. New infrastructure finding: Mem0 1.0.6's UPDATE path can silently overwrite metadata.timestamp on an existing memory to match a later unrelated call's date even when that memory's text is untouched (SUP3 case), weakening evidence_times as a trustworthy signal for any mechanism depending on it (including the already-paused TEMPORAL_ANCHOR_AT_CONTEXT). Mechanism's own logic verified correct wherever it had material: 0/3 false supersession on R4 controls both runs, correct tie-safe no-guess fallback. title: MECHANISM_B_STAGE1: DROP (V1 harness) -- mechanism logic unexercised, not refuted

body:
Why this mechanism, why now: per the autonomous campaign contract section 11, after Mechanism B closed (DROP, V1 harness, PM-20260824-ba483b92), the next candidate should be independent and well-motivated. RAW_PROVENANCE (C4) already has design, calibration, and one exploratory result in this project (E3, CLEAN_RAW_PROVENANCE_RETEST_V2), scored CONDITIONAL (1/9 repair, 0 regressions) -- weak enough to warrant fresh replication before any stronger claim, exactly the kind of ambiguous signal this campaign's Stage 2-equivalent gate exists to resolve. This avoids re-inventing a mechanism from scratch and reuses already-audited, already-tested code (arena.mechanism_ablation.build_arms(), arena.retrieval_truth.session_map/raw_session -- deterministic, session-date-only, no gold-aware matching, code-audited earlier this project).

Mechanism definition (unchanged from E3): C4, read-side only. BASE = Mem0's own compact retrieved context (native). TREATMENT 1 (compact_plus_raw) = compact context + the raw source session text behind Mem0's top-1 retrieval hit, appended verbatim. TREATMENT 2 (raw_only) = the raw source session alone, no compact context -- a control isolating whether raw content alone (without Mem0's extraction) suffices.

Selection: 8 fresh units, gold-blind, category-stratified (2 knowledge-update, 2 multi-session, 1 temporal-reasoning, 1 single-session-user, 1 single-session-assistant, 1 single-session-preference), deterministic first-by-question_id-sort within category, excluding all 20 units used anywhere in this arena to date (the original 10 + Stage 2's fresh 10). Frozen in data/lab/arena/raw-provenance-fresh-replication-v1/selection.json before any ingest. Verified (not assumed): small haystack-session overlap (0-3 of 40-50 sessions per unit) with previously-used units exists for some selected units -- checked explicitly, judged non-disqualifying since it matches Stage 2's own established precedent (which excluded only exact question_id matches, not haystack-session-level overlap) and LongMemEval-S's corpus design intentionally reuses sessions across questions about the same simulated user profile; no unit swapped on this basis, no vector-store-level contamination is possible since each unit gets its own reset, isolated Mem0 bank.

Not biased toward knowledge-update exclusively despite E3's one success being knowledge-update: the mechanism's own target failure (compact-context absence or under-detail on a competing-facts case) is not category-specific by the mechanism's own definition per E3's own report, so a 2-unit quota (proportionate emphasis, not exclusivity) is used rather than an all-knowledge-update sample, which would be closer to gold-aware post-hoc curve-fitting than a legitimate prior.

Baseline discipline: same reader (fixed_reader.py's frozen READER_PROMPT/READER_PARAMS), same judge (judge_pilot.py's frozen per-category templates and 2-pass+3rd-on-disagreement protocol, matched to each unit's REAL question_type -- knowledge-update/temporal/generic/preference exactly as LongMemEval defines them, no new criterion), same contamination-audit discipline as Stage 2 (store_before_reset == store_after_reset == 0, foreign_from_other_units == 0 required before any arm is trusted).

Success gate: RAW_PROVENANCE_REPLICATED_SUPPORTED if >=1 net repair (compact wrong -> compact_plus_raw correct), 0 regressions (compact correct -> compact_plus_raw wrong), and the repair(s) show a traceable causal path in the raw session text (not a coincidental match). Failure gate: RAW_PROVENANCE_FAILED_REPLICATION if 0 net repairs, OR any regression, OR the effect is attributable only to added token volume rather than the raw content itself.

Cost estimate: ingest ~$0.57 (8 units x ~$0.0715/unit, per Stage 2's own measured per-unit ingest rate), reader+judge ~$0.02 (24 reader calls across 3 arms x 8 units, ~48-72 judge calls). Hard cap $0.75 (per-mechanism replication preference from the campaign contract section 16), well under the $1.50 per-mechanism absolute ceiling (Mechanism C's design+calibration were $0, reusing E3's prior work).

No experiment run yet at the time of this registration -- this is the preregistration, written before the first paid call, per the required discipline.

Same frozen reader/judge as every prior AAMR experiment. Projected cost ~$0.57 ingest + ~$0.02 reader/judge, hard cap $0.75 (per-mechanism replication budget preference).
title: RAW_PROVENANCE_FRESH_REPLICATION_V1 preregistration (Mechanism C)

body:
Full context: after Mechanism B (state/supersession, CURRENT_STATE_OVER_HISTORY) closed as DROP (harness precondition never met, PM-20260824-ba483b92), the autonomous campaign selected RAW_PROVENANCE (C4) as Mechanism C, reusing already-designed, already-calibrated, already-audited mechanism definition and code from E3 (docs/research/CLEAN_RAW_PROVENANCE_RETEST_V2.md, which itself replaced an earlier contaminated-data DROP conclusion). E3's own result was CONDITIONAL: 1/9 repair, 0 regressions -- too thin to trust without independent replication, exactly the kind of signal this campaign's fresh-replication gate exists to resolve.

Selection discipline: 8 fresh units, gold-blind, category-stratified (2 knowledge-update, 2 multi-session, 1 temporal-reasoning, 1 single-session-user, 1 single-session-assistant, 1 single-session-preference), deterministic first-by-question_id-sort within category after excluding all 20 units used anywhere in this arena to date (original 10 + Stage2's fresh 10). Frozen in data/lab/arena/raw-provenance-fresh-replication-v1/selection.json before any ingest call, registered as PM-20260824-0a6fc616. Verified, not assumed: small haystack-session overlap (0-3 of 40-50 sessions) with previously-used units for some selected units, checked explicitly and judged non-disqualifying (matches Stage2's own precedent, matches LongMemEval-S's own corpus-construction property of session reuse across questions about the same simulated user, and no vector-store-level contamination is possible since every unit gets its own reset isolated Mem0 bank).

Execution: clean ingest of all 384 haystack sessions across the 8 units (contamination_status PASS on all 8, reset postcondition held), retrieval via Mem0's own search, three arms built with the SAME already-audited deterministic logic as E3 (arena.mechanism_ablation.raw_session/gold_state, arena.retrieval_truth.session_map/canonical_time -- no gold-aware matching). Frozen reader (fixed_reader.py) and frozen judge (judge_pilot.py, matched to each unit's REAL LongMemEval question_type: knowledge-update/multi-session/temporal-reasoning/single-session-user/single-session-assistant/single-session-preference templates exactly as the benchmark defines them, no new criterion). Total spend $0.575419 of the preregistered $0.75 cap (ingest $0.558693 dominant, reader+judge $0.016726).

Results: compact 5/8, compact+raw 6/8, raw_only 4/8 -- a near-exact proportional replication of E3's own 5/9, 6/9, 4/9 shape. COMPACT_WRONG_RAW_FIXES = [0e5e2d1a], RAW_CAUSES_REGRESSION = [] (0/8). 0 disputed judge passes (fully stable, both passes agreed on every one of the 24 reader outputs across 8 units x 3 arms).

The one repair, examined not assumed: 0e5e2d1a (single-session-assistant), question about how many subjects were in a Music and Medicine journal study on binaural beats, gold "38 subjects". Compact answer: "I cannot determine the number of subjects... the context only notes you were seeking examples of studies... but does not include the details" -- WRONG, Mem0's compact extraction kept the topic but dropped the specific figure. Compact+raw answer: "...involved 38 subjects." -- CORRECT, gold_state confirms gold_in_context=True, gold_rank=1 in the raw-augmented arm. Raw-only also correct, confirming the number lives in the raw session text itself. This is a genuine ABSENCE-type repair, distinct from E3's own repair mechanism (which was competing-facts disambiguation between an already-present stale count and an already-present updated count, not absence) -- this broadens the mechanism's demonstrated repair territory to both failure sub-types E3's own report distinguished (absence vs under-detail/competing-facts), where E3 itself explicitly noted it had no absence-regime failure to test against.

Two non-repairs examined: 078150f1 (multi-session, charity cycling fundraising) -- both arms correctly report the amount raised but neither finds the initial goal; the raw session behind the TOP-1 hit specifically does not happen to be the session containing the goal figure, a genuine single-hop limitation (this mechanism only reaches one session, the top-1 hit's), not a malfunction. 0bc8ad93 (temporal-reasoning, museum visit) -- raw text made literally zero difference, both arms give byte-identical wrong answers, suggesting an entity/visit-matching confusion (a different museum visit than the one "two months ago") that raw content alone does not resolve -- structurally H5-adjacent (harmful-sibling/distraction axis), noted as a parallel but not conflated with Ledger Entry C.

One minor anomaly noted, not hidden: 2 of 384 ingest calls produced "Invalid JSON response" warnings during Mem0's own extraction step, absorbed by Mem0's existing error handling without stopping the run; all 8 units still show sane stored-item counts (171-256) and PASS contamination status -- not investigated further as it did not affect any arm's correctness.

Verdict: RAW_PROVENANCE_REPLICATED_SUPPORTED, meeting the preregistered gate exactly (>=1 net repair, 0 regressions, traceable causal path). Per the campaign's own status ladder (contract sections 17 and 20: external motivation + isolated transplant + exploratory positive + fresh gold-blind replication + confirmed mechanistic trace = promotion beyond EXPLORATORY_SUPPORTED), this is recorded as the project's FIRST REPLICATED_VALIDATED_TRANSPLANT. Explicitly calibrated, not overclaimed: the effect is real and independently replicated twice via two DIFFERENT repair mechanisms (competing-facts, absence) with zero regressions across 17 combined observable units total (9 + 8), but the magnitude is small (1 repair per ~8-9 unit sample each time) and the mechanism is single-hop-limited (078150f1 names the boundary directly).

Consequence for the campaign: this is the first of the 2 REPLICATED_VALIDATED_TRANSPLANT mechanisms needed before any BASE/+A/+B/+A+B interaction test is unlocked (contract section 21). A second independently-validated mechanism is still needed. Ledger Entry H records this; a multi-hop provenance extension (addressing the 078150f1-class single-hop limitation) is named as a natural but untested, unscheduled next step for this specific mechanism, separate from finding a second, independent mechanism family.

summary: RAW_PROVENANCE_FRESH_REPLICATION_V1 result (Mechanism C): RAW_PROVENANCE_REPLICATED_SUPPORTED -> promoted to REPLICATED_VALIDATED_TRANSPLANT, the campaign's first validated mechanism. 8 fresh, gold-blind, never-used units. compact 5/8, compact+raw 6/8, raw_only 4/8 -- 1 repair (0e5e2d1a, genuine absence-type: compact dropped a specific number "38 subjects" that the raw source session states directly, gold_in_context=True gold_rank=1 confirmed), 0 regressions, 0 disputed judge passes. Closely replicates E3's original shape (5/9, 6/9, 4/9, also 1 repair 0 regressions there, via a different mechanism -- competing-facts disambiguation rather than absence). Spend $0.575419 of $0.75 cap (384 ingest sessions across 8 units + 24 reader + ~48 judge calls). title: RAW_PROVENANCE fresh replication: REPLICATED_VALIDATED_TRANSPLANT (first in project)

body:
Candidate ranking (self-directed, no user consultation, per the autonomous research contract): three shortlisted at $0 using already-recorded frontier docs and this project's own ledger/roadmap, no new web/GitHub search performed (existing knowledge sufficient).

1. HARMFUL_SIBLING/DISTRACTOR flagging -- target: entity-identity confusion (Ledger Entry C, H5, one real AAMR case: E1's Spirit/Delta). High external evidence (arXiv:2606.10388, harmful-sibling-rate ~1/3 of correct-looking retrievals). Scored down on transplantability/clear-falsifiability: the actual observed AAMR case (Spirit vs Delta) requires a multi-hop inference distinction (a directly-named wrong entity vs a correct entity requiring linking an unnamed item to a separate mention) that a simple deterministic entity-clash detector cannot reliably characterize without drifting toward gold-aware or question-aware logic. Design attempted, not adopted for V1 -- kept as a documented future candidate.

2. RETRIEVAL_SUFFICIENCY / explicit abstention strengthening -- target: reader answers confidently despite insufficient evidence ("Sufficient Context" paper, PAPER_CLAIM per the frontier map). Scored down: modifying reader behavior this directly borders on changing the frozen READER_PROMPT, a hard invariant across every AAMR experiment to date; a context-embedded version is possible but converges heavily with option 3 below without option 3's clean, already-available deterministic signal.

3. RETRIEVAL_CONFIDENCE_SIGNAL (selected) -- target: reader over-trusts the single most-prominent retrieved item when retrieval itself was ambiguous (near-tied top candidates), a distinct axis from both RAW_PROVENANCE (content absence) and the dropped state/supersession mechanism (temporal validity). Uses Mem0's own retrieval scores, already returned by Memory.search() (confirmed zero-cost to inspect: search performs no LLM call). Externally motivated by the "confident-but-wrong"/retrieval-utilization-gap family (frontier map top-10 family #5, "When Confidence Takes the Wrong Path" 2606.22728: 42-59% of RAG errors show zero answer dispersion). This project's OWN prior roadmap work (RESEARCH_ROADMAP_EVIDENCE_DRIVEN_V1.md, controller-gate discussion) explicitly flagged "the retrieval-confidence/score-margin gap... still unprecedented anywhere, still worth a free check on our own data first" -- directly anticipating this exact mechanism. Scored highest on EXPECTED_INFORMATION_GAIN x COST x ORTHOGONALITY x TRANSPLANTABILITY x EXTERNAL_EVIDENCE x CLEAR_FAILURE_MODE among the three.

Zero-cost calibration performed before probe selection: inspected real retrieval scores from the 8 already-ingested, already-persisted RAW_PROVENANCE fresh-replication units via a fresh Memory.search() call against the existing on-disk store (no LLM call, confirmed free). Observed top1-top2 margin range ~0.025-0.34 across those 8 units -- a meaningful, non-degenerate spread. Chose MARGIN_THRESHOLD=0.10 (scripts/arena/retrieval_confidence_signal.py) as a round, defensible cutpoint from that observed range, BEFORE selecting this mechanism's own fresh probe set, to avoid any circularity between threshold-setting and probe-outcome. The 8 units used for this calibration are explicitly excluded from this experiment's own probe set (already deeply read/analyzed for RAW_PROVENANCE, would violate blindness if reused).

Mechanism definition: read-side, post-retrieval, pre-render, fully deterministic, zero LLM calls in the mechanism itself. BASE = Mem0's native compact retrieved context, unmodified. +D = same context, with one fixed, content-free note appended IF AND ONLY IF the top-1 vs top-2 retrieval score margin is below 0.10; otherwise byte-identical to BASE (inert by construction, verified by 8/8 passing unit tests in tests/test_retrieval_confidence_signal.py, no LLM call). The note text never references any retrieved content, question, or gold -- purely a generic instruction to check less-prominent candidates.

Selection: 5 fresh units, gold-blind, category-stratified (2 multi-session, 1 temporal-reasoning, 1 knowledge-update, 1 single-session-user), deterministic first-by-question_id-sort within category, excluding all 28 units used anywhere in this arena to date (original 10 + Stage2's 10 + RAW_PROVENANCE's 8). Frozen in data/lab/arena/retrieval-confidence-signal-v1/selection.json before any ingest. Sized smaller than RAW_PROVENANCE's fresh-replication (8 units) because this is the EXPLORATORY stage for a brand-new mechanism (contract preference <$0.30 for exploratory), not yet a replication stage -- projected ingest cost ~$0.32 (222 sessions across 5 units).

Success gate: MECHANISM_D_EXPLORATORY_SUPPORTED if >=1 net repair (BASE wrong -> +D correct), 0 regressions (BASE correct -> +D wrong), and the repair(s) show the reader explicitly using or referencing a less-prominent candidate after the note (a traceable causal path, not coincidental). Failure gate: MECHANISM_D_FAIL if 0 net repairs, OR any regression, OR the note's mere presence/token-volume explains any change without a traceable use of a less-prominent item.

Same frozen reader (fixed_reader.py) and frozen judge (judge_pilot.py, matched to each unit's real LongMemEval question_type) as every AAMR experiment to date. No new criterion invented.

Cost estimate: ingest ~$0.32 (222 sessions), reader+judge ~$0.01 (10 reader calls, ~20-30 judge calls). Hard cap for this exploratory stage: $0.35. Per-mechanism absolute ceiling $1.50 remains far off (design+calibration $0 marginal, this exploratory stage ~$0.32).

No experiment run yet at the time of this registration.

body:
Candidate selection rationale (self-directed): of the remaining candidate families, HARMFUL_SIBLING/DISTRACTOR handling was chosen because it is the most concretely evidenced within AAMR itself (one confirmed TRACEABLE_DISTRACTOR case, Ledger Entry C) as opposed to purely externally-motivated candidates. Rejected on a prior pass (Mechanism D selection turn) for a generic, gold-adjacent design; revisited here with a narrower, template-based, non-gold-aware design mirroring Mechanism B's successful state-key template approach, judged tractable on reflection.

Mechanism definition: read-side, post-retrieval, pre-render, fully deterministic, zero LLM calls. BASE = Mem0's native compact retrieved context, unmodified. +E = same context with one explicit enumeration note appended per category where 2+ distinct entity names sharing a category suffix (from a fixed 22-category list: Airlines, Airways, Museum, Hotel, Restaurant, University, College, Hospital, Church, Bank, Corp, Inc, Company, Store, Cafe, Gym, Club, Park, Theater, Theatre, Library, School, Academy) are found among the retrieved items. The note lists the distinct entities found under that category; it never indicates which is correct -- purely surfaces plurality already present in the delivered context, exactly like Mechanism B's provenance-preserving current/history split never deleted anything.

Bug found and fixed before any paid call: the entity-extraction regex initially over-captured sentence-initial capitalized words (e.g. "Flew Delta Airlines" -> captured "Flew Delta Airlines" as the entity name instead of "Delta Airlines"). Caught by this mechanism's own unit tests (tests/test_sibling_entity_enumeration.py), not by luck -- 2 of 8 tests failed on first run. Fixed with a small, fixed stoplist of common leading verbs/articles stripped from the left edge of any match (scripts/arena/sibling_entity_enumeration.py). Reverified: all 8 unit tests pass, AND the fix was checked against the real historical case that motivates this mechanism (E1's gpt4_f420262c, mem0_3000 arm, 208 retrieved items) -- the mechanism correctly and cleanly identifies American Airlines / Spirit Airlines / United Airlines as three distinct entities sharing the Airlines category, confirming it would have fired on the actual case that inspired it. This check used only already-existing, already-paid-for retrieval data (mem0-breadth-arms.json), zero new API spend.

Selection: 8 fresh units, gold-blind, category-stratified (3 multi-session, 2 temporal-reasoning, 1 single-session-user, 1 single-session-assistant, 1 knowledge-update), deterministic first-by-question_id-sort within category, excluding all 33 units used anywhere in this arena to date (original 10 + Stage2's 10 + RAW_PROVENANCE's 8 + Mechanism D's 5, including the dropped/incomplete unit). Frozen in data/lab/arena/sibling-entity-enumeration-v1/selection.json before any ingest. Weighted toward multi-session/temporal-reasoning categories (richer conversation histories, more opportunities for repeated entity mentions across many sessions) as a category-structure-based prior, not content-based -- matching this campaign's established selection discipline. Sized at 8 units (not a smaller 5) specifically to reduce the regime-mismatch risk that closed Mechanism D -- a mechanism whose precondition (2+ same-category entities actually co-occurring) might be rare needs a reasonably-sized sample to have a fair chance of firing at all.

Success gate: MECHANISM_E_EXPLORATORY_SUPPORTED if >=1 net repair (BASE wrong -> +E correct) on a unit where the note fired, 0 regressions, and the repair shows the reader's answer changing away from the sibling entity toward the correct one after the note (a traceable causal path). Failure gate: MECHANISM_E_FAIL if 0 net repairs, OR any regression, OR the mechanism never fires on any of the 8 units (a pure regime-mismatch outcome, distinct from a fired-but-ineffective outcome -- both classified honestly if they occur).

Same frozen reader (fixed_reader.py) and frozen judge (judge_pilot.py, matched to each unit's real LongMemEval question_type) as every AAMR experiment to date. No new criterion invented.

Cost estimate: ingest ~$0.54 (373 sessions across 8 units), reader+judge ~$0.02. Hard cap for this stage: $0.60. Per-mechanism absolute ceiling $1.50 remains comfortably distant.

No experiment run yet at the time of this registration.

body: This is recorded as a durable, general lesson for this project: sub-agents doing 'CODE_VERIFIED' claims about this project's own vendored/pinned dependencies must be explicitly pointed at the actual installed path (external/venvs/<name>/Lib/site-packages) and warned that any external/repos/* clone of an upstream project is a DIFFERENT, likely newer, unpinned codebase -- never assume they are the same without checking pip show / a version string. This exact confusion, if acted upon without verification, would have wasted the discovery phase's entire strategic value by re-opening an already-correctly-closed mechanism on a false premise. Also confirms the source-of-truth hierarchy already established in the AAMR contract (VALID AAMR experiment > external research claim) worked exactly as designed: my own prior empirical Mechanism B result outranked a fresh, confidently-labeled external code-reading claim, and re-verification (not blind trust) resolved the conflict in favor of the empirical result.\n\nSecondary finding: independently ran my own zero-cost precondition check (querying the already-persisted RAW_PROVENANCE stores, free Mem0 search() calls, no LLM) on the next viable candidate, SECOND_HOP_ASSOCIATIVE_EXPANSION -- confirmed LongMemEval-S's own multi-session structural distribution directly from the local corpus (250/500 questions need exactly 2 gold sessions, the single largest bucket; 324/500 need 2+), matching the discovery agent's primary-source claim. Also found compact top-10 retrieval already naturally spans 2-7 distinct sessions per unit even without any second-hop mechanism, and a second-hop query (seeded from the top-1 hit's own text) surfaces a genuinely new item beyond the top-10 in 2 of 8 already-ingested units (25%) -- a real, moderate, verified precondition rate, not the near-zero rate that sank Mechanisms D and E.
summary: Campaign V2 external-discovery workflow (12 agents, wf_d25fd577-a75, $0 AAMR spend) produced 28 ranked candidates. Top-ranked candidate (STATE_SUPERSESSION_BREADTH_REDIAGNOSIS) claimed CODE_VERIFIED proof that Mem0's write path is purely additive (no UPDATE/DELETE), which would have reopened Mechanism B's DROP verdict. FALSE for this project's actual harness -- the discovery agent had read external/repos/mem0ai__mem0 (upstream GitHub, v2.0.18) and mistook it for this project's actually-vendored, actually-pinned external/venvs/mem0 (mem0ai==1.0.6, confirmed via pip show). Caught independently twice: by me directly (pip show + grep confirming live UPDATE/DELETE code paths, matching Mechanism B's own empirical memory.get_all() observations) and by the workflow's own archaeology agent. Mechanism B's DROP stands, reinforced not reopened. Candidates #2 (SERIAL_POSITION_CONTEXT_REORDER, lost-in-the-middle reorder) and #3 (RETRIEVAL_BREADTH_AND_THRESHOLD_EXPANSION) were also disqualified by archaeology using real accumulated AAMR data: gold_rank=1 in 17/17 observed retrievals ever run (never buried mid-list), and breadth-widening to the literal whole-store ceiling was already tested months ago with a flat/regressive result. summary:
MECHANISM_H_PREREGISTRATION -- HYDE_QUERY_REFORMULATION. Campaign V2's second candidate, selected after Mechanism G's DROP (SECOND_HOP_ASSOCIATIVE_EXPANSION). Selection process: rather than pick the next-ranked pool entry blindly, ran a fresh $0 diagnostic across all 11 BASE-wrong units observed project-wide to date (across raw-provenance-fresh-replication-v1, retrieval-confidence-signal-v1, retrieval-rank-annotation-v1, second-hop-expansion-v1, sibling-entity-enumeration-v1) and classified each as retrieval-absence vs evidence-present-but-misread. Result: 9/11 (82%) were absence failures -- meaning the entire verification/repair-against-same-context tier (CHAIN_OF_VERIFICATION_FACTORED, PARAPHRASE_SELF_CONSISTENCY, VERBALIZED_CONFIDENCE_GATED_REPAIR, TARGETED_EVIDENCE_REPAIR, EVIDENCE_TAGGED_CITATION -- ranks 4/14/15/17/21 in the discovery pool) has almost no precondition to fire against in this project's actual failure distribution, since all of them require evidence to already be present in the retrieved context to check against. Deprioritized that whole tier on this basis (documented in HYDE_QUERY_REFORMULATION_V1.md), a different reason than the earlier CONTEXT_WRITE_TIME_ONLY_LEVERAGE deprioritization of the conflict/supersession family.

Follow-up $0 check (memory.get_all(), zero LLM calls) on 2 of the 9 absence units (mechd-0a995998, meche-10d9b85a, both already-persisted stores from Mechanisms D and E) found the missing fact WAS present in the full store (not a write-time Mem0 extraction loss) but outside the top-10 the reader saw. A further $0 check using a hand-written HyDE-style hypothetical query (not the literal question) against the same free Mem0 search() moved the missing fact from entirely absent in the literal-question top-10 to RANK 1 in the hypothetical-query top-10, in BOTH cases tested (2/2) -- a strong, confirmed, large-effect precondition, stronger than any prior mechanism's $0 check in this campaign. Independent external support: LongMemEval's own primary-source construction methodology (arXiv:2410.10813, appendix A.1) states evidence sessions are built so the evidence is conveyed indirectly rather than in the question's own words -- by-construction phrasing mismatch, not a rare edge case.

MECHANISM: read/query-side only, one extra small temp=0 LLM call per unit (HYDE_PROMPT, max_tokens=60) generates a short hypothetical memory-note sentence; Mem0 search() is called with that hypothetical text in place of the literal question (pure/faithful HyDE variant, matching Gao et al. ACL 2023 -- no blend with the literal query, to keep this exploratory test a clean one-variable replication). Orthogonal to RAW_PROVENANCE (upstream of retrieval vs. post-hoc raw-text injection) and to Mechanism G (query reformulation vs. second-hop expansion). Does not touch the visible answer's phrasing or add any caveat/annotation, so it does not carry the "judge-penalized epistemic caution" risk that sank 3 earlier mechanisms.

UNIT SELECTION: data/lab/arena/hyde-query-reformulation-v1/selection.json, 6 fresh gold-blind units (1 per LongMemEval-S category), frozen before any ingest, excluding all 55 previously used/examined units project-wide.

SUCCESS GATE: MECHANISM_H_EXPLORATORY_SUPPORTED if >=1 net repair (BASE wrong -> +H correct) on a unit where the hypothetical-query top10 differs from the literal-query top10 and contains the previously-missing evidence, 0 regressions, traceable causal path.
FAILURE GATE: MECHANISM_H_FAIL if 0 net repairs OR any regression traceable to hallucination-guided retrieval drift (the hypothetical confidently invented a wrong-but-plausible detail that steered retrieval away from the correct memory -- the specific negative regime flagged in this candidate's own archaeology) OR net effect not clearly positive.

Budget: cap $0.50 (per-mechanism-before-replication preference), Campaign V2 running total before this stage $0.414206 of $5.00.
