BACKGROUND: TEMPORAL_ANCHOR_AT_CONTEXT (render each retrieved fact as "[YYYY-MM-DD] fact" using its session timestamp, read-side, zero LLM) showed a real positive effect in E1 (exploratory, Ledger Entry A) and was given a fresh 10-unit gold-blind replication in Stage 2 (70/30 temporal/control mix). Stage 2's OVERALL, pre-registered-bucket verdict was TEMPORAL_ANCHOR_FAILED_REPLICATION (net -1: 3 regressions vs 2 repairs, 0 repairs in the predicted TEMPORAL_POSITIVE bucket) -- this mechanism is NOT dropped, its ledger status is SUPPORTED/qualified, narrowed. Each retrieved compact fact rendered as "[YYYY-MM-DD] {fact}" using its own positionally-aligned session timestamp (scripts/arena/temporal_anchor_at_context.py, reusing canonical_time()). FAILURE GATE: MECHANISM_I_FAIL if regressions >= repairs, OR any regression traces to the same diverging-session-anchor trap this classifier was designed to avoid (which would mean the classifier itself failed to exclude it) OR the net effect is not clearly positive.

summary:
FINDING (not yet actioned as a mechanism -- recorded for future work): scripts/arena/run_arena_pilot.py's as_records() -- the shared ingest function every mechanism run script in this project uses to build the BASE Mem0 store -- deliberately drops ALL assistant-role turns before Mem0 ever sees them ("Assistant turns are dropped here rather than downstream, because CUPMem's chunker drops them silently and an adapter that hands over turns it knows will vanish is reporting an ingest it did not make" -- a deliberate fair-comparison-with-CUPMem design choice, not a bug).

Consequence, confirmed by direct corpus inspection: LongMemEval-S's single-session-assistant question category (56/500 = 11.2% of the full benchmark) asks the user to recall something the ASSISTANT said in a prior session. Checked 16c90bf4 directly against the raw corpus: the gold answer ("Pilsner or Lager") appears ONLY in the assistant's own turn ("it's recommended to use a light or medium-bodied beer... a pilsner or lager wo[uld be good]"); the user's own turn only echoes a PARTIAL, incomplete version ("I'll definitely try this recipe with a Pilsner"), framed as a future plan, not a recollection. Since as_records() drops the assistant turn before ingest, Mem0 (and any RAW_PROVENANCE-style raw-injection mechanism, which also depends on as_records' output) structurally cannot recover the complete original content for this category -- at best a partial, incidentally-user-echoed fragment survives.

Every single-session-assistant unit observed project-wide to date (4/4: 16c90bf4 Mechanism F, 18dcd5a5 Mechanism G, 1568498a Mechanism E, 1903aded Mechanism H) has been BASE=WRONG, consistent with this being a single common root cause rather than 4 independent failures. This is a different, more fundamental failure mode than any of the 3 absence subtypes named so far (write-time-extraction-loss, retrieval-ranking-miss, temporal-representation-loss) -- call it subtype (4), assistant-turn-scoping-loss: content is dropped BEFORE the extraction call even runs, not compressed or mis-extracted by it.

Any future mechanism addressing this would need a SEPARATE ingest path for its own treatment arm (not a modification to the shared as_records() function itself, which every other mechanism's BASE comparison in this entire project depends on staying constant) -- e.g. a parallel record set that includes assistant turns, ingested into a second Mem0 bank, used only by that mechanism's +ARM, leaving BASE and every other mechanism's comparison untouched. Not designed or tested this turn -- flagged as a well-evidenced candidate for a future mechanism (tentatively ASSISTANT_TURN_INCLUSION_AT_INGEST or similar), pending careful design of how to keep it isolated from the shared BASE construction.
title: New absence subtype (4): assistant-turn-scoping-loss -- as_records() drops assistant turns, capping single-session-assistant category (11.2% of benchmark)

summary:
MECHANISM_J_CALIBRATION_PREREGISTRATION -- EXTRACTION_COMPLETENESS_VERIFICATION_PASS. Selected as the top candidate (STRONG_CANDIDATE archaeology verdict, composite score 567, rank 3 in the deduped pool but highest-confidence verdict of the discovery-rebuild's top 3) from the fresh external-discovery-rebuild workflow (docs/research/EXTERNAL_DISCOVERY_CANDIDATE_POOL_V3.md), triggered by Campaign V2's 3-consecutive-failure strategy pivot (Mechanisms G, H, I). This is the first mechanism this campaign to target write-time extraction loss directly (subtype 1 of this campaign's own absence taxonomy) -- every mechanism tested so far (D through I) operated read-side/query-side on content Mem0's write-time extraction already chose to keep.

MECHANISM: after Mem0's normal write-time extraction call returns its facts list, one additional LLM call re-reads the original session text against those already-extracted facts and proposes any standalone facts omitted -- especially individual items within an enumerated list, which the shipped extraction prompt's own few-shot example currently teaches the model to merge (two favorite movies -> one fact string, CODE_VERIFIED against external/venvs/mem0/Lib/site-packages). External evidence: ProMem, measured directly on LongMemEval with an ablation isolating this exact stage (removing it drops HaluMem integrity 73.80%->60.33%).

IMPLEMENTATION (already applied, gated off by default): a vendor patch to external/venvs/mem0/Lib/site-packages/mem0/memory/{utils.py,main.py} (data/lab/arena/extraction-completeness-verification-v1/vendor-patch/, manifest.json, matching the project's established PER_SESSION_REFERENCE_DATE_AT_EXTRACTION / EVENT_TIME_RESOLUTION_AT_EXTRACTION precedent). utils.py gets one new, purely additive function get_completeness_check_messages(). main.py's SYNC _add_to_vector_store() (only -- this project's Mem0Adapter is synchronous, the async twin is untouched) gets one new gated block: if metadata["completeness_check_enabled"] is truthy, issue the extra call and merge any genuinely new missed_facts (case-insensitive substring dedup) into new_retrieved_facts before Mem0's own ADD/UPDATE/DELETE reconciliation runs -- composing with it rather than intervening inside it (the reason CURRENT_STATE_OVER_HISTORY was dropped does not apply here). Gate defaults falsy, so every existing call site, including this project's own shared BASE Mem0 construction used by every other mechanism in this campaign, remains byte-identical to unpatched behavior. Both file hashes recorded before/after in the manifest.

WHY CALIBRATE FIRST (mandatory per this project's own established discipline): this is the largest code-surface change of any mechanism tested this campaign (a real vendor patch to Mem0's own write-time pipeline, not a read-side render transform), and this project's own precedent (EVENT_TIME_RESOLUTION_AT_EXTRACTION, Ledger Entry E) found a different write-side instruction inert (0/5 cases changed extraction behavior) on this exact model (deepseek-chat) -- a concrete, specific reason for caution before committing to a paid 8-unit exploratory run. Mirrors the E2 calibration-only methodology exactly (scripts/arena/calibrate_extraction_completeness.py, modeled on calibrate_event_time_resolution.py): calls the real extraction path directly for an honest baseline (not a hand-faked "already extracted" set), then the completeness-check call against that same real output. No memory.add() pipeline, no vector-store write. 5 synthetic cases (4 with a clear enumerable list of varying shape: inline-and-list, numbered list, named entities, list-amid-other-content; 1 negative control with no list, checking for over-triggering/hallucination), 2 calls each = 10 calls total.

GATE: proceed to a full preregistered 8-unit exploratory test ONLY if calibration shows the completeness-check call recovers genuinely new, correct items (not hallucinated, not already present) on at least 2 of the 4 list-bearing cases, AND the negative control returns an empty or genuinely-non-overlapping missed_facts list (no fabrication). If calibration shows the mechanism is inert (0/5 changed) or fabricates facts not present in the source text, this is MECHANISM_J_CALIBRATION_FAILED and the vendor patch is NOT eligible for a paid exploratory run without a redesign, mirroring Entry E's own precedent and gate language exactly.

Budget: cap $0.05 for calibration (hard, enforced by SpendLedger, cap_scope="mechj-calib-"). Campaign V2 running total before this stage $1.410904 of $5.00.

summary:
MECHANISM_J_CALIBRATION_RESULT -- EXTRACTION_COMPLETENESS_VERIFICATION_PASS. First calibration run (cap_scope mechj-calib-, prompt asking only about "omitted" facts) was inert on all 4 list-bearing synthetic cases: an already-merged fact (e.g. "Favorite movies are Inception, Interstellar, and Tenet") technically contains every item's name, so nothing reads as "missing" under that wording even though 3 distinct items were bundled into 1 fact. Caught this as a real prompt-design gap BEFORE any paid exploratory spend (the intended purpose of calibration), not a retry of a failed paid mechanism. Revised get_completeness_check_messages() (external/venvs/mem0/Lib/site-packages/mem0/memory/utils.py) to explicitly ask for two distinct correction kinds -- MISSING (facts_to_add) and BUNDLED (facts_to_replace: original fact + split_into items) -- and updated main.py's merge logic to apply replacements before additions.

Second calibration run (cap_scope mechj-calib2-) showed the revised prompt DOES correctly split bundled facts, but my own calibration SCRIPT still parsed the old "missed_facts" key (a bug in the test harness, not the mechanism) and printed empty results. Fixed the script's parsing to match the new facts_to_add/facts_to_replace schema and reran (cap_scope mechj-calib3-).

FINAL RESULT: 4/4 list-bearing calibration cases (inline "and" list, numbered list, named entities, list-amid-other-content) correctly split into individual facts by the completeness-check pass -- e.g. "Favorite movies are Inception, Interstellar, and Tenet" -> 3 separate facts. The negative control (no enumerable list) returned empty facts_to_add/facts_to_replace, confirming no fabrication/over-triggering. This clears the preregistered gate (PM-20260824-f8d5e89c: >=2/4 list cases recovered AND clean negative control) with margin (4/4, not just 2/4). MECHANISM_J_CALIBRATION_PASSED. Proceeding to the full preregistered 8-unit gold-blind exploratory test.

Total calibration spend across all 3 runs: ~$0.006 (well under the $0.05 cap per run). Vendor patch manifest (data/lab/arena/extraction-completeness-verification-v1/vendor-patch/manifest.json) updated with final file hashes and the calibration-driven revision documented inline.

summary:

Responds to ResearchOS candidate rmc-2026-08-24-001 (Dokumenty z Resherchera/candidates/2026-08-24_mechanism_candidate_semantic-entropy-escalation-gate.md) and AAMR's own outstanding research request arr-2026-08-24-001 (compact-vs-raw sufficiency gate, GAP-005). Per the standing "prefer calibration before full test" discipline and explicit instruction not to jump to M=20 samples when M=3-5 gives calibration information: this is a CALIBRATION, not a causal mechanism test. Zero new gold-blind selection, zero new ingest -- reuses the already-persisted, already-labeled RAW_PROVENANCE fresh-replication-v1 store (data/lab/arena/raw/raw-provenance-fresh-v1-store, banks rawprov-{qid}) and its already-known ground truth (5 units where compact was sufficient/BASE correct, 3 where compact was insufficient/BASE wrong) from data/lab/arena/raw-provenance-fresh-replication-v1/results.json. For each of the 8 units: re-query the persisted store (free, no LLM cost) to reconstruct the frozen compact context, sample the frozen reader M=4 times at temperature=0.7 on (question, compact context) -- these M reader calls are the only paid cost -- embed each generation with the same local MiniLM checkpoint Mem0 itself uses (external/models/all-MiniLM-L6-v2, sentence_transformers.SentenceTransformer, CPU), greedy-cluster by cosine similarity (threshold 0.85), compute semantic entropy H = -sum(p_i * log2(p_i)) over cluster-size proportions. No judge calls -- this measures entropy, not accuracy, and per the standing discipline "nie uzywaj calibration jako evidence skutecznosci," this result will NOT be reported as proof the mechanism works, only as a precondition/signal-quality check informing whether a full causal test is worth designing.

QUESTION: does mean semantic entropy differ meaningfully between the 5 known-compact-sufficient units and the 3 known-compact-insufficient units, in the theoretically expected direction (higher entropy = more sample-to-sample disagreement = compact context insufficient)?

Budget: 32 reader calls (4 samples x 8 units), projected ~$0.02-0.04 based on this project's own established per-call reader cost. Hard cap $0.08 for this calibration.

GATE: if entropy shows a real, interpretable separation between the two known groups, this justifies designing a genuine, fresh gold-blind causal test of the gate (a new, separate paid experiment, its own preregistration). If entropy shows no separation, or an inverted/uninterpretable pattern, this closes the semantic-entropy-escalation-gate candidate as PRECONDITION_ABSENT / weak-signal, and the finding gets written back into DO_NOT_REDISCOVER and reported to ResearchOS via the existing research request's own review file, without spending on a full test.

summary:

MECHANISM: for each unit, retrieve standard compact top-10 context (adapter.query()). Sample the frozen reader M=4 times at temperature=0.7 on (question, compact context) -- reusing the calibration's own embed+cluster+entropy code (scripts/arena/calibrate_semantic_entropy_gate.py's greedy_cluster/semantic_entropy functions, imported not reimplemented). If semantic entropy > 0.5 bits (a round threshold between the calibration's own observed sufficient-cluster mass at 0.000 and insufficient-cluster floor at 0.811 -- NOT re-tuned to perfectly separate the 8 calibration units, to avoid overfitting a threshold to n=8): escalate by appending RAW_PROVENANCE's raw session behind the top-1 hit (scripts/arena/mechanism_ablation.raw_session(), the same, already-frozen, already-validated code Entry H itself uses) to the compact context. Else: use compact-only. Generate ONE final answer at temperature=0 (matching every other mechanism's final-answer protocol) on the gate-selected context.

ARMS: BASE (compact-only, unconditional, temp=0 -- identical construction to every prior mechanism's BASE) vs GATE (entropy-conditional compact-or-compact+raw, temp=0 final answer).

UNIT SELECTION: data/lab/arena/semantic-entropy-gate-v1/selection.json, 6 fresh gold-blind units (1/category), excluding all 85 previously used/examined units project-wide (including the calibration's own 8, already excluded via raw-provenance-fresh-replication-v1's own selection).

PRIMARY METRIC: (a) correctness -- net repairs vs regressions, GATE vs BASE; (b) cost-efficiency -- token cost of GATE's realized context vs. what unconditional RAW_PROVENANCE would have cost on the same units (computable without a new arm, since compact-only token counts are already recorded and RAW_PROVENANCE's own ~21.4x multiplier is already measured).

SUCCESS GATE: MECHANISM_SEG_EXPLORATORY_SUPPORTED if GATE matches or exceeds BASE's accuracy (0 regressions, or explained/outweighed) AND the gate fires selectively (not on 100% of units, which would be functionally identical to unconditional RAW_PROVENANCE and defeat the cost-efficiency purpose) AND at least 1 escalated unit shows a traceable repair (gate correctly identified an insufficient case and fixed it via raw injection, matching RAW_PROVENANCE's own known repair mechanism).
FAILURE GATE: MECHANISM_SEG_FAIL if any regression not clearly explained, OR the gate fires on 0% or 100% of units (uninformative / functionally unconditional), OR entropy shows no correlation with actual correctness on this fresh sample (the calibration's separation does not transfer).

Budget: cap $0.60 (single-bank ingest ~6x$0.07-0.09=$0.42-0.54 dominates; entropy sampling ~$0.02; final answers + judge negligible, per the calibration's own $0.003/32-calls rate).
